   369	### Running Tests
   370	
   371	```bash
   372	# TypeScript / JavaScript
   373	pnpm test                                    # All JS/TS tests
   374	pnpm vitest --run                            # All tests (non-watch)
   375	pnpm vitest --run path/to/test.spec.ts       # Specific file
   376	
   377	# Rust — CANONICAL agent gate
   378	node scripts/gate.mjs                         # THE Rust gate (SINGLE-TEST-UNIVERSE: ONE full workspace build, ONE full nextest run — see docs/arch/refactor/rev11/rulings/MAINTAINER-DIRECTIVE-SINGLE-TEST-UNIVERSE.md). Builds and lists the test universe ONCE via `cargo nextest archive --workspace` (dev profile). After those shared preconditions, archive-backed SURFACE 1 (`cargo nextest run`, per-test process isolation) is the verdict. The shipped-cfg lane is currently SKIPPED (temporary; `SHIPPED_CFG_LANE_ENABLED` in `scripts/gate-internals.mjs`) — a PASS is Surface 1 only, disclosed on every run. Deliberate shared-process coverage (leaked statics, TLS surviving a test, a global cache mutated by one test changing another's result) lives INSIDE Surface 1 as ordinary `#[test]`s in `verter_session/tests/cases/shared_process_contract.rs`, each performing many operations sequentially in the one process nextest gives it — not a second archive, not a second run. The skipped lane stays implemented: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --profile no-debug-assertions` (compile-only — catches an item wrongly hidden behind `cfg(debug_assertions)`), then a small package-scoped `cargo nextest run -p verter_shipped_cfg_contract --cargo-profile no-debug-assertions` — the ONLY tests in the repo that execute with `debug_assertions`/overflow-checks off (two profile-sanity canaries plus real `VerterHost` scenarios). Until it is re-enabled, that defect class is uncovered by the gate. Before the archive build it runs a freshness-tooling preflight: it ensures the workspace `buf` + `oxfmt` binaries are present (auto-running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` inside the mutex/timeout/stall machinery when the `node_modules/.bin` shims are missing), then VERDICT-GATES the `cases::typeinfo_proto_ts_freshness::*` byte-pin tolerance on the outcome — tooling present/installed ⇒ tolerance OFF, so a freshness failure is a HARD gate failure (exit 1), NOT PASS-WITH-TOLERATED; a deterministic install failure (e.g. frozen-lockfile mismatch) ⇒ a LOUD setup failure (exit 127), never silently tolerated (when an install is attempted — both `node_modules/.bin/{buf,oxfmt}` shims already present ⇒ the preflight returns already-present and no install runs); when pnpm is not resolvable AND `buf` is not resolvable the Rust byte-pin pair SKIPS gracefully and PASSES, so the gate reports an ORDINARY PASS (no FAIL line) — the verdict-gated tolerance flips ON there only as a LATENT safety net that would surface PASS-WITH-TOLERATED solely in the unusual case the pair produced a tolerated FAIL despite `buf` being absent. `oxfmt` absence NEVER grants tolerance — with `buf` present, a missing `oxfmt` is a LOUD setup failure (exit 127), not a degraded run. Run it with `node_modules` present (the normal path) so the byte-pin runs GENUINELY: with the tooling present a freshness failure is a HARD FAIL (a real stale-binding regression to regenerate + commit) — PASS-WITH-TOLERATED is NEVER the regression signal on a normal machine, and on a buf-less runner the pair yields an ordinary PASS via the skip, not PASS-WITH-TOLERATED. See docs/arch/gate-performance.md.
   379	node scripts/gate.mjs --exhaustive            # CI/release/complete diagnostics/comparable benchmarks: Surface 1 collects all failures (`--no-fail-fast`). The shipped-cfg lane is currently skipped in this mode too.
   380	
   381	# The underlying SURFACE 1 — runnable directly (no Node, or debugging in isolation):
   382	cargo nextest run --workspace                # SURFACE 1 — every workspace test target INCLUDING the verter_session integration binaries AND shared_process_contract.rs, per-test process isolation
   383	cargo test --workspace --doc                 # Rust doctests only; run when rustdoc examples changed or explicitly requested
   384	cargo test --package verter_compiler test_name   # Specific Rust test
   385	# NOTE: bare `cargo test --workspace --tests` historically SILENTLY SKIPPED the verter_session integration
   386	# suite (~4404 tests) because a `session_metrics` Cargo feature unified differently standalone vs in the
   387	# workspace, dropping those binaries from the workspace test set. That feature was removed (metrics are now
   388	# a runtime `HostConfig.metrics_enabled` toggle, not a Cargo feature) and the skip no longer reproduces —
   389	# confirmed by diffing the built executable sets of `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run -v` against
   390	# `cargo test -p verter_session --tests --no-run -v` (same verter_session executables in both). Still run
   391	# `node scripts/gate.mjs` as the sole Rust gate regardless (Surface 1; the shipped-cfg guard is currently
   392	# skipped and disclosed). Bare `--workspace --tests` and plain `cargo nextest run --workspace` are not
   393	# that gate.
   394	cargo test --package verter_compiler 2>&1 | tail -60  # Full suite with truncated output
   395	```
   396	
   397	The bare gate is the local fail-fast policy: nextest stops scheduling after its first failure. A PASS means
   398	Surface 1 passed; the shipped-cfg guard is currently skipped and is disclosed on every run. Use `--exhaustive`
   399	when the red run itself must collect every Surface 1 failure; CI and release always pass it explicitly.
   400	
   401	**Oversize-source advisory:** `scripts/gate.mjs` scans production Rust sources and warns for each
   402	non-exempt file above 1,500 lines as `path (N lines)`. File size is informational and never affects the
   403	gate verdict.
   404	
   405	**Resource ceilings — MEMORY-CEILING-MANDATORY.** Every gate/`--prepare` run is bounded by three flags,
   406	each host-derived by default and overridable: `--build-jobs <N>` (cargo build parallelism, default
   407	`min(cpuCount, memory tier)` where the effective memory ceiling selects 12 jobs at `>=16GiB`, 8 jobs at
   408	`>=12GiB`, otherwise 4), `--test-threads <N>` (nextest/libtest thread count, gate-only, default
   409	`min(12, cpuCount)`), `--memory-limit <SIZE>` (active child-tree RSS ceiling, e.g. `8GiB`/`12288MiB`,
   410	default `max(512MiB, 50% of physical RAM)`). Policy: every gate run — agent or CI — goes through this
   411	bounded wrapper with an explicit or defaulted `--memory-limit`; there is no sanctioned unbounded
   412	invocation. Build jobs and test threads are independently owned defaults; the omitted build value is CPU-
   413	and memory-clamped, the omitted test value is CPU-clamped, and explicit positive overrides are preserved
   414	exactly. A breach kills the active child tree fast
   415	and exits 123 (`ABORTED — memory ceiling`) — this
   416	means NO gate verdict was produced. The same rule covers TIMEOUT (124), STALL (125), and any run whose
   417	summary did not complete: an aborted or incomplete run is NOT PROVEN, never a PASS, and must never be
   418	recorded as one.
   419	
   420	**Build-prerequisite preflight (fail-closed, the gate's FIRST step).** Parts of the Rust suite load
   421	artifacts cargo does not build: the real-provider suites spawn the pinned tsserver with `--globalPlugins
   422	@verter/typescript-plugin --pluginProbeLocations packages/vue-vscode/node_modules`, a pnpm symlink to
   423	`packages/typescript-plugin` whose `main` is `dist/index.js` — a `tsc -b` OUTPUT that `pnpm install` does
   424	NOT produce. With the symlink present but the dist absent, tsserver loads no plugin and ~64 `*_tsserver`
   425	tests fail with `TS2307: Cannot find module './Comp.vue'`, indistinguishable from a compiler regression.
   426	So before the freshness preflight, before cargo, and before any test, `gate.mjs` **loads** that plugin
   427	entry in a child process (`require()` of the probe directory, exactly what tsserver resolves) and on any
   428	load failure FAILS CLOSED (exit 127, marker `BUILD-PREREQUISITE MISSING`) naming the probe target, the
   429	load error, the producing packages, and the producer command. The oracle is a real load, not a list of
   430	files to stat: the entry eagerly requires its emitted helpers and `@verter/language-shared`'s entry
   431	re-exports a dozen emitted siblings, so a stat list mirrors the emit graph and drifts — both `index.js`
   432	present with one helper missing passes every stat and still throws inside tsserver. The probe runs under
   433	**tsserver's** environment, not the gate's — it strips the `CHILD_PROCESS_ENV_DENYLIST` the tsserver
   434	launcher strips, read out of `crates/verter_type_runtime/src/tsserver/ipc.rs` so the two cannot drift,
   435	because otherwise a `NODE_OPTIONS` preload can forge a status-0 load — and its timeout is a hard `SIGKILL`
   436	bounded by the gate's own remaining deadline, since `spawnSync`'s default SIGTERM is trappable and a
   437	trapping child both hangs the gate (with the single-flight mutex held) and returns a false positive.
   438	Failure classes are typed (`reason`), so only `module-not-found` may ever be read as "never built". It
   439	proves the closure **resolves**, not that it is **fresh**; a stale-but-loadable dist is a separate,
   440	deliberately out-of-scope problem. It never builds the artifacts (the verdict must not depend on a mutation the gate performed) and
   441	never skips the affected tests (with no install at all those tests SKIP and the gate goes green while
   442	proving nothing). Produce them with `pnpm --filter @verter/language-shared --filter
   443	@verter/typescript-plugin build` — deliberately NOT `pnpm build` and NOT `--filter
   444	@verter/typescript-plugin...` (the trailing ellipsis pulls in `@verter/native`'s `napi build --release`).
   445	`--prepare` is exempt; it runs no test. `(GB9)` in `scripts/gate-selftest.mjs` proves the discrimination in
   446	six directions against the real production CLI on a synthetic miniature of the package graph.

   448	### End-of-change Checks
   449	
   450	Run after **every** change. Verter's crates are highly interconnected — a change in one crate frequently breaks tests in dependent crates. Always run the full workspace suite:
   451	
   452	```bash
   453	node scripts/gate.mjs 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.txt   # CANONICAL Rust gate — SINGLE-TEST-UNIVERSE: one dev archive/list, then archive-backed SURFACE 1 (`cargo nextest run`, process isolation, including `shared_process_contract.rs`). The shipped-cfg lane is currently SKIPPED (temporary; `SHIPPED_CFG_LANE_ENABLED` in `scripts/gate-internals.mjs`) — a PASS is Surface 1 only, disclosed on every run. Run with `node_modules` present so the freshness-tooling preflight is a no-op and the `cases::typeinfo_proto_ts_freshness::*` byte-pin runs GENUINELY: with the tooling present a freshness failure is a HARD gate failure (exit 1, a real stale-binding regression to regenerate + commit), NOT tolerated. On a buf-less runner (pnpm not resolvable AND `buf` not resolvable) the Rust byte-pin SKIPS and PASSES, so the gate reports an ordinary PASS — the verdict-gated tolerance flips ON there only as a latent safety net (PASS-WITH-TOLERATED appears solely if the pair somehow emitted a tolerated FAIL despite `buf` being absent, which the skip does not). `oxfmt` absence never grants tolerance (with `buf` present a missing `oxfmt` is a LOUD setup failure); a deterministic install failure (frozen-lockfile mismatch) fails loud as setup (exit 127) when an install is attempted (both shims already present ⇒ no install runs).
   454	cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
   455	cargo check --workspace --release   # Compiles the REAL release profile (opt-level 3 + fat LTO), which the gate does not: surface 1 is debug, and the shipped-cfg lane (cheap `no-debug-assertions` profile) is currently skipped. `debug_assert!` gates on `cfg!` — a RUNTIME constant — so its body still name-resolves in release: a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` helper called inside one is an E0425 in every release build (napi and wasm artifacts included) while compiling clean in debug. This is a CHECK — it RUNS NO TESTS, so it CANNOT observe the runtime half of the same class (a state mutation written inside a `debug_assert!` argument, which compiles fine and silently never executes in a shipped build). That half is covered only by `verter_shipped_cfg_contract` under `no-debug-assertions`, which the gate currently skips. Do not read a green `cargo check --workspace --release` as coverage of `debug_assert!` behaviour.
   456	cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p verter_wasm -- -D warnings   # Host clippy cannot see target-gated code. The wasm32 artifact is what the playground and `@verter/wasm` consumers run. The `wasm32-wasip1`/`wasip2` clippy jobs cover the SEPARATE lapce/zed manifests, not this one.
   457	cargo fmt --all --check
   458	pnpm install --frozen-lockfile   # Verify lockfile is in sync (CI uses this); also what the gate's preflight runs to make the freshness byte-pin run genuinely
   459	```

   461	Confirm `cargo clippy --version` reports the `rust-toolchain.toml`-pinned version before
   462	trusting any of the three lint/check results — a clippy run on a different toolchain is not
   463	evidence about the one CI uses.

   469	**Agent test policy:** `node scripts/gate.mjs` is the default local Rust gate; after one archive/list it runs archive-backed Surface 1. The shipped-cfg check/contract lane is currently skipped (temporary; disclosed on every run — a PASS is Surface 1 only). It is fail-fast on red. `node scripts/gate.mjs --exhaustive` is required for CI, release, complete failure diagnostics, and comparable benchmarks; it changes failure collection only, adding `--no-fail-fast` to the Surface 1 nextest invocation. Neither policy creates a second whole-workspace archive, and either may emit PASS only after Surface 1 completed. The skipped lane is not part of that PASS. A contributor without Node, or debugging Surface 1 in isolation, runs `cargo nextest run --workspace` directly. The `cases::typeinfo_proto_ts_freshness::*` buf/oxfmt byte-pin is the only tolerated failure, and tolerance remains verdict-gated by the freshness-tooling preflight: tooling present/installed makes freshness failures hard; when neither pnpm nor buf resolves, the pair skips and the ordinary verdict stays PASS. `oxfmt` absence alone never grants tolerance, and a deterministic tooling-install failure is a loud setup failure. Run the gate with `node_modules` present. Do not run bare `cargo test --workspace` (no `--tests`) by default: it pulls in doctests and example builds without improving the normal verification loop. Run doctests (`cargo test --workspace --doc`) only when rustdoc examples changed or the user explicitly asks.

   471	### Documentation Updates
   472	
   473	After adding, changing, or removing features, update the **owning** documentation:
   474	
   475	- **Domain skills** (`.claude/skills/`) — update the skill that owns the affected module or API
   476	- **`CLAUDE.md`** — only if summaries or skill pointers change
   477	- **`AGENTS.md`** — if skill routing or shared sources change
   478	- **`docs/`** — API docs, guide pages, contributing guides
   479	- **Inline doc comments** — Public API rustdoc (`///`) and JSDoc (`/** */`) on changed signatures
   480	
   481	Skip for purely internal refactors that don't change public behavior, module paths, or APIs.
   482	
   483	### Testing Requirements
   484	
   485	**MANDATORY: TDD must be followed for EVERY code change. Non-negotiable.**
   486	
   487	1. Write failing tests FIRST — verify they fail before implementing
   488	2. Implement minimum code to pass
   489	3. Run tests, verify green
   490	4. Refactor while keeping tests green
   491	
   492	Coverage: new features need tests, bug fixes need regression tests, refactors must keep existing tests passing.
   493	
   494	**Always include negative assertions**: verify both what SHOULD and should NOT be present. Codegen tests must check removed syntax is absent. Type tests must include `@ts-expect-error` guards against `any`/`never`.
   495	
   496	**Public-boundary acceptance**: for every changed user-visible IDE, API, or compiler outcome, each affected acceptance ID has an automated public-boundary test asserting the required result AND the relevant forbidden or fail-closed result. Provider-selection, status, unit, and architecture tests supplement but do not substitute for that boundary test. A substrate block may inherit a parent boundary test only by recording the acceptance-ID mapping and executing that test in its gate. Enforcement is judgment — reviewers assess the actual invocation path and assertions, not the filename; §1a proves discrimination; confirm reruns the mapped test.
   497

   504	### Verification Must Prove Execution (MANDATORY)
   505	
   506	A required gate passes only on fresh, input-bound evidence that: every applicable required job was eligible and ran; the intended tree-derived surface was owned and independently discovered; selectors matched non-zero work; required source, build, and fixture prerequisites matched the tested tree; executed work was non-zero; unexpected prerequisite skips were zero; child deadlines were strictly below their parent killer; and a terminal summary completed. **Exit status 0 alone, a self-declared test universe, or a missing required-job result is FAIL.** Every tracked test or guard has exactly one declared primary gate; a hand-maintained filename list may not define the primary universe unless generated from independent discovery and parity-checked.
   507	
   508	Attestation alone is insufficient — a receipt faithfully attests whatever incomplete universe the runner defines for itself. The durable design needs all three: fresh execution attestation; independently tree-derived inventory/discovery parity; and per-surface negative-control mutation through the exact canonical entry point. A single global canary cannot detect an omitted unrelated spec.
   509	
   510	**The negative control must itself be proven to have applied.** A plant that fails to apply reports a pass: `perl`/`sed`/`grep` exit 0 on a non-match, so a mutation's exit code is never proof it landed, and a verification search hitting a PRE-EXISTING occurrence of the planted string is a false positive. Prove the mutation is present, unique, and new in the source before trusting the run; a green planted run means the plant failed until proven otherwise. A discrimination check that cannot distinguish "the plant did not apply" from "the code is correct" is not a discrimination check.

Until that guard, its attesting driver, and the required-job aggregator land, this rule is held only by §1a and confirm judgment.

So the gap is named rather than hidden — the deferral, its owner (the gate-integrity block), its resolution gate (that block's landing), and the live in-tree instances are recorded in [`docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md`](docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md). Promotion to `(CRITICAL)` with its own `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS` row, in the same change that lands the guard, is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION of that block (ledger row GI-4).    160	### Carrier IDE TS Surface Principle
   161	
   162	North star for the IDE/LSP experience: for every carrier with an IDE projection (`.vue`, `.svelte`), the script block (`<script>`, `<script setup>`, Svelte module/instance scripts) AND the supported template/markup expressions are **ONE** generated TypeScript/JavaScript/JSX surface — interpolations (`{{ }}`, Svelte `{expr}`), directive/attribute expression values (`v-if`/`v-for`/`v-bind`/`:`/`v-on`/`@`/`v-model`/`v-slot` and dynamic args; Svelte `bind:`/`on:`/`class:`/`style:`/`use:`, `{#if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`/snippets, `{@render}`/`{@html}`/`{@const}`, rune calls) all lower into it. That surface is obtained through the IDE path (`CompileTarget::IDE`/`TSX`), synced to the active TypeProvider, with provider positions/ranges/edits mapped back through the document's `ProviderPositionMapper`.
   163	
   164	**The bar:** for any supported mapped TS/JS expression position, every provider-backed IDE feature — diagnostics, hover, definition/type-definition, references, rename, completion/resolve, signature help, document highlights, semantic tokens, inlay hints, and generic code actions whose edits map exactly — should behave like the equivalent standalone `.ts`/`.js`/`.jsx` program, with results mapped back to the carrier source. A binding represented in BOTH script and template is discoverable and renamable from either side (rename spans script + template; find-all-references finds both). This holds for **both Vue and Svelte** over the shared LSP path.
   165

Source actions (organize-imports, fix-all, formatting) require explicit per-action support and tests; they are NOT implied by this principle. This is a **principle, not yet a `(CRITICAL)` guarded rule** — it is promoted to CRITICAL once real-provider cross-region Vue/Svelte regression tests guard it.

    39	   lines), the TypeScript-style module resolver wrongly homed in the scheduler/tsgo-dependent
    40	   `verter_workspace` crate today. This is a multi-crate structural move touching `verter_session`'s
    41	   module tree, `verter_workspace`'s module tree, `verter_semantic`'s Cargo.toml dependency edges, and
    42	   the landed dependency-layers closure guard — not a `pub(crate)` facade behind which nothing moves.
    43	2. **The `NeedInputs`/`AttemptOutcome` cutover is full-coverage, not a first cut.** Every non-flow
    44	   `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
    45	   batched outcome — not just the two `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` call sites the prior
    46	   draft scoped it to. TypeInfo projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` today
    47	   (`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`), so "module/import resolution only"
    48	   was never even a clean existing boundary to cut at.
    49	
    50	Effort and breadth are not reasons to shrink this (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning: "Time constraints,
    51	implementation size, migration breadth... are not valid reasons to weaken the design"). The charter
    52	states the true scope instead of preserving the five-line framing that would mislead whoever picks this
    53	up. C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
    54	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and `verter_workspace::resolver` — into the
    55	two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a `ModuleResolverCore` that owns
    56	TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow `TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node
    57	traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution, relation/inference, effective typing,
    58	recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and exactness/completeness propagation. Neither
    59	target type exists in code today; both names describe roles the current tree already plays under
    60	different names, in the wrong crate, with the wrong I/O coupling. C1 does not invent new resolution
    61	semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be identical to
    62	today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code (crate, not just module), how
    63	many duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform
    64	I/O directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
    65	
    66	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
    67	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
    68	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
    69	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions, even
    70	though (per the full-coverage ruling) the *plumbing* around every call into them now must support
    71	`AttemptOutcome`. It owns convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, physical crate
    72	placement, and full-coverage batched/resumable load outcomes so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume
    73	the same kernel a blocking lifecycle consumes today.
    74	
    75	## Sequencing
    76	
    77	C1's predecessor set is satisfied: `A6`, `B1`, `B2` are `ACCEPTED`, and `CM1` is now `ACCEPTED` with
    78	all three review mandates `PASS` (`program-state.toml`, CM1 row); it was `REVIEW` when this was written. C1's own ledger `status`
    79	is `LOCKED`, not `READY` (`program-state.toml`, block C1) — even once predecessors clear, predecessor
    80	satisfaction alone does not authorise dispatch; this charter still reads DRAFT and no AMD ratifies it, so
    81	C1 stays gated on charter ratification independently of its DAG predecessors. The ledger's `current_block`
    82	is `J1` (`program-state.toml:22`); BV1, the block C1 previously sequenced after, has itself long since
    83	reached `ACCEPTED`. **C1 dispatch follows charter ratification AND CM1 reaching `ACCEPTED`**, not a
    84	specific other block's landing alone. This charter does not
    85	propose running C1 concurrently with any other in-flight block absent a ratified concurrency exception.
    86	
    87	## Intent Contract
    88	
    89	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
    90	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
    91	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
    92	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
    93	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation), by omission (no lifecycle exists
    94	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), and by the wrong crate holding the kernel at all (a session-tier
    95	crate that already depends on the compiler, so nothing compiler-tier can embed it without a cycle) — not
    96	by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added
    97	without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
    98	
    99	**Required observable outcomes.**
   100	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
   101	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
   102	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
   103	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
   104	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
   105	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
   106	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer — for **every** non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/
   107	  `TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt, not a subset.
   108	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_workspace`,
   109	  `verter_session`, `verter_scheduler`, nor `verter_tsgo_api` on any target — this closes debt row A5-DD1
   110	  by *deleting* the exception, not widening it (`crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/
   111	  workspace_dependency_layers.rs`, the `ratified_upward_exceptions()` row keyed
   112	  `"verter_semantic"`).
   113	- `resolver_core`, `resolver_store`'s immutable observation types, `project_semantic_dispatch`, and
   114	  `ModuleResolverCore` (the relocated `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver`) physically live in
   115	  `verter_semantic`. `verter_compiler` can depend on the converged kernel directly — it already does
   116	  (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`, `verter_semantic = { path = "../verter_semantic" }`) — with no
   117	  new edge and no cycle.
   118	- A new capability-limited, immutable **observation interface**, defined inside `verter_semantic`, does
   119	  **not** extend today's `ResolverContext` and cannot name, hold, or return `VerterHost` or the
   120	  scheduler — not because a marker says so, but because `verter_semantic`'s crate dependency closure
   121	  makes those types structurally unnameable from inside it.
   122	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (relocated to `verter_semantic`) has exactly as many
   123	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct blocking lifecycles; a lifecycle that
   124	  cannot resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
   125	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
   126	
   127	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
   128	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
   129	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
   130	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:790-796` — C1 preserves this unchanged across the
   131	  crate move).
   132	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
   133	  observation views").
   134	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
   135	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext`/observation-interface implementor
   136	  served it, for identical inputs.
   137	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
   138	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
   139	- A marker type presented as *the* proof of I/O freedom. Per the ruling on Fork 3, a marker may
   140	  *classify* the observation interface; the proof is that the interface's home crate cannot name the
   141	  host/scheduler types at all. A subtrait of `ResolverContext` is never an acceptable substitute — it
   142	  inherits `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`/the host escape hatch
   143	  (`resolver_context.rs:780-782,261-266,700-717`) exactly as the rejected draft position did.
   144	- Any resolver-tier operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt that is left blocking-only, with no
   145	  `NeedInputs`-capable path — that is exactly the coverage gap Fork 4's ruling forecloses.
   146	
   147	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
   148	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
   149	point) — unchanged by the crate move. `ResolverContext`/observation-interface implementors are lifecycle
   150	*adapters* over that one authority, never alternate authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot
   151	prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s
   152	`CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split, `.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) —
   153	C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken it while adding the `NeedInputs` outcome
   154	alongside it.

Per C1-AC-7 and the Authority/fallback order clause, the observation interface is the *only* surface an I/O-free (C2-shaped) caller can reach a non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation through — `ResolverContext` itself can call `ensure_loaded`/`wait_or_drive`, so it is not usable I/O-free. "Every reachable operation" therefore reduces to "every method on this one finite, closed trait." The trait is defined so every method returns `AttemptOutcome<T>` at the type level (never a bare `T`, `Result<T, _>`, or a call that can block) — a non-conforming method is a compile error at authoring time, not a gap a test could miss. Gate: one exhaustive test double (`impl <ObservationInterface> for TestDouble`) that must implement every trait method to compile; a method added later that does not return `AttemptOutcome<T>` fails to compile at the double, not at a sampled runtime assertion. If a future operation cannot be expressed this way, that is itself a Fork-4-reopening discovery (see Abort/rescope), not a reason to fall back to sampling. |

   221	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract — full coverage (Fork 4)
   222	
   223	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
   224	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
   225	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   226	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
   227	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
   228	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet" crates/`
   229	— zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
   230	
   231	**Coverage is full, per the Fork 4 ruling — not "module/import resolution only."** Every non-flow
   232	`ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
   233	outcome: module/import resolution, decl-body lowering, relation/inference queries driven through
   234	`execute_relate`'s plumbing (the algorithm itself stays `Preserve`; only the calling convention around it
   235	changes), and the member/JSDoc-hydration path that already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   236	(`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`) today. `contracts/input-loading.md:5-19`
   237	is unqualified across compiler/resolver/TypeInfo kernels, and ADR-011:19-28 requires each attempt to
   238	report the maximal sound missing-observation set — a partial cut would leave C2 unable to plan its
   239	complete semantic demand closure before projection (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:18,44-53`) for
   240	whichever operations were left out. Internally, `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` may still
   241	become the two central observation-or-demand choke points every covered operation funnels through — that
   242	is an implementation strategy, not a scope carve-out. Acceptance is never "one real load point exercised
   243	by a test harness"; it is every reachable operation covered.
   244	
   245	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
   246	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
   247	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
   248	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
   249	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
   250	C1's obligation ends at: every resolver-tier operation reachable from a projection attempt, one immutable
   251	snapshot, one typed outcome per attempt. C2's obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the
   252	snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay tokens.
   253	
   254	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
   255	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
   256	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
   257	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome, across the full operation surface, so a *new* I/O-free
   258	lifecycle can reuse the same resolution logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every
   259	existing call site to stop blocking — `HostResolverContext`/`SessionResolverContext` keep blocking by
   260	design.

   366	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
   367	
   368	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
   369	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
   370	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
   371	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
   372	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
   373	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges (now physically in
   374	`verter_semantic`) remains the single authority `D1` integrates against behind its private non-production
   375	test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later extends without needing a second relation/name
   376	authority (`program.md:253`). The full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` threading touches the *calling
   377	convention* around `execute_relate` (per Fork 4) but never the relation algorithm itself.
   378	
   379	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
   380	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
   381	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
   382	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
   383	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is now concretely: a converged kernel
   384	physically resident in `verter_semantic` that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be
   385	driven from an I/O-free observation interface and returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking across its
   386	**full** operation surface, and (c) is constructible without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/
   387	`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery *by construction of the crate graph*, so C2's compiler-facing
   388	facade embeds `verter_semantic` the same way `verter_compiler` already does today
   389	(`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`) with no cycle risk.

   393	Per `program.md:196`: **lifecycle differs; module/name/type/relation meaning does not.** Concretely: the

   395	algorithms, dependency-neutral value types, `AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`) lives in `verter_semantic`; the
   396	three (or more, once the I/O-free observation interface exists) lifecycle implementors give bit-identical
   397	resolved answers for identical inputs; the duplicated boilerplate between `HostResolverContext` and
   398	`SessionResolverContext` is gone; `verter_semantic`'s production closure excludes `verter_workspace`,
   399	`verter_session`, `verter_scheduler`, and `verter_tsgo_api` on every target with the A5-DD1 exception row
   400	deleted, not recorded as still-permitted; `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` exists and covers every

   441	   immutable `RouteAnalysisInputs` snapshot **downward** into the existing pure extractors. This does not
   442	   foreclose `F1`'s future committed-input-authority design; relocating the trait would have.

   444	   subtrait of `ResolverContext`, inherits `ensure_loaded`/the host escape hatch — the draft's claim that

   447	   and cannot return a host; the crate firewall (from ruling 1) is what makes the host unnameable, not the
   448	   marker by itself.
   449	4. **Fork 4 (coverage scope) — VIOLATES.** "Module/import resolution only" was never a clean cut — TypeInfo
   450	   projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`. `contracts/input-loading.md` is unqualified,
   451	   and ADR-011 requires the maximal sound missing-observation set per attempt. Ruling:

   453	   from a C2 projection attempt; `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` may become internal choke

   223	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
   224	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
   225	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   226	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
   227	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
   228	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet" crates/`
   229	— zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
   230	
   231	**Coverage is full, per the Fork 4 ruling — not "module/import resolution only."** Every non-flow
   232	`ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
   233	outcome: module/import resolution, decl-body lowering, relation/inference queries driven through
   234	`execute_relate`'s plumbing (the algorithm itself stays `Preserve`; only the calling convention around it
   235	changes), and the member/JSDoc-hydration path that already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   236	(`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`) today. `contracts/input-loading.md:5-19`
   237	is unqualified across compiler/resolver/TypeInfo kernels, and ADR-011:19-28 requires each attempt to
   238	report the maximal sound missing-observation set — a partial cut would leave C2 unable to plan its
   239	complete semantic demand closure before projection (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:18,44-53`) for
   240	whichever operations were left out. Internally, `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` may still
   241	become the two central observation-or-demand choke points every covered operation funnels through — that
   242	is an implementation strategy, not a scope carve-out. Acceptance is never "one real load point exercised
   243	by a test harness"; it is every reachable operation covered.
   244	
   245	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
   246	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
   247	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
   248	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
   249	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
   250	C1's obligation ends at: every resolver-tier operation reachable from a projection attempt, one immutable
   251	snapshot, one typed outcome per attempt. C2's obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the
   252	snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay tokens.
   253	
   254	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
   255	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
   256	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
   257	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome, across the full operation surface, so a *new* I/O-free
   258	lifecycle can reuse the same resolution logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every
   259	existing call site to stop blocking — `HostResolverContext`/`SessionResolverContext` keep blocking by
   260	design.

    14	
    15	# C1 architecture addendum — three execution gaps
    16	
    17	**Source:** bounded architecture challenge, read-only, run against `program/architecture-lock`
    18	at `8c2189389`. Commissioned by the maintainer when C1 was held before ratification, scoped to
    19	exactly three discovered execution gaps and forbidden from re-scoping C1 smaller.
    20	
    21	**Baseline preserved:** the C1 charter, its research, and all four prior architecture rulings
    22	(`ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS`) remain binding and were not reopened.
    23	
    24	**Amendment determination:** no accepted ADR, no DAG edge, and no program outcome changes under any
    25	of the three gap resolutions, so no AMD is required. The extraction into `verter_semantic` and full
    26	behavioural `AttemptOutcome` coverage both remain required.
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## GAP 1 — Cross-crate trait sealing
    31	
    32	Use the repository’s existing idiom exactly:
    33	
    34	```rust
    35	// verter_semantic/src/type_info/observations.rs
    36	mod sealed {
    37	    pub trait Sealed {}
    38	}
    39	
    40	pub trait ObservationRead: sealed::Sealed {
    41	    fn lookup(&self, key: &ObservationKey) -> ObservationValueRef<'_>;
    42	}
    43	
    44	impl sealed::Sealed for ObservationSnapshot {}
    45	impl ObservationRead for ObservationSnapshot { /* ... */ }
    46	```
    47	
    48	The private module is the sealing token. Only code inside `verter_semantic` can name `sealed::Sealed`; a foreign `impl ObservationRead for CompileTypeInfo` fails because `CompileTypeInfo: sealed::Sealed` cannot be satisfied, and attempting the marker impl fails with private-module error E0603. This is the same shape used by:
    49	
    50	- `ResolverContext`: private marker at `crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:82`, supertrait at `:161`, sanctioned marker impls at `:745`.
    51	- Public cross-crate `AttachOwnership`: `crates/verter_tsgo_api/src/attach.rs:85`, `:98`, `:113`.
    52	- `NegativeEvidence`: `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/framework_facts/mod.rs:35`, `:45`; its sanctioned implementation is at `framework_facts/svelte.rs:178`.
    53	- The existing foreign-implementation compile failure: `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/compile-fail/deferred_callable_is_sealed_to_its_two_consumers.rs:21-38`.
    54	
    55	Therefore the legal implementors are semantic-owned types only: production `ObservationSnapshot`, and—if useful—a test-only type whose implementations are written inside `observations.rs`. `verter_compiler`, `verter_session`, integration tests, and external mocks consume an `ObservationSnapshot`; they do not implement the trait. They construct it through a semantic-owned builder from immutable data. No callbacks, closures, host references, or trait objects belong in the snapshot.
    56	
    57	`CompileTypeInfo` must compose an `ObservationSnapshot` and call the kernel. If it genuinely must implement the interface, the interface cannot remain sealed: Rust has no friend-crate exception. The same applies to external test doubles. An exhaustive external double and a private-supertrait seal are directly incompatible.
    58	
    59	This also falsifies C1-AC-4’s proposed relocated `ResolverContext`: `VerterHost` being local makes the foreign-trait impl orphan-legal, but it cannot implement the foreign trait’s private semantic supertrait (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:149`). Keep the lifecycle `ResolverContext`/`RequestBoundResolverContext` seal and its adapters in `verter_session`; extract their semantic operations behind the semantic-owned snapshot/gateway. This changes the charter’s file-level split at `C1.md:186`, not the kernel extraction or C1 outcome.
    60	
    61	Mechanical gates:
    62	
    63	- A compile-fail fixture in `verter_semantic/tests/compile-fail/` attempts both foreign marker and observation-interface impls.
    64	- `rg 'impl (sealed::Sealed|ObservationRead)' crates/verter_semantic/src/type_info` has only the sanctioned implementations.
    65	- Compiler/session tests use the public builder or semantic-owned test fixture, never a foreign `impl`.
    66	
    67	## GAP 2 — Complete extraction dependency closure
    68	
    69	Disproved as a literal file/directory relocation.
    70	
    71	The complete direct session-module cut set reached by the named members is:
    72	
    73	`build_toolchain_fingerprint`, `cache_runtime`, `capture_token`, `component_meta_audit`, `component_meta_caches`, `component_meta_materialize`, `decl_body_memo`, `decl_lowering`, `fact_emission`, `fact_signature_helpers`, `file_artifact_store`, `flow_return_audit`, `flow_slice_content`, `hash`, `host_executor`, `host_manage`, `host_resolve`, `identity_interner`, `instant`, `intrinsic_registry`, `invalidation_domain`, `locator_identity`, `loop5_instrumentation`, `mapper_binder_registry`, `meta_resolve`, `project_type_store`, `request_context`, `resolved_import_facts`, `semantic_query`, `semantic_query_memo`, `session_view`, `store_view_roots`, `structural_carrier_producer`, `typeinfo`, `types`, and `VerterHost`.
    74	
    75	Representative roots are mechanically visible in `project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:62-71`, `resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:68-78`, `resolver_store.rs:1-2`, and the module declarations at `crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:274-369`. The dispositions are:
    76	
    77	- Move into `verter_semantic`: `semantic_query`, `semantic_query_memo`’s graph/value core, `identity_interner`, `intrinsic_registry`, `locator_identity`, `mapper_binder_registry`, `flow_slice_content`, and the pure algorithm/value portions of `component_meta_materialize`, `decl_body_memo`, `fact_emission`, `fact_signature_helpers`, `meta_resolve`, `project_type_store`, `structural_carrier_producer`, and non-flow `typeinfo`.
    78	- Stay in `verter_session`, with captured data passed down: `VerterHost`, `host_*`, lifecycle `ResolverContext`, artifact/project/store managers, `session_view`, `store_view_roots`, `resolved_import_facts` storage, lowering services, cache admission/singleflight/retention, request context/cancellation, audit and instrumentation. The relevant live accesses appear at `resolver_context.rs:188-196,261-266,700-717`, `project_semantic_dispatch/lower.rs:403-418`, and `project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:2016-2078`.

Cut these paths and supply captured language, prepared-declaration, surface, and cancellation-state observations. The host/native/wire portions of those files stay behind, so `component_meta/` cannot move as an unmodified wildcard despite `C1.md:19-24`.
    88	
    89	4. **Store and cache infrastructure.** `HostStoreView` is not a dependency-neutral value: its snapshot contains session `StoreViewRoots` (`resolver_store.rs:1385-1411`), and those roots retain scheduler, workspace, artifact-store, project-store, and resolution-store handles (`store_view_roots.rs:385-418`). Its capture reads `VerterHost` and workspace generations (`resolver_store.rs:638-655,792-816`). Keep `HostStoreView`, its roots, and manager in session; move `StoreViewValidationToken`-like scalar DTOs and introduce the semantic-owned observation snapshot. This changes the member boundary claimed at `C1.md:187`.
    90	
    91	5. **Workspace fact vocabulary.** `resolver_core/fact_read_set.rs:1-5`, `resolver_core/reuse.rs:46-51`, `resolver_core/request_store_view.rs:81-94`, and `resolver_core/mod.rs:669-672` import workspace-owned fact/cache types. Move the neutral fact identities, read-set values, populations, and validation-result vocabulary into semantic; workspace and session then import them downward. Live fact registries, published roots, transactions, and generation capture remain workspace/session.
    92	
    93	6. **`ProjectResolver`.** Its pure algorithm depends on workspace DTOs and membership (`verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs:11-17,74-114`), but its resolution entry accepts live `WorkspaceRead` (`:321-365`), path resolution calls `probe_path`/`realpath` (`:1251-1267`), and package resolution calls live manifest reads (`:1654-1663`). Move the algorithm, request/result/manifest DTOs, and immutable membership predicate into semantic. Replace `WorkspaceRead` with snapshot lookups whose missing keys produce `NeedInputs`. Keep `resolve_tracked`, `TrackedResolutionCapability`, and `TransactionReader` in workspace (`:354-384`).

Deleting `verter_semantic → verter_workspace` at `crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml:24-27` removes the presently ratified transitive scheduler/tsgo reach (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:108-126`).

Its architectural home is genuinely ambiguous because C1 excludes flow behavior while requiring the entire dispatcher to relocate. To preserve the stated member scope, move the flow query/value and pure evaluation code unchanged; leave cache-node admission, retention, audit, and capture above.     98	
    99	`ConfiguredMembership` is the other ambiguous member: it mixes an immutable predicate with workspace construction/cache machinery (`membership.rs:13-17,189-256`). The executable split is a semantic immutable membership snapshot, populated by the workspace builder.
   100	
   101	Cycles to prevent:
   102	
   103	- `semantic ↔ compiler`: `template_class_facts.rs:6` versus compiler `Cargo.toml:59`.
   104	- `semantic ↔ protocol`: component-meta `:115` versus protocol `Cargo.toml:18`.
   105	- `semantic ↔ session`: any retained host/store/session reference versus session `Cargo.toml:122`.
   106	- `semantic ↔ workspace`: workspace must call the relocated resolver; semantic’s current workspace edge at `Cargo.toml:27` must be deleted first.
   107	
   108	Final verification is the existing Cargo-metadata production-closure gate (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:1-18,316-350`) with the semantic exception at `:118-126` deleted. No source scanner substitutes for that gate.
   109	
   110	## GAP 3 — Full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` proof
   111	
   112	The charter’s exhaustive-`impl` mechanism is invalid.
   113	
   114	- Adding a required method makes an existing impl incomplete, but adding a defaulted method does not. The repo demonstrates this directly: `ResolverContext::is_request_bound` has a default at `resolver_context.rs:179-181`, while the large `impl ResolverContext for VerterHost` beginning at `:817` omits it and compiles.
   115	- Even a required method proves only that the double supplies a body. A new method returning bare `T` can be added, implemented with bare `T`, and the exhaustive impl compiles. The impl does not constrain the trait author’s return type.
   116	- Generic methods, associated output types, and `async fn` do not improve this. They may make the trait non-dyn-compatible—the current code separately pins that at `resolver_context.rs:805-815`—but they do not force `AttemptOutcome`. An associated type can resolve to any type.
   117	- A Rust type alias to `AttemptOutcome<T>` is type-identical and therefore valid. It only defeats textual/name-based checking, not Rust type equality.
   118	- A foreign exhaustive double is forbidden by GAP 1’s seal. Only an in-module semantic test type can implement it, and it still suffers the default/return-shape defects above.
   119	- “Sole entry surface” is currently false: ProjectResolver uses `WorkspaceRead` directly (`resolver.rs:321-365`), component-meta reaches the host/scheduler (`component_meta/mod.rs:251-288`), and dispatch lowering calls host materialization (`lower.rs:403-418`).
   120	
   121	Replace the operation trait with one closed, non-overridable inherent gateway:
   122	
   123	```rust
   124	pub enum NonFlowOperation { /* every C2-reachable operation */ }
   125	pub enum NonFlowValue { /* heterogeneous results */ }
   126	
   127	impl TypeInfoCore {
   128	    pub fn attempt(
   129	        &self,
   130	        observations: &ObservationSnapshot,
   131	        operation: NonFlowOperation,
   132	    ) -> AttemptOutcome<NonFlowValue>;
   133	}
   134	```
   135	
   136	Keep the implementation modules and fields private. Match `NonFlowOperation` exhaustively with no wildcard. Adding a variant then forces the dispatcher to change, while every cross-crate operation necessarily returns the one inherent method’s `AttemptOutcome`. Compile-fail fixtures prove foreign code cannot implement a query/observation trait or access an alternate kernel operation. This is a mechanically valid proof of the closed cross-crate entry surface and its return shape.
   137	
   138	It is not—and stable Rust cannot make it—a complete proof that every internal helper is I/O-free. `verter_semantic` can still compile `std::fs`, `std::net`, a blocking primitive, a global/TLS read, or an I/O-capable callback without naming `VerterHost` or scheduler. Cargo’s crate firewall cannot observe those effects. A dedicated `#![no_std]` capability crate could strengthen that proof, but the binding ruling requires the existing `verter_semantic` crate.
   139	
   140	The honest mechanically checkable criterion is therefore:
   141	
   142	- Every external C2 operation is a `NonFlowOperation` and enters through `TypeInfoCore::attempt`.
   143	- All kernel internals are private to that module tree.
   144	- The semantic Cargo closure contains only layers 1–3.
   145	- Compile-fail tests pin sealing and private-entry unreachability.
   146	- Exhaustive all-missing-observation tests cover every enum variant and require `NeedInputs` or `Terminal`, never blocking.
   147	- Internal absence of direct I/O/blocking remains an audited/linted source invariant, not a type-system proof.
   148	
   149	Accepted ADR: unchanged by all three gap resolutions.
   150	
   151	Program DAG edge: unchanged; the planned dependency inversion remains higher layers → `verter_semantic`.
   152	
   153	Program outcome: unchanged; full non-flow extraction and full behavioral `AttemptOutcome` coverage remain required.
   154	
   155	GAP 1 VERDICT — Current cross-crate sealing design is impossible; seal semantic-owned snapshots and require compiler/session composition, not foreign implementations.
   156	
   157	GAP 2 VERDICT — The proposed files do not close below layer 4 as-is; C1 is executable only through the listed splits, cuts, and capture inversions.
   158	
   159	GAP 3 VERDICT — The exhaustive-`impl` proof is false; a closed inherent gateway proves boundary shape, but total internal I/O-freedom has no mechanically valid proof under the preserved existing-crate architecture.

   143	the same race one step further on.

   422	The bytes must be present at that path in the tree the validator runs against, per §0 step 2; the row
   423	and the bytes are one act, not two. The same digest is the value §1.4's `c1_stage2_ruling_sha256`
   424	carries, and the blob holding those bytes is what §1.2 calls `RULING_BLOB` — one set of bytes named
   425	three times, never three values to reconcile.
   426	
   427	#### SPEC 2 — the IN-PLACE extension of the existing C1 `[[authorization]]` (§0 step 4)
   428	
   429	**There is exactly one `[[authorization]]` for block `C1`, it already exists, and it is EXTENDED — not
   430	replaced, not duplicated, not recreated.** The validator rejects a second record for a block and
   431	requires one for a block past LOCKED, so both a duplicate and a delete-then-recreate are wrong; but
   432	neither failure is the dangerous one. **The dangerous edit passes every check: a wholesale rewrite of
   433	`scope` into the key block alone.** The field is only tested for non-emptiness, so replacing a long
   434	ratified semantic scope with a short key string is invisible to the validator and destroys authority
   435	that was recorded deliberately.
   436	
   437	Two fields change, and only by appending:
   438	
   439	| Field | Operation |
   440	|---|---|
   441	| `documents` | **APPEND** `"RULING-2026-08-25-C1-STAGE2-CUTOVER"` as a new final element. The two existing elements — `"C1-CHARTER"` and `"RULING-2026-08-24-C1-CHARTER-RATIFICATION"` — are retained in place, so the field ends with three ids. Dropping either while adding the third still satisfies the validator, which checks only that each listed id is known; §7.6 records the closure obligation. |
   442	| `scope` | **APPEND** §1.4's key run to the end of the existing string, preceded by a single space, with **every byte of the existing value preserved as a prefix of the new one**. Nothing in the existing text is reworded, resequenced, shortened or re-punctuated. |
   443	
   444	**The preservation requirement is stated as a prefix relation on purpose.** Quoting the current scope
   445	text here would create a second copy of trunk-owned authority inside a block document — the exact
   446	drift this plan refuses elsewhere — and a quoted copy goes stale the moment the owner corrects a word
   447	of it. The check that does not go stale is: *the value the field held before the edit is a prefix of
   448	the value it holds after, and the remainder is exactly the appended key run.* For orientation only,
   449	the existing value opens *"Ratifies the C1 charter text"* and closes *"Execution authority requires a
   450	further record."*; those are landmarks for the owner's eye, not a transcription.
   451	
   452	Every other field remains byte-for-byte unchanged: `block` retains the existing block id, while
   453	`ratified_by` and `ratified_at` retain the existing ratification metadata. SPEC 2 permits no field
   454	other than `documents` and `scope` to be added, removed or edited.
   455	
   456	## 2. Stage 2 intent contract
   457	
   458	**Owned invariant.** After Stage 2, `verter_semantic::resolver_core::ModuleResolverCore` is the sole
   459	production module resolver in the workspace, reached through one dependency direction
   460	(`verter_workspace → verter_semantic`), with no forwarding wrapper, alias, feature flag or dual path
   461	in any landed state.
   462	
   463	**Required outcomes.**
   464	
   465	| ID | Required |
   466	|---|---|
   467	| S2-R1 | `verter_workspace` depends on `verter_semantic`; `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains none of `verter_workspace`, `verter_session`, `verter_scheduler` or `verter_tsgo_api` on any target, and `verter_semantic` has no `verter_workspace` dependency, normal or dev. This is C1-AC-2's invariant as the charter states it — its production-closure bullet in the Owned-invariant list, and the `C1-AC-2` row of its acceptance matrix — not a narrower half of it. |
   468	| S2-R2 | The A5-DD1 upward exception row for `verter_semantic` is deleted, and the dependency-layer guard asserts both directions. |
   469	| S2-R3 | Every production caller resolves through `ModuleResolverCore`. |
   470	| S2-R4 | The workspace retry/replay driver satisfies all five F24 contracts (§5). |
   471	| S2-R5 | The converted dual-runner coverage (§6) passes against the final production driver on the final candidate. |
   472	| S2-R6 | `A6_META_COMPILE_40_COLD_RUST` and its two counters do not regress (§7.4). |
   473	
   474	**Forbidden outcomes.**
   475	
   476	| ID | Forbidden |
   477	|---|---|
   478	| S2-F1 | A landed state containing two production module resolvers, or a forwarding `ProjectResolver`/`NativeProjectResolver` wrapper or alias. |
   479	| S2-F2 | A committed both-edges Cargo state. |
   480	| S2-F3 | Code and dependency-guard flip landing in separate commits. |
   481	| S2-F4 | A landed state where any test asserting the retained coverage was deleted rather than converted. |
   482	| S2-F5 | Final evidence produced on a tree other than the final candidate — in particular, evidence from a harness that the same change then deletes. |
   483	| S2-F6 | A new fuse table, or reweighting/reinterpreting the A6 cell after measurement. |
   484	
   485	**Authority order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
   486	remains the sole query-time resolver, unchanged by the crate move. `ModuleResolverCore` is the module
   487	resolver; it is not a second type-resolution engine and gains no query-time resolution role.
   488	
   489	**Performance contribution.** Stage 2 is a relocation, not an optimisation: its contribution is
   490	**neutrality**. It must not introduce cross-crate call overhead beyond ordinary function-call cost —
   491	no new serialization, no heap round-trip at the crate seam, no added clone or `Arc` construction in
   492	`ResolverContext` construction, and no new allocation per fact in the warm-hit
   493	`validate_fact_signature` loop.
   494	
   495	**What this section claims.** Each row is a finite, checkable proposition derived from the ratified
   496	charter, stated as an outcome rather than a reference. **It does not claim any row is decided.**
   497	Which rows are decided and which are unmet is not restated here. **§7.6 owns that status, except
   498	S2-R6 and S2-F6, whose status is §7.4's; S2-F2 and S2-F3, whose status is §7.5's; and S2-F4's
   499	conversion half, whose status is §6.4's.**

   627	## 4. One atomic transition, and the compiler-repair fixpoint
   628	
   629	**Work order.**
   630	
   631	1. Establish the semantic-owned values, workspace projections, and workspace value re-exports (§3),
   632	   honouring §3's within-crate relocation precondition before step 6 removes the crate-root authority
   633	   re-exports. Which definitions that covers, and why the ordering binds, are §3's; naming them again
   634	   here is how two copies of one roster start to differ.
   635	2. Repoint the inert kernel so production `verter_semantic` names no `verter_workspace` type.
   636	3. Reverse both Cargo edges and flip the whole dependency-guard cluster **together** — code-first
   637	   leaves the guard too permissive, guard-first false-fails, so same-commit is the only correct
   638	   choice. The three edits are: remove `verter_semantic` from `ratified_upward_exceptions()`
   639	   (keeping `verter_diagnostics`, which has an independent reason); shrink `RATIFIED_ROOT_CRATES` to
   640	   `&["verter_diagnostics"]`; replace the semantic→workspace canary with a both-directions
   641	   assertion.
   642	4. §5.
   643	5. §2 (S2-R3).
   644	6. §3; §6.
   645	7. §7.
   646	
   647	**The compiler-repair fixpoint.** Intermediate rounds are working-tree iteration and are NOT
   648	evidence: no round is receipted, and the evidentiary claim is narrowed to the single unchanged
   649	post-squash run required by step 7. `cargo` does not check dependents of a crate that failed, so a single red run shows only
   650	the lowest failing layer — an observed property of this repository, recorded at
   651	`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A1/command-proofs/02-cargo-clippy.txt`, where a full-workspace
   652	invocation terminates at `error: could not compile verter_session (lib)` with `EXIT: 101` without
   653	reaching that crate's dependents. Therefore:
   654	
   655	1. Run the §7.1 and §7.3 commands, collecting diagnostics.
   656	2. Repoint what that round reports.
   657	3. Repeat until every §7.1 and §7.3 command is green on one unchanged tree.
   658	
   659	Errors surface in dependency order. **Termination is green across the §7.1 and §7.3 commands on the
   660	final candidate; that, and only that, is what the fixpoint claims.** It makes no static-universe
   661	claim, and no intermediate round claims anything.
   662	
   663	**What this section claims.** Each round reports actual unresolved references in the configurations
   664	executed, never an unexecuted command's selection. That narrowing is the whole of the claim; whether
   665	those executions were recorded and bound to the final tree is §7.6's.

   746	### 6.1 The PRESTART source roster

   749	claim a hand-written enumeration did not carry. The fix is to define the set by its SOURCE rather than
   750	to list it:

  1078	  invoke — if it exists only as a description that each consumer re-implements — then V12 cannot be
  1079	  discharged as written, and no amount of care inside C1 fixes that. Making it callable belongs to
  1080	  the maintainer / A6 lock authority together with the pin correction above, and this plan records it
  1081	  as a dependency rather than quietly reconstructing the protocol again.
  1082	- **Raw evidence never lands in the tree it measures.** The earlier form redirected stdout into
  1083	  the absent ledger-local destination `docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/C1/evidence/`, creating an
  1084	  untracked file inside the very checkout other receipts assert is clean. Writing measurement output
  1085	  into the subject of the measurement is self-defeating regardless of whether a `.gitignore` entry hides it.

  1088	benchmark process running; the memory ceiling free per the resource-ceiling policy; power and thermal
  1089	governor unchanged between baseline and candidate runs. A run that cannot assert quiescence is

  1092	### 7.5 Atomic-history obligations — RECORDED UNMET, and the landing-hygiene rule survives as a rule
  1093

  1095

  1097	|---|---|
  1098	| Exactly one commit lands on the landing basis (S2-F3) | **UNMET** as a plan-owned receipt. |

  1104	head that contains the squash.
  1105	
  1106	**Why a Git-reading check was not retained even though Git decides these propositions.** The
  1107	propositions are decidable, but the checks read revisions the caller names. Nothing bound
  1108	`--base` to the authorized baseline, so the family could only ever have established *relative* facts
  1109	about an arbitrary one-commit checkout — true statements about the wrong subject. Re-sourcing an
  1110	expected value from the Git object at a caller-supplied revision does not fix this; it relocates the
  1111	trust root without closing it. That was the defect in the last proposal to keep this family, and it
  1112	is why the family goes rather than shrinks.

  1114	### 7.6 How a claim acquires a receipt
  1115	
  1116	**There is no claim-to-receipt table in this ruling, and its absence is deliberate.** The previous
  1117	form was a hand-written map from claim to instrument. A text table can assert that an instrument
  1118	discharges a claim the instrument never established, and nothing in the mechanism prevents it —
  1119	which is precisely how a `--lib` selection came to be recorded as proving a guard that lives in an
  1120	integration target, and how a dependency-closure test came to be recorded as proving STAY ownership
  1121	and a MIRROR projection it cannot see.
  1122	
  1123	**A claim is discharged only by a witness that established it, and the witness names its own
  1124	claims.** Concretely:
  1125	
  1126	- **No digest-bound verifier is among this plan's witnesses (§10).** §1.5's and §7.5's obligations
  1127	  therefore have no emitting witness at all and are recorded unmet in the tables there. What this
  1128	  plan does hold emits its result directly: the canonical gate and the repository tests it selects
  1129	  either pass or fail, and there is no separate place to write down what they proved.
  1130	- A check that does not run, errors, or returns an indeterminate state emits **no** claim. Absence of
  1131	  a claim is visible in the receipt as an unmet obligation; it cannot be supplied from elsewhere.
  1132	- A claim with no emitting witness is **unmet**, and this plan says so rather than mapping it to the
  1133	  nearest plausible instrument.
  1134	
  1135	What follows are the final-tree obligations owned here. All have no witness in this plan and are
  1136	recorded as unmet rather than mapped to the nearest instrument.
  1137	
  1138	- **§3 STAY rows.** A dependency-closure test proves no edge crosses upward; it does not prove that a
  1139	  named definition still lives in the crate that is supposed to own it, nor that a duplicate neutral
  1140	  definition was not left behind. Discharging this needs a structural assertion about ownership —
  1141	  a repository test that names the owning module and fails if the definition moves or is duplicated.
  1142	  Until such a test exists in the repository, the STAY rows are an **intent record, not a proven
  1143	  claim**, and this ruling does not assert otherwise.
  1144	- **§3 MIRROR row.** The mirror needs a test that names both sides and asserts the projection; until
  1145	  it exists the row is likewise **intent, not proof**.
  1146	- **§3 MOVE roster.** Compilation proves the moved definitions exist *somewhere* the callers can
  1147	  reach; it does not prove each named definition landed in the crate §3 assigns it to, and no cited
  1148	  test asserts per-definition destination. A definition moved to the wrong owning crate compiles and
  1149	  passes every gate named here. Discharging it needs a structural ownership assertion — the same
  1150	  instrument §3's STAY rows need. Until one exists, the MOVE rows are **intent, not proof**.
  1151	- **§3 RETARGET roster.** Its only witness is the `raw_resolver_entry_points_are_private` compile-fail
  1152	  fixture, which the canonical gate does not select (§7.2), so nothing in this plan executes it.
  1153	  Until it is selected by something, the RETARGET rows are **intent, not proof**.
  1154	- **§3's DELETE roster IN FULL, and the no-forwarder obligation.** On the boundary §7.2 draws, the
  1155	  part compilation cannot carry is the whole of what this roster asserts: a repository compile-fail
  1156	  fixture exists for the eight resolver-authority public paths but is inert until the transition
  1157	  activates it, and even activated it establishes only that **those named public paths do not
  1158	  resolve** — never that a private copy, a renamed copy, or a copy in another module is gone. The
  1159	  roster is **intent, not proof**, in full.
  1160	- **Source absence for every MOVE definition, and the no-copy half of STAY (§3).** No sufficient
  1161	  instrument exists: destination reachability is not relocation while a source copy satisfies it, a
  1162	  path-named fixture sees only the paths it names, and the §7.2 dependency-closure guard cannot see a
  1163	  duplicate. Both halves are **unmet**, and no approximation of them appears anywhere in this plan.
  1164	
  1165	- **S2-R3 (§2): intent, not proof.**
  1166	- **S2-R5 and S2-F4 (§2, §6): intent, not proof.**
  1167	
  1168	- **Registration of the relocated C1-AC-3 witness.** §7.2 names
  1169	  `project_semantic_dispatch_invariants` in its post-transition home. Selection requires that the
  1170	  relocated suite be registered by its new parent. Nothing establishes that registration. **UNMET.**
  1171	- **Registration of the §5 `resolution_driver_tests` module.** The planned module must be declared
  1172	  by its parent to enter the lib test target. Nothing establishes that registration. **UNMET.**
  1173	- **That the §7.1 gates and the §7.3 command were run and passed.** This plan records what they are
  1174	  required to establish, and nothing observes that any of them was executed or what it returned.
  1175	  **UNMET** — the same gap as the final-tree binding row below, and the reason that row bounds every
  1176	  §7 result.
  1177	- **RETARGET (§3): UNMET.**
  1178

  1180	restates after its instrument is removed is exactly the work that reaches trunk unowned:
  1181	
  1182	- **Authorization-scope exactness** — that the scope carries precisely the required key set, with no

  1221	## 8. Abort procedure and return-to-known-good
  1222	
  1223	**This section carries a recoverability claim, not a completeness claim.** It does not assert what
  1224	has been found or what exists; it asserts that intermediate work stays unlanded, and it prescribes
  1225	the procedure for returning to `c1-stage2-prestart`. **That recovery is CONDITIONAL on the return
  1226	point.** See §1.5. Where its obligations do not hold, the procedure below has nothing correct to
  1227	return to.
  1228	
  1229	**Abort procedure.** Stop editing; do not commit; do not push; `git reset --hard c1-stage2-prestart`
  1230	and discard the working tree. Nothing landed, so nothing is reverted and no trunk state is touched.
  1231	Record the trigger and the evidence before any retry.

  1234	with `git tag -d c1-stage2-prestart`; a tag that already exists at retry means the previous abort did
  1235	not complete, which is a state worth failing on rather than overwriting.

   504

   627	## 4. One atomic transition, and the compiler-repair fixpoint
   628	
   629	**Work order.**
   630	
   631	1. Establish the semantic-owned values, workspace projections, and workspace value re-exports (§3),
   632	   honouring §3's within-crate relocation precondition before step 6 removes the crate-root authority
   633	   re-exports. Which definitions that covers, and why the ordering binds, are §3's; naming them again
   634	   here is how two copies of one roster start to differ.
   635	2. Repoint the inert kernel so production `verter_semantic` names no `verter_workspace` type.
   636	3. Reverse both Cargo edges and flip the whole dependency-guard cluster **together** — code-first
   637	   leaves the guard too permissive, guard-first false-fails, so same-commit is the only correct
   638	   choice. The three edits are: remove `verter_semantic` from `ratified_upward_exceptions()`
   639	   (keeping `verter_diagnostics`, which has an independent reason); shrink `RATIFIED_ROOT_CRATES` to
   640	   `&["verter_diagnostics"]`; replace the semantic→workspace canary with a both-directions
   641	   assertion.
   642	4. §5.
   643	5. §2 (S2-R3).
   644	6. §3; §6.
   645	7. §7.
   646	
   647	**The compiler-repair fixpoint.** Intermediate rounds are working-tree iteration and are NOT
   648	evidence: no round is receipted, and the evidentiary claim is narrowed to the single unchanged
   649	post-squash run required by step 7. `cargo` does not check dependents of a crate that failed, so a single red run shows only
   650	the lowest failing layer — an observed property of this repository, recorded at
   651	`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A1/command-proofs/02-cargo-clippy.txt`, where a full-workspace
   652	invocation terminates at `error: could not compile verter_session (lib)` with `EXIT: 101` without
   653	reaching that crate's dependents. Therefore:
   654	
   655	1. Run the §7.1 and §7.3 commands, collecting diagnostics.
   656	2. Repoint what that round reports.
   657	3. Repeat until every §7.1 and §7.3 command is green on one unchanged tree.
   658	
   659	Errors surface in dependency order. **Termination is green across the §7.1 and §7.3 commands on the
   660	final candidate; that, and only that, is what the fixpoint claims.** It makes no static-universe
   661	claim, and no intermediate round claims anything.
   662	
   663	**What this section claims.** Each round reports actual unresolved references in the configurations
   664	executed, never an unexecuted command's selection. That narrowing is the whole of the claim; whether
   665	those executions were recorded and bound to the final tree is §7.6's.

   811	
   812	Named so a reviewer can check the converted suite without re-deriving intent: the four core surfaces
   813	(`resolve_attempt`, `resolve_for_project_attempt`, `preferred_specifier_candidates`,
   814	`project_exact_result`); every resolution branch — relative, absolute for an owned importer,

   816	cycle proven to terminate, `#imports`, `node_modules` exports-with-conditions and the array form,

   818	dangling project reference falling through without panicking, and the full-chain miss; precedence
   819	competition (alias over `paths` over `baseUrl`); carrier/provider projection end to end; ordered
   820	consumed selectors and `NeedInputs` wave counts; the complete `ResolveResult` DTO comparison, not

   826	identified as the `#[test]` roster of a named Git object rather than a hand-written list — an

   828	what follows from that. The converted tests are REQUIRED to run against the production entry point on
