   832	### 6.4 The conversion mapping — RECORDED UNMET, with the destination and rule still normative
   833	
   834	**Destination.** All converted cases land in the planned, presently absent
   835	`crates/verter_workspace/src/resolution_conversion_tests.rs` — a sibling `*_tests.rs` unit-test
   836	module of the `verter_workspace` lib target, the crate that owns the production driver. It adds no
   837	integration-test binary, per the anti-binary-growth layout rule. **The module must be declared by its
   838	parent**, or it compiles into nothing and the canonical gate never selects it; an orphan file in the
   839	tree is not a converted test.
   840	
   841	**Mapping rule.** Each case keeps its function name; only its home and its oracle change. The mapping
   842	is therefore the identity on names, which makes it checkable without a 24-row correspondence table
   843	and leaves nothing to interpretation. Both destination and rule remain normative.
   844	
   845	**The generator that checked the mapping is deleted, and the mapping obligation is UNMET.** V20 read
   846	both blobs from Git — the right sources — and still could not decide its proposition, because the
   847	name extractor was a line-oriented regex over source text. It counted textual patterns, not test
   848	cases: one genuine `#[test]` plus twenty-three inside a `/* */` block comment yields twenty-four
   849	names, twenty-four of them distinct, satisfying the check while a single real case exists. That
   850	defect survived three successive repairs in the same shape — a subset relation, then a bare count,
   851	then a distinct count — each closing the previous counterexample and leaving the class open. A text
   852	scanner cannot decide what is a compiled test; only the compiler and the runner can, and the runner
   853	family was already deleted as unauthenticable (below).
   854	
   855	| Obligation | Status |
   856	|---|---|
   857	| No converted case name was dropped (part of S2-F4) | **UNMET.** |
   858	| The PRESTART roster is exactly the documented 24 cases | **UNMET** — the stronger identity claim was never established, only approximated. |
   859	| The converted module is registered and therefore selected by the canonical gate | **UNMET** — an unreferenced file satisfies any read of its bytes. |
   860	| The conversion preserved what each case tested | **UNMET** — no instrument here reads a case body. |
   861	| Each of the 24 named cases executed | **UNMET** — see the runner note below. |
   862	| The dual-runner harness was green BEFORE its legacy-side runners were deleted, and in that order (§6) | **UNMET.** Nothing observes the harness's result, and nothing observes that the deletion followed it rather than preceded it. |
   863	
   864	**The runner (V21) was deleted first, and for a different reason worth keeping distinct.** It
   865	asserted that the converted cases actually executed. `cargo` resolves through `PATH`, which the
   866	invoker owns, so asking that binary to identify itself authenticated nothing — a substituted binary
   867	answers the probe and prints a convincing summary having run no tests. Its per-case enumeration
   868	parsed the shared human output stream, which `NEXTEST_SUCCESS_OUTPUT=immediate` lets a single passing
   869	test write arbitrary result lines into, and its pattern was independently inverted against reality:
   870	it required two tokens after the duration where real output carries three
   871	(`PASS [ 0.059s] (10/94) <binary> <name>`), so it rejected genuine lines and accepted fabricated
   872	ones — the signature of a check that had only ever been read, never executed against real output. A
   873	process cannot authenticate a subprocess in an environment its caller controls.
   874	
   875	**Where these obligations should end up.** Registration, selection and the surviving-coverage
   876	properties are durable facts about the final tree, so they belong in ordinary repository tests the
   877	canonical gate selects (§7.2). Until such tests exist, the rows above stand as unmet and this ruling
   878	claims nothing further.

   880	## 7. Exact-candidate evidence manifest
   881	
   882	All evidence is produced on **one final candidate tree** — `FINAL_SHA` / `FINAL_TREE`, after every
   883	deletion in §3 and §6 and after the squash. Passing a harness and then deleting that harness is not
   884	proof about the final candidate (S2-F5). This is a list of **obligations with exact procedures**, not
   885	a coverage claim and not a record of execution: it states that these named executions are REQUIRED to
   886	run and pass on this tree. Whether they did, and whether the tree they ran on was the final candidate
   887	unchanged, is §7.6's.

   889	Every result is required to record: the exact command; selected targets; the §7.0 tool identity block;
   890	`FINAL_SHA`; `FINAL_TREE`; exit status; the test enumeration the runner reported; and artifacts.

   895	the command set in §7.1–§7.3. **It does not claim to enumerate every executable reachable
   896	during a build**, and it is not falsified by naming one it omits — a shell's transitive utilities

   940

   944	of a repository test proves nothing the repository does not already prove, and creates a second
   945	universe whose completeness has to be argued separately.
   946	
   947	| Invariant | Where it lives | Selected by |
   948	|---|---|---|
   949	| The production-layer firewall and equality-pinned upward-exception set over normal and build edges — the production-closure portion of S2-R1, excluding its dev-edge and positive replacement-edge requirements | `verter_identity` — `workspace_dependency_layers::workspace_production_closures_never_cross_upward_except_the_recorded_exception` | V1 |
   950	| the exception edges' target conditions, so a target-gated resolve cannot silently shrink the recorded reach | `verter_identity` — `workspace_dependency_layers::the_ratified_exception_records_its_target_condition_precisely` | V1 |
   951	| Closure-walk non-vacuity: `verter_session` reaches the five named deep dependencies, and the pre-cutover `verter_semantic` closure reaches `verter_workspace` | `verter_identity` — `workspace_dependency_layers::closure_walk_is_non_vacuous_for_known_deep_reaches` | V1 |
   952	| authority uniqueness after the move (C1-AC-3) | `verter_semantic` — `project_semantic_dispatch_invariants`, relocated with the module it tests as C1-AC-3 requires (it is in `verter_session` until the transition moves it) | see §7.6 |

   955	layered production graph from `cargo metadata --all-features`, without `--filter-platform`, so every
   956	target-gated edge is unioned; that union is what licenses "on every target", and it is a property of
   957	the invocation rather than of the crate. It then treats **both** recorded exception roots identically:
   958	`RATIFIED_ROOT_CRATES` holds `verter_semantic` **and** `verter_diagnostics`, and
   959	`ratified_upward_exceptions()` maps each to the same set `{verter_workspace, verter_scheduler,
   960	verter_tsgo_api}` — both in
   961	`crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs`. The map is equality-pinned rather
   962	than subset-checked, so once `verter_semantic`'s entry is deleted its expected upward set is empty and
   963	any surviving member fails. `verter_diagnostics` keeps its entry (§4 step 3) and is untouched by this transition.
   964

   966	entry left in place while the edges are gone makes the expected set the three crates and the observed
   967	set empty, and the assertion fails. It does not follow that the pin detects every way the row could be
   968	wrong — an entry left in place beside edges left in place passes it, which is the state before the
   969	transition and not one this row distinguishes.

   975	  See §3 for the separate dev-dependency disposition.
   976	- **It does not by itself assert the positive `verter_workspace → verter_semantic` edge**, so it does
   977	  not carry "both directions" alone. A closure reaching nothing upward is equally consistent with the
   978	  two crates wired the new way and with their not being wired at all. The pair is named today only by

   983	canonical gate excludes the entire `cases::g_compile::compile_fail::` prefix, so a fixture placed
   984	there is never executed by the gate and cannot be cited as a repository-owned witness. That is the

   989	neither is fixable by rewriting the pattern:
   990	
   991	- **It is fail-open.** `grep` exits non-zero both when it matches nothing and when it fails to

   999	narrower than the obligation.** This subsection owns where that boundary falls; §7.6 owns what the
  1000	remainder's status is.

  1092	### 7.5 Atomic-history obligations — RECORDED UNMET, and the landing-hygiene rule survives as a rule
  1093	
  1094	The four obligations below have no plan-owned instrument (§10). They are recorded, not discharged:
  1095	
  1096	| Obligation | Status |
  1097	|---|---|
  1098	| Exactly one commit lands on the landing basis (S2-F3) | **UNMET** as a plan-owned receipt. |
  1099	| Linear fast-forward, one parent, and that parent is the landing basis | **UNMET** as a plan-owned receipt. |
  1100	| Edge, guard, code and deletions land in one commit, with a deletion not satisfiable by a modification (S2-F2, S2-F3) | **UNMET** as a plan-owned receipt. |

  1102	
  1103	The landing parent is the trunk commit onto which the squash lands. It is not the working-branch
  1104	head that contains the squash.
  1105	
  1106	**Why a Git-reading check was not retained even though Git decides these propositions.** The
  1107	propositions are decidable, but the checks read revisions the caller names. Nothing bound
  1108	`--base` to the authorized baseline, so the family could only ever have established *relative* facts
  1109	about an arbitrary one-commit checkout — true statements about the wrong subject. Re-sourcing an
  1110	expected value from the Git object at a caller-supplied revision does not fix this; it relocates the
  1111	trust root without closing it. That was the defect in the last proposal to keep this family, and it
  1112	is why the family goes rather than shrinks.
  1113	
  1114	### 7.6 How a claim acquires a receipt
  1115	
  1116	**There is no claim-to-receipt table in this ruling, and its absence is deliberate.** The previous
  1117	form was a hand-written map from claim to instrument. A text table can assert that an instrument
  1118	discharges a claim the instrument never established, and nothing in the mechanism prevents it —
  1119	which is precisely how a `--lib` selection came to be recorded as proving a guard that lives in an
  1120	integration target, and how a dependency-closure test came to be recorded as proving STAY ownership
  1121	and a MIRROR projection it cannot see.
  1122	
  1123	**A claim is discharged only by a witness that established it, and the witness names its own
  1124	claims.** Concretely:
  1125	
  1126	- **No digest-bound verifier is among this plan's witnesses (§10).** §1.5's and §7.5's obligations
  1127	  therefore have no emitting witness at all and are recorded unmet in the tables there. What this
  1128	  plan does hold emits its result directly: the canonical gate and the repository tests it selects
  1129	  either pass or fail, and there is no separate place to write down what they proved.
  1130	- A check that does not run, errors, or returns an indeterminate state emits **no** claim. Absence of
  1131	  a claim is visible in the receipt as an unmet obligation; it cannot be supplied from elsewhere.
  1132	- A claim with no emitting witness is **unmet**, and this plan says so rather than mapping it to the
  1133	  nearest plausible instrument.
  1134	
  1135	What follows are the final-tree obligations owned here. All have no witness in this plan and are
  1136	recorded as unmet rather than mapped to the nearest instrument.
  1137	
  1138	- **§3 STAY rows.** A dependency-closure test proves no edge crosses upward; it does not prove that a
  1139	  named definition still lives in the crate that is supposed to own it, nor that a duplicate neutral
  1140	  definition was not left behind. Discharging this needs a structural assertion about ownership —
  1141	  a repository test that names the owning module and fails if the definition moves or is duplicated.
  1142	  Until such a test exists in the repository, the STAY rows are an **intent record, not a proven
  1143	  claim**, and this ruling does not assert otherwise.
  1144	- **§3 MIRROR row.** The mirror needs a test that names both sides and asserts the projection; until
  1145	  it exists the row is likewise **intent, not proof**.

     1	# Verter Architecture Convergence Program — Revision 11
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative dependency-ordered implementation authority.  
     4	**Durable authority:** `architecture.md`, contracts, and accepted ADRs.  
     5	**Proof authority:** `verification.md`.  
     6	**Governance authority:** `governance.md`.  
     7	**Machine-readable predecessor authority:** `program-dag.toml`.
     8	
     9	# 1. Program law
    10	
    11	The program is a DAG of bounded clean cutovers. A block may start when every predecessor has its required accepted state and the validated `program-state.toml` marks it `READY`/`BLOCK_READY`. A dependent upper layer may instead perform contingent `READY`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`REVIEW` work only when each unaccepted predecessor is a lower layer in the same validated immutable stack snapshot. It cannot become `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED` or `ACCEPTED` until those predecessors are formally satisfied and the upper candidate is restacked/revalidated on the accepted base. Except for the explicit `D1` private checkpoint, accepted block state means the predecessor is integrated on the intended lineage. `D1` is reviewed on the bounded `D2` integration branch and is never merged/released independently; `D2` is the atomic landing unit. Parallel work is legal only when cutover closures, writable worktrees, and shared generated/owner surfaces are disjoint or explicitly serialized.
    12	
    13	A pull-request stack is transport only. Bounded stack windows may linearize one short dependency path for review, but they do not create semantic predecessor authority. A program-wide mega-stack is prohibited. Atomic private layers land only through their final atomic candidate.
    14	
    15	Before `A6`, only Gate 0 work is legal. `A2C` is not executable. `A3` may change behavior solely to retract a non-G10 A2-catalogued wrong-complete result through the existing typed degradation/non-admission rails; it has no structural-completion or G10 obligation. Exact structural completion and G10 discrimination remain debt `FR-D8`, owned by D6. No Gate 0 block may create a syntax-only completion detector, second graph/classifier, or false refusal of a checker-correct clean/warm result.

    19	```text
    20	A0–A6  implementation lock
    21	   ↓
    22	B      deterministic direct compiler and shared syntax ownership
    23	   ├─────────────┐

    25	C semantic core  J CSS convergence (bounded parallel after shared identities)

    42	# 3. Universal block admission
    43	
    44	A non-local block is `BLOCK_READY` only when:
    45	
    46	- the `A6` Implementation Lock Record is accepted;

    57	
    58	## 3.1 Program-wide timing law
    59	
    60	Every block classifies a timing-sensitive mechanism as **owned causal progress**, **semantic time**, **external liveness**, or **performance measurement**, using `architecture.md` §1.6. Internal correctness cannot use fixed sleeps, repeated `yield_now`, atomic/refcount polling, counters unchanged for a duration, elapsed-time assertions, global-idle heuristics, or time-substituting retry loops. External polling is admitted only with a written proof that no event, receipt, OS primitive, or callback exists and with one real outer watchdog.
    61	
    62	No block may introduce a global clock trait, global event bus, universal workspace-generation cache key, global idle/readiness service, global duration registry, production-state-machine event log, or generic coordinator duplicating G2's `FlightCell`.
    63	
    64	This four-part taxonomy binds every DAG block that owns a timing-sensitive surface, including the TypeScript content-mapper train (`TCM0`–`TCM4`). TCM0 is lock-only and TCM1 is mapping-product geometry; neither owns a live coalescer, queue, or protocol-admission surface, and they receive no extra concurrency criteria. TCM2's JSON-RPC/stdio mapper boundary is external liveness (protocol completion plus one independent real monotonic watchdog) and TCM2 is the sole owner of mapper-protocol admission inside cancellation and one absolute deadline; G3 may supply a reusable bounded-admission primitive and must not implement that path. TCM3's snapshot-bound oracle is owned causal progress; its bounded concurrent queries consume G2 `FlightCell` and must not ship a second generic coordinator. TCM4's atomic activation is owned causal progress of the cutover; the Project-Bound External-TS rule remains in force and TCM4's performance obligation is not waived. Same-key coalescers are inventoried BY NAME in `charters/K3.md` and each named cell is dispositioned with its final owner; an unnamed cell is NOT a close failure and no search is required to prove absence (`rulings/MAINTAINER-RULING-COALESCER-CLOSURE-IS-NAMED-DISPOSITION.md`: K3 closes when everything named is dispositioned, and we do not keep testing for unnamed cells).     67	
    68	`block/deterministic-tests` is a prerequisite correction branch, not a new DAG block and not the G/H runtime redesign. It is limited to:
    69	
    70	- deterministic test infrastructure;
    71	- exact timer tests;
    72	- direct lost-wake and lifecycle corrections discovered while removing timing assumptions;
    73	- production/test topology alignment needed to test those mechanisms;
    74	- removal of newly added or directly touched polling and elapsed-time correctness checks.

    76	It must not add a permanent readiness coordinator or generic flight system. Those responsibilities remain G2/G3/G5/H2/H3. A narrow urgent latency bridge may land before those blocks only when all seven conditions hold:

    86	A bridge is not approved merely to improve current benchmark results. Public `LspConfig` switches `suppress_edit_debounced_import_publication` and `suppress_sync_coordinator_signal` are not timing architecture; they create a non-production topology and must not land as production configuration. If they exist on the branch, they name H3 as deletion owner before landing; K3 verifies residual deletion. Gate-performance work stays a separate, independently measurable landing unit; deterministic correctness cannot depend on that experiment landing. Its evidence includes single-gate idle and concurrent-gate contention measurements on the target M3/24GB machine; p50/p95/p99 wall time per lane; CPU, memory, queue/blocked time, and cache misses where available; timeout/retry/flake rate; critical-path attribution; per-lane stall detection; and narrow resource classes instead of unnecessarily broad serialization.    886	notes = "Created by the maintainer's beta.4 regression-intake directive to own Findings B and C, both regressions against published beta.3 and both beta.4 blockers. THE DECISIVE RULING IS THAT THESE ARE TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS, NOT ONE: the in-repo investigation reproduced a SILENT degrade to Unknown(MissingOutput) upstream of the raise layer, while the external benchmark observed a HARD UnraisableSource error at exposed[].type. Closing only the reproduced one would have left a release blocker armed and shipping, so the hard-error fixture is an ADDITIONAL acceptance condition and CM1 is not complete until both are closed with their own reproducing tests. Finding B root cause: eval_env.rs component_meta_binding_type_entries gated only on PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation.classification and ignored signatures, so a defineExpose'd function declaration or a const initialized by a call such as ref or computed - typed OR untyped - was never offered to macro-type expansion. Repair: structurally admit demanded visible value bindings, fix the call-binding owner/preparation handoff, and preserve Failed through publication. Finding C root cause: the macro runtime-constructor path recognized runtime prop constructors but wrote DISPLAY TEXT only, never a semantic source, while the sibling Options-API path mapped constructor identity to a real Primitive fact - which is why optionality survived while the primitive type vanished. Repair: the Options path's closed primitive semantics became the shared analyzer model; the runtime-macro path was the anomaly, and semantics are never derived from display text or at the output seam. Both defects reproduce identically across sequential, warm, concurrent and batch invocation, which rules out view/concurrency causes - the directive's request-view hypothesis was not what the evidence showed. Ruled fixable under the CURRENT architecture (Path A), so no C1 rework is required; C1 gains CM1 as a predecessor while RETAINING A6, B1 and B2 so it must preserve the corrected behaviour and migrate the new tests. Acceptance uses Verter's intended canonical type output from product contracts and beta.3 behaviour, never the benchmark's permissive string|String comparison. The strict output error remains PREFERABLE to an invented type: no unknown substitution, no omitted exposed entries, no swallowed failures, no stale graph state, no bypassed request-view isolation. LANDED SLICES ON TRUNK (dispatch authorization only - NOT ledger-ACCEPTED): predecessors BV1/BS1 were both already ACCEPTED at dispatch (2026-08-20), so CM1 was legitimately authorised (authority-registry.toml, block=CM1). CM1's work reached trunk as THREE real commits across two days, not one and not two: 0e5177931 (2026-08-22, Finding B - aliased-binding identity resolution, the exhaustive PreparedValueDecl admission gate, Failed-vs-Absent preservation, and the Present->UnraisableSource producer repair), 13eafb2ab (2026-08-22, Finding C - the owner-aware RootBindingIndex replacing the deleted, structurally-unsound shadow scanner, shared by the Options and macro runtime-constructor paths), and 571ad4dd1 (2026-08-23, the corrective follow-on - owner-keyed binding resolution through admission to the join with a fail-closed residual double match, macro-indexed slot identity, and spec-direct eval classification for every Reference-preserving wrapper). Neither corresponds to implementation_candidate_sha (block/cm1's tip 47e8515): 0e5177931 is a divergent squash of block/cm1's own corrected end state (that branch's internal revert a7bf8c696 already dropped the unsound shadow scanner before its own tip), and 13eafb2ab is an entirely separate lineage block/cm1 never contained - see evidence/CM1/landing-equivalence.md for the full ancestry proof. implementation_candidate_sha/implementation_ref are retained as the historical WIP-dispatch record only, per the field's documented meaning once a block leaves IN_PROGRESS; they are NOT CM1's landed identity. FOLLOW-ON DEFERRALS NOW CLOSED: 571ad4dd1 closed the three crates/ gaps the genuine BLOCK review recorded (evidence/CM1/2026-08-22-acceptance-repair.md) - the D3 Local+Absent arm now fails closed with SemanticSourceFailure::UnrepresentableRequiredMemberValue instead of falling through to the caller's unannotated default; D1 nullable-constructor-array adoption was verified against vendored @vue/runtime-core (getType(null) returns the string null; assertType accepts only value === null) rather than guessed; and the eval-classification bug was fixed conservatively, poisoning skipped ONLY for a provably fresh, unmutated, unredeclared non-global function binding, with alias/reassignment/redeclaration/optional-call/comma-expression tests each asserting the direction it must not drift toward. The compat regression that same review recorded (packages/component-meta/test/compat-gaps.test.ts asserting the pre-repair unknown | undefined value for the exact shape Finding C targets) is likewise resolved - that test now asserts string | undefined. evidence/CM1/binding-index-deferrals.md records the closures. CHARTER-COMPLETION CANDIDATE (this row's current base_sha/candidate_sha): the three charter exits that survived 571ad4dd1 are closed by this candidate. (1) Charter item 4 (CM1.md:110) required a producer-owned typed runtime-constructor fact/enum; constructor identity was still a raw Arc<str> spelling on ConstructorBindingEntry, folded by a string match at component_meta.rs's primitive_of and mapped a second time by macros.rs's constructor_to_ts_type. Both string switches are DELETED. verter_type_expr::RuntimeConstructorIdentity is a closed enum minted ONCE at the analyzer's extraction boundary (root_binding_index::resolve_constructor_binding classifies the identifier's own source text; macros::resolve_runtime_constructor_array mints NullLiteral for the literal element and Unclassifiable for a non-identifier position) and matched EXHAUSTIVELY downstream through identity.primitive() / identity.display_ts_type() / identity.spelling(). ConstructorBindingEntry no longer carries a spelling field at all, so a downstream re-classification is a compile error, not a review catch - the structural confinement the charter's Structural confinement section requires (a closed enum matched exhaustively, never a name-keyed source scanner). (2) Charter item 7 / the acceptance matrix (CM1.md:165) required the literal cross of runtime forms, invocation modes and native/compat surfaces at the PUBLIC boundary; coverage was strong at analyzer/fold level but the public half was narrow. crates/verter_session/tests/cases/runtime_constructor_matrix.rs now drives every DEMANDED runtime form (shorthand, expanded, required, optional, with-default, constructor array, nullable) and every demanded constructor kind (String/Number/Boolean positive; module-owned and imported custom classes as negative controls that must not be folded). Three authored-type forms are EXCLUDED from the demanded set by ratified rulings and carried as ignored discriminating captures instead - PropType<T>, a script-setup-local class, and the mixed runtime + type-declared form - so this row no longer claims the matrix drives them or uses PropType<T> as a control through BOTH the macro and Options-API extraction paths, under cold, warm, sequential, concurrent, batch and overlay/base invocation, asserting both per-cell exactness and cross-mode identity. packages/component-meta/test/runtime-constructor-matrix.test.ts mirrors the same fixtures on the compat surface. (3) The Present->UnraisableSource fixture asserted by panic-message style rather than the exact error variant; exposed_binding_regression.rs's fixture now matches the Result explicitly and asserts the exact ComponentMetaOutputLane::Exposed / ComponentMetaOutputFailure::UnraisableSource pair on the failure arm, separating the pre-repair defect from a different typed failure and from the forbidden Ok(None) swallow. LEDGER IDENTITY CORRECTION: base_sha/candidate_sha previously declared eadec2dc0..13eafb2ab as if it were a CM1-only delta. It is not: that range spans eight commits and 3,839 changed paths, with six unrelated Svelte-oracle, LSP, gate, harness and CSS commits sitting between CM1's own two 2026-08-22 commits, and it omitted 571ad4dd1 entirely. That mis-modelled range - not any CM1 content disagreement - is what produced the validator's CM1 landing-order replay conflict: a read-only three-way over the declared range reports conflicting paths whose intersection with the union of paths 0e5177931, 13eafb2ab and 571ad4dd1 actually changed is EMPTY, exactly the failure mode scripts/validate-program-state.mjs's own design comment describes for a declared base that predates unrelated intervening work. The orchestrator has since advanced it, so that residual no longer stands and this row no longer claims it does. Deliberately stated WITHOUT quoting either sha: the pin is orchestrator-owned and advances by design, so prose naming its value goes stale on the next advance - as this sentence itself did once, within an hour of being written. Replaying this candidate's delta onto the LIVE trunk tip is clean (git merge-tree --write-tree exit 0, no conflicted paths); replaying it onto the stale-pin cumulative is not. Advancing that pin is a program-level edit whose blast radius is every active block - doing so surfaces a separate J1 replay conflict - so it is left to the program orchestrator rather than taken here. REVIEW STATE: the three mandates remain BLOCKING. The single genuine acceptance review ever dispatched (against 13eafb2ab, under the BV2/B5/J1/CM1 single-lane waiver ratified by MAINTAINER-RULING-2026-08-22-BV2-B5-J1.md) returned BLOCK; that is a fact and is never relabelled PASS. CM1 stays REVIEW until all three mandates PASS against the exact candidate_sha above and the maintainer records the decision."

     1	# C3 — Project-aware Vue macro projection
     2	
     3	**Status:** PROPOSED amendment / LOCKED. **Predecessor:** C2.
     4	
     5	C3 retains sole ownership of project-aware imported Vue macro projection. It fulfils
     6	the closed typed project-information demands accepted in BV1 using the canonical
     7	project/type substrate. It cannot reinterpret framework options, replace Vue semantic
     8	analysis/codegen, invoke the official compiler, or introduce open-ended fact bags.
     9	
    10	## Closed BV1→C3 demand protocol
    11	
    12	Every demand carries the exact prepared-root `SourceIdentity`, macro
    13	`syntax_index`, closed macro role, closed product lane, typed subject identity,
    14	`TypeScriptSemanticProfileId`, and `ProjectionPlanToken`. A subject is the closed
    15	`TypedSubject { position, locator, lexical_owner }`, where `position` is
    16	exactly `TypeArgument`, `locator` is the content-free
    17	`MacroPayloadLocator` validated against the prepared-root identity, and
    18	`lexical_owner` is the exact `TopLevelOwnerId`. C3 lowers that locator through the
    19	canonical retained-snapshot service to owned `TypeExpr` typed IR; the demand never
    20	contains source text, an OXC/AST handle, a resolver callback, or a raw semantic query.
    21	
    22	The demand vocabulary has exactly one variant: `MacroPayload { role, subject, lane }`,
    23	where `role` is `Props`, `Emits`, `Model`, `Slots`, `Expose`, or `Options`. `Props`,
    24	`Emits`, and `Model` admit `RuntimeBindingNames`, `RuntimeConstructors`, `PublicApi`,
    25	`Tsc`, and `Declaration`; `Slots`, `Expose`, and `Options` admit only the three
    26	type-product lanes. When typed `defineProps` is wrapped by `withDefaults`, its demand
    27	still names only the inner props type argument. BV1 retains the wrapping syntax,
    28	association, and defaults application; none of them enters C3 demand identity.
    29	
    30	This is the typed-IR macro shape retained from `CLAUDE.md`: C3 resolves one typed
    31	subject through the single five-mode project dispatch and then applies a thin
    32	role-specific normalizer. There is no macro-specific resolver, eager unrelated-import
    33	walk, text reparse, or compiler-local fallback. Runtime-form object/array arguments,
    34	the `withDefaults` object and its eligibility/merge semantics, and all other
    35	source-local macro syntax remain parser/BV1-owned. They never lower to `TypeExpr`,
    36	enter a C3 demand, or get merged by C3.
    37	
    38	Each variant has one corresponding success payload:
    39	
    40	- `RuntimeBindingNames` returns `MacroRuntimeBindingProjection`;
    41	- `RuntimeConstructors` returns `MacroRuntimeProjection` with normalized
    42	  props/emits/model shapes and typed member degradation;
    43	- `PublicApi`, `Tsc`, and `Declaration` return `MacroTypeProductProjection` for the
    44	  named product.
    45	
    46	Every payload is wrapped in the closed result envelope

    49	exactly `MissingImport`, `MissingExport`, `MissingDeclaration`, or

    51	`InputBasisMismatch`, `DependencyFingerprintMismatch`,
    52	`SemanticProfileMismatch`, or `ProjectionPlanMismatch`. `ErrorReason` is exactly
    53	`UnsupportedTypeShape`, `BudgetExceeded`, `Recursion`, `Cancelled`, or
    54	`InternalFailure`. Every arm repeats the demand identity; success additionally
    55	carries the sorted unique dependency identities and the exact semantic profile/input
    56	basis that produced it.
    57	
    58	Demand identity is the deterministic tuple of every common field above plus the

    61	(`RuntimeBindingNames`, `RuntimeConstructors`, `PublicApi`, `Tsc`, `Declaration`).

    63	planned identity in that order. Missing, extra, duplicate, or reordered results, or
    64	any token/profile/root mismatch, reject the entire facts batch before codegen.
    65	
    66	BV1 converts an omitted result or any top-level `NotFound`, `Stale`, or `Error` arm

    68	anchor and publishes no artifact. A `Success` may carry only the explicitly typed

     1	# F1 — One committed input and coherent snapshot authority
     2	
     3	**Status:** LOCKED — contains binding acceptance criteria from the ratified timing directive; this charter is not separately authorized or dispatched. See the [landed timing ruling](../rulings/ARCHITECT-RULING-2026-08-23-TIMING-ARCHITECTURE.md).  
     4	**Class:** Foundational.  
     5	**Predecessors:** `A6`, `B6`, `C4`, `D2`.
     6	
     7	## Objective
     8	
     9	Converge committed sources, overlays, project topology, and configuration into one coherently captured authority, with exact typed revision dimensions for later facts and flights.
    10	
    11	## Acceptance criteria
    12	
    13	- One immutable capture provides the exact document revision, relevant source-root/project revision, and configuration/resolver epoch.
    14	- The capture contract has typed seams for a producer-owned provider/program-applied generation and a dependency read-set/stamp; F1 does not infer either from elapsed time or global idleness.
    15	- `EngineRevision` orders commits and captures snapshots only. It is not a universal invalidation value, cache key, readiness receipt, or substitute for any exact dimension.
    16	- An unrelated edit does not change an unrelated fact's basis and does not invalidate that fact.
    17	- Ordered document mutation, coherent before/after snapshots, short write critical sections, and parse/compile/provider work outside the write critical section remain mandatory.
    18	
    19	## Proof
    20	
    21	Discriminating capture tests cross document, project/source-root, configuration/resolver, and unrelated-edit changes. Each test proves the affected dimension advances and unaffected dimensions remain reusable. A global-generation-only implementation fails this charter.
    22	
    23	## Non-scope
    24	
    25	F1 does not implement provider readiness, a generic flight system, a global clock, or a universal workspace-generation cache key. F2 composes exact observation bases; H2 mints provider-applied receipts.

     1	# Roles, communication and state
     2	
     3	## Program orchestrator — thin scheduler and landing coordinator
     4	
     5	Owns the DAG, sequencing, dependencies, capacity and landing order. Spawns and steers block
     6	orchestrators and the landing agent — nothing else — and is the single landing authority.
     7	
     8	Never implements, runs a review-fix cycle, manages implementers or reviewers, or ingests raw worker
     9	logs, traces or review reports — it reads compact receipts only. Reacts to milestone, blocker,
    10	decision and completion events rather than polling. Keeps only unblocked trains active; checkpoints
    11	or shuts down finished teammates.
    12	
    13	## Block orchestrator — owns durable local context
    14	
    15	Owns the charter, scope boundary, relevant architecture, dependencies, settled decisions, acceptance
    16	criteria, and decomposition into reviewable slices.
    17	
    18	Spawns one manager and resumes it while it remains effective, priming it with the relevant
    19	architecture and current slice — not the whole doctrine. Validates scope and completion without
    20	duplicating code review. Sends compact events upward. Never implements.
    21	
    22	**A block drives itself to ready. Everything inside its charter is its decision, including the
    23	authority instruments its own work needs.** It determines which instrument is required, authors it,
    24	obtains its ratification by consult — that verdict is the decision, not advice — performs the
    25	ratifying acts its own scope covers, and dispositions its own findings. It does not ask permission to
    26	proceed with work it owns.
    27	
    28	Instruments and evidence accumulate on the block's own line. **The program orchestrator places and
    29	registers them once, from the ready package, at landing** — not one at a time, mid-flight. A block
    30	that escalates each instrument as it is produced converts its own authority into a queue.
    31	
    32	**Escalate only four things:** a conflict with another block, a change to program structure or a
    33	dependency edge, an act on an artifact another block owns, or a consult returning inconclusive after
    34	one attempt. Everything else is the block's, and a question that could be settled by reading the
    35	charter or the tree is not an escalation.
    36	
    37	**A block owner gets its own rulings.** Design, wording, in-charter scope and evidence questions go
    38	to an architecture consult (`prompts/architect.md`) — read-only, question-shaped and unprimed, asking
    39	whether something violates a named invariant rather than asking for confirmation. That verdict is the
    40	recorded decision. Escalate to the program orchestrator only for landing order and the machine,
    41	ledger and authority-registry writes, cross-block conflicts, a charter scope change, or a consult
    42	that comes back inconclusive. Where the option set collapses to one survivor under a rule and a
    43	proven fact, decide and record it — a consult that cannot change the answer buys a record, not a
    44	decision.
    45	
    46	**Its role ends at reporting the block ready and verified** — the candidate identity, the evidence,
    47	and the manager's drafted squash message. That report is an input to landing confirmation, never a
    48	substitute for it: the program orchestrator, or the landing agent acting for it, confirms
    49	independently.
    50	
    51	**A block never authorises itself.** A block branch carries no authority-registry delta — the registry
    52	is authored trunk-side by its owner and inherited byte-for-byte through rebase, so a branch-local
    53	registry edit is dropped rather than repaired. The ledger's `base_sha` and everything under
    54	`repository.*` are orchestrator-owned in the same way.
    55	
    56	## Manager — owns delivery
    57	
    58	Dispatches implementation, selects risk-appropriate review lanes, adjudicates and deduplicates
    59	findings, verifies a potentially blocking finding before it interrupts an implementer, dispatches the
    60	smallest sufficient fix, and manages targeted re-review and acceptance. Drafts the squash message —
    61	subject and body — at verification, and sends it upward with the acceptance evidence.
    62	
    63	Stops when acceptance is met and no confirmed in-scope blocker remains. Escalates architecture, scope
    64	or non-convergence rather than buying more rounds. Never writes production code.
    65	
    66	## Workers
    67	
    68	Implementers write code and its tests. Reviewers are independent and read-only. External tool
    69	sessions (Codex, Grok) are manager-controlled workers, not teammates. Claude workers run in-process
    70	or in the supplied CLI pool (runtime modes, `README.md`); the role contract is identical in both.
    71	
    72	**One writer per candidate worktree at a time.** Parallel implementers only for naturally independent
    73	slices with disjoint ownership, isolated worktrees and stable boundaries.
    74	
    75	## Communication contract
    76	
    77	**Program → block:** objective; in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries; acceptance criteria; relevant
    78	architecture paths; dependencies; available capacity; any binding user instruction.
    79	
    80	**Block → program:**
    81	
    82	    STATUS: running | blocked | ready | complete
    83	    RESULT: <one sentence>
    84	    CANDIDATE_SHA: <the sha the evidence binds to, or none>
    85	    EVIDENCE: <paths or commands>
    86	    SQUASH_MESSAGE: <subject and body — required on ready>
    87	    ACCEPTANCE_COVERAGE: <each material change → the acceptance id covering it — required on ready>
    88	    DECISION_NEEDED: <only if blocked>
    89	    NEXT: <next material action>
    90	
    91	**Manager → block:** outcome; changed scope if any; acceptance evidence; the drafted squash message;
    92	confirmed unresolved risks; required decision if any.
    93	
    94	**An idle notification is not completion.** A role sends its result before going idle.
    95	
    96	Do not repeatedly paste SHAs, digests, diffs or reports between layers. Raw logs and review traces
    97	stay out of parent contexts and are referenced by path.
    98	
    99	## Block state — one compact record, replaced in place
   100	
   101	Not an append-only ledger. One file per active block, containing only:
   102	
   103	    OBJECTIVE:      what this block delivers
   104	    IN SCOPE:       what it may change
   105	    OUT OF SCOPE:   what it may not
   106	    ARCHITECTURE:   the invariants and paths that bind it
   107	    ACCEPTANCE:     the criteria, each with how it will be evidenced
   108	    SLICE:          the current review slice
   109	    CANDIDATE_SHA:  the frozen candidate under review, or empty
   110	    DECIDED:        settled decisions, with what settled them
   111	    DONE:           completed work
   112	    OPEN:           confirmed findings still open
   113	    BLOCKED ON:     required decisions, or empty
   114	    EVIDENCE:       latest validation, by path
   115	    NEXT:           next material action
   116	
   117	Agents reread it after a resume or context replacement. If an agent repeats mistakes, contradicts
   118	settled decisions, forgets scope or degrades, checkpoint and replace it — reuse is the default, not a
   119	law.
   120	
   121	## Large blocks
   122	
   123	Large cohesive blocks are legitimate. Do not force decomposition on line, commit or file count alone;
   124	treat size as a signal. Decompose for independent acceptance boundaries, owners, risks or review
   125	surfaces.
   126	
   127	Keep one persistent block orchestrator. Give each slice explicit scope and acceptance evidence, and
   128	review it while its context is small — the acceptance phase in `review.md` is what covers cross-slice
   129	behaviour, so do not rerun a cumulative review after every slice. Targeted tests per slice; the full
   130	gate only on the final landing candidate. Do not invent interfaces or scaffolding to make artificial
   131	slices. Sequential slices when ownership overlaps; parallel only for genuinely independent work.
   132	
   133	A block that does not converge after targeted fix cycles is resliced or escalated, not reviewed
   134	harder.
   135	
   136	## Liveness
   137	
   138	**A worker stops when it reports and stays stopped.** That is correct for finished work and a defect
   139	for unfinished work, and nothing notices the difference on its own. Twice in one session a block sat
   140	idle with work owed, surfaced only because someone happened to ask.
   141	
   142	**Keep a roster, not a memory.** Every block is non-complete (live, or parked with the unblocking
   143	EVENT named so the check is on the event rather than the agent), or complete (stopping is correct;
   144	do not resume). Sweep it on a cadence: compare the roster against what is actually running, resume
   145	anything non-complete that stopped, and check whether a parked block's event has fired.
   146	
   147	**A worker stamps its stop reason** — reported-and-complete, reported-and-owed, waiting on an
   148	external run, blocked on a decision. Without it a sweep sees stop-to-resume time and cannot tell idle
   149	from working, so the cost of a cadence is unmeasurable.
   150	
   151	**Sweep cadence is the cheapest lever and the first one to take.** Expected idle per stop is half the
   152	interval; shortening it cuts idle proportionally at no coordination cost. Take that before adding a
   153	seat.
   154	
   155	**Add a second orchestrator seat only above roughly five non-complete blocks, or when blocks need
   156	real-time adjudication rather than resumption** — below that a sweep services them and the cost is
   157	idle minutes. Two seats double the surface for divergent judgement without doubling the checking, and
   158	this program's expensive failures have been judgement, not throughput. If block count forces it: block
   159	ownership is disjoint in the roster so no block is addressable twice; one decision authority per
   160	question class, or two seats rule differently on the same doctrine and both cite it; the roster is the
   161	only coordination artifact, never seat-to-seat messages about state; and escalation precedence is
   162	defined, so a trigger neither arrives twice nor is assumed sent by the other seat.
   163	
   164	**A standing check that depends on the checker surviving is not standing.** Write the roster to disk,
   165	where it outlives the session that maintains it; a schedule is ephemeral and the file is not. The
   166	successor's first act is to read it.
   167	
   168	## Machine resources
   169	
   170	Read-only review work may run in parallel. Write work runs only in isolated ownership.
   171	
   172	**Heavy Cargo work — a full gate, a build, a mutation run — goes through the machine semaphore:**
   173	
   174	    rust-lock.sh <name> -- <command>
   175	
   176	Host-provided, on `PATH`; verify `command -v rust-lock.sh` before the first dispatch that needs it.
   177	It bounds concurrent builds host-wide — not memory — and passes through re-entrantly, so a nested call
   178	cannot deadlock on a slot its own tree holds. A "wait until no cargo is running, then start" check is
   179	not mutual exclusion — every waiter sees idle at once and they all start together.
   180	
   181	A gate carries its own memory ceiling and aborts its child tree on breach; a bare `cargo nextest`
   182	under the semaphore carries none, so shed that unprotected workload first. Steer on swap used, not
   183	free RAM — macOS keeps free pages near zero by design, and `vm_stat` reports its own page size, which
   184	is not 4096 on Apple Silicon. Take two `loadavg` samples before calling a trend.
   185	
   186	Cargo waiting on a target lock is not progress; do not read it as a stalled agent. Run the full gate
   187	only on the final landing candidate; workers run targeted affected checks.

     1	# Review — three phases, not repeated panels
     2	
     3	## 1. Discovery
     4	
     5	**One** independent review against a frozen slice. Lanes are selected by risk — correctness;
     6	architecture conformance; adversarial challenge of specification, scope and simplicity; a specialist
     7	lane only where concurrency, security or performance genuinely applies.
     8	
     9	Reviewers are blind to each other's findings. A low-risk candidate does not get a full panel.
    10	
    11	## 2. Closure
    12	
    13	The manager verifies findings before they block. **A finding blocks only when all four hold:**
    14	
    15	- supported by concrete evidence or a realistic reproduction;
    16	- introduced or exposed by this candidate;
    17	- within the block's responsibility;
    18	- material to correctness, safety, architecture or acceptance.
    19	
    20	Confirmed **P0/P1** findings go to the implementer as **one deduplicated minimal fix packet**;
    21	P2/P3 are carried, never forwarded. The reviewer
    22	that raised a finding may be resumed to verify that finding and its delta — targeted verification,
    23	not a fresh review. Do not rerun the panel after every fix.
    24	
    25	## 3. Acceptance
    26	
    27	After confirmed findings are closed, **one fresh review of the final frozen candidate** by an agent
    28	that has not seen it. It receives the charter, architecture and final diff — not prior conclusions —
    29	and looks for missed defects and integration problems. A high-risk candidate may get one additional
    30	targeted lane.
    31	
    32	## Acceptance is not reopened later — two checks that prevent it
    33	
    34	Reopening an accepted block is expensive and always has the same two causes.
    35	
    36	**A criterion that names a document requires a verified correspondence to that document.** Not "this
    37	bullet covers it" — an actual comparison, clause by clause, recorded. A block once satisfied
    38	"distinct identity types from the architecture document" with types that collapsed four of that
    39	document's variants into one, losing two identity distinctions. Every review passed, the criterion
    40	looked met, and the divergence surfaced only when a later block became the first consumer and found
    41	the contract's invariant inexpressible. A coverage mapping would not have caught it: the mapping was
    42	correct. What was missing was anyone reading the two side by side. Divergence found this way is
    43	recorded as a deviation for ratification, never resolved silently in either direction.
    44	
    45	**An artifact with no consumer has no evidence, and acceptance says so.** The same type had zero
    46	production callers, so no test could fail and none did. Compilation proved only that it was
    47	well-formed. Where a block delivers something nothing yet uses, its acceptance states that plainly
    48	rather than resting on a green gate that never exercised it — and names what would exercise it.
    49	
    50	## Sub-blocks — decompose so a review can finish
    51	
    52	**A block too large to review in one pass is decomposed into sub-blocks before implementation, by an
    53	architecture consult.** The consult owns the decomposition: each sub-block digestible, independently
    54	reviewable, and bounded so a reviewer can hold all of it at once. A block orchestrator does not
    55	self-decompose — the point is a boundary drawn by someone who is not implementing it.
    56	
    57	**Up to three review rounds per sub-block.** Then it is done, or it is escalated — not carried into
    58	the next sub-block.
    59	
    60	**When every sub-block is complete, the manager runs one conformance and one adversarial pass over
    61	the whole block.** Sub-block reviews establish each part; that final pair establishes that the parts
    62	compose, and it is where cross-sub-block defects are caught. Neither pass substitutes for the other,
    63	and neither substitutes for the sub-block reviews.
    64	
    65	## When rounds are the wrong instrument
    66	
    67	**A complete list closes its class and says nothing about any other.** Eighty-three enumerated
    68	restatements were repaired to two, and two internal contradictions then surfaced for the first time in
    69	twenty-three rounds — they had never been enumerated, so no amount of repairing against that list
    70	could reach them. That sharpens the enumeration thesis rather than weakening it: enumerate the class
    71	you intend to close, and do not read its closure as coverage of another.
    72	
    73	**Iterative repair on a large interlocking document can introduce defects as fast as it removes
    74	them.** Where a count plateaus and new findings trace to previous rounds' own edits, the method is the
    75	suspect, not the effort. Pre-register the disconfirming result before the next round runs — and treat
    76	reaching it as a question about the method rather than a failure of the block, the same shape as
    77	stopping rounds that cannot enumerate.
    78	
    79	**An explanation can be true and insufficient.** One block's non-convergence was diagnosed as
    80	resampling a proper subset, and a stop was lifted on that basis for one enumeration over the correct
    81	universe. The sweep was genuinely better — 1715 rows across 50 artifacts against 1164 across 21 — and
    82	an independent lane then found roughly thirteen more of the same species. The diagnosis accounted for
    83	the 39% nobody had examined and did not account for defects surviving a complete enumeration of the
    84	right population.
    85	
    86	**Accept-as-debt covers claims wider than their evidence, and nothing else.** A present-tense
    87	assertion that a ratified act has already settled is stale with an authority behind it, not imprecise
    88	— that gets a ruling, not a debt row. Getting the disposition right for the right reason matters,
    89	because the wrong reason sends the next instance to the wrong instrument.
    90	
    91	**A lifted stop that produces a better result and still does not converge is the outcome most likely
    92	to be filed as progress.** Say both halves: it was better, and it was not sufficient. Where a surface
    93	has now failed to converge under two explanations, the disposition for its prose class is
    94	accept-as-debt with the residue named — never a further round. Structural findings close regardless
    95	and are not folded into that debt: a gate whose reach is narrower than its claim is not prose drift,
    96	and a row proven against a different candidate is not a wording defect.
    97	
    98	**Never judge convergence on count.** One block's finding counts across nine rounds ran 5, 5, 6, 4,
    99	5, 6, 7, 6, 6 — flat, and by that measure nine rounds of nothing. Underneath, its blockers went from
   100	six against legacy text to two against text written in the previous round, and its dominant class from
   101	eighty-three occurrences to two. A convergence judgement on count would have been correct by its own
   102	measure and wrong in fact.
   103	
   104	**Read where findings land, not only how many.** Findings against a document's newest additions are
   105	convergence on a moving front; findings against legacy text mean the population is still unenumerated.
   106	A round falling from a dominant class to two of six, with both blockers against work written since the
   107	previous round, says the repair held — which the count alone does not.
   108	
   109	
   110	**A population no one has enumerated cannot be cleared by sampling it.** One block's surface held 47
   111	non-owner restatements; a review round finds one to six. That is roughly twenty rounds, and twenty-one
   112	had run without converging — not for want of reviewer or repair quality, but because rounds were the
   113	wrong instrument at any quality. Enumerate the population, then repair the class.
   114	
   115	**An inventory column is evidence, not a verdict.** Applied literally it manufactures findings —
   116	most flagged identity bindings were correct by construction, since a plan must define a derived
   117	identity before it exists. Discarding it loses the class. The defect was narrower than the column: a
   118	derived identity used as the *pin* for a measurement or a source location.
   119	
   120	**A receipt's count is a claim about what the producer found, never about what it delivered.** An
   121	enumeration reported 477 rows and 47 findings and delivered 120 rows containing 9, with its prompt
   122	already requiring it to declare truncation. Counting the artifact's own rows against its receipt is
   123	what exposed it, so require both numbers — rows found and rows listed — and a truncation flag when
   124	they differ. This is the truncation family again, and the first instance where the truncation was in
   125	the producer rather than the reader.
   126	
   127	**Treat a predicate miss as formatting before treating it as absence.** A receipt delivered as a
   128	table rather than marker lines read as zero results. Require markers at column one.
   129	
   130	## Ask a reviewer to defeat a gate, not to check it
   131	
   132	**A reviewer asked to check a gate reads it; a reviewer asked to defeat it runs it.** Set the task as
   133	construction: make this gate pass while something it exists to catch is broken. That found a totality
   134	check asking whether each scope item had at least one row rather than whether that item's obligations
   135	were present — ten of eleven rows could be deleted and the gate stayed admissible.
   136	
   137	**A gate that cannot fail invalidates every result it ever produced.** Not only the current one: each
   138	earlier pass was weaker than it was reported to be, so fixing it means re-running everything it
   139	cleared. Half-fixing it is worse than leaving it alone, because the passes then split into two classes
   140	nobody can tell apart.
   141	
   142	**An instruction is evidence about what its sender believed when they wrote it, never about the
   143	current state.** Refuse one that a later verdict has overtaken, and say which verdict overtook it.
   144	
   145	## Review churn — stop the reviewer prospecting
   146	
   147	**A reviewer may always find a new path.** But if two consecutive rounds surface previously-unexamined
   148	paths, the surface is not being enumerated and further rounds will keep finding more.
   149	
   150	**At that point, stop reviewing and dispatch a low-effort consult to enumerate the remaining paths.**
   151	Its output is the surface; review resumes against it. Enumeration is cheaper than discovery repeated
   152	per round, and it converts an unbounded sequence of rounds into a bounded one.
   153	
   154	## Documents get two rounds
   155	
   156	**A document gets at most two review rounds. Then it ratifies with its residue recorded, or it is
   157	rescoped.** Only a contradiction or a false claim blocks ratification; a proof gap, a wide phrasing,
   158	an underspecified field are recorded as open findings and the plan proceeds.
   159	
   160	A plan is a means. A block's deliverable is the code, and a document polished past two rounds is
   161	spending the block's budget on the wrong artifact — one plan took twenty-three ratification rounds and
   162	eight repair rounds while the cutover it gated had not started. Iterative repair on a large
   163	interlocking document introduces defects at roughly the rate it removes them, so the rounds do not
   164	converge; they circulate.
   165	
   166	## Convergence
   167	
   168	**Default maximum: two substantive fix cycles per slice.** Not converging means stop and rescope,
   169	replace a failing agent, or request an architecture decision — never buy another round.
   170	
   171	**Every third round, an architecture consult joins the next cycle.** Not to review the candidate
   172	again — to ask why three rounds have not closed it. Three failed cycles on one slice is evidence
   173	about the approach, not about the fixes: the same defect class keeps reappearing in new instances,
   174	or the mechanism cannot express what its criterion requires, or the work sits with an owner who
   175	cannot finish it. A fix cycle cannot see any of those, because it is looking at the finding.
   176	
   177	The consult is given the round history and the findings, and asked what is producing them. Its answer
   178	shapes the next cycle rather than being another verdict on the current one.
   179	
   180	**The cap is a signal, never a reason to land or supersede a block that can be made correct.** It
   181	exists because repeating a round that is not working wastes a lane; it does not exist to force a
   182	block out of the program. Where the work is genuinely closable and the only obstacle is a round
   183	count — the block's own or this one — the count is lifted and the block continues until it is
   184	correct. Superseding a block that could have finished, or landing one that is not finished, are both
   185	worse outcomes than another round. Rescope when the approach is wrong; lift the limit when only the
   186	budget is.
   187	
   188	## Reviewer calibration
   189	
   190	Every reviewer dispatch says this, because reviewers otherwise inflate:
   191	
   192	- The objective is finding real defects, **not maximising findings. Reporting none is acceptable.**
   193	- Severity is impact × likelihood — not confidence, and not tone.
   194	- A potential future concern is not a defect without a current requirement or a realistic failure
   195	  path. An architectural preference is not an architecture violation.
   196	- Pre-existing and out-of-scope issues are recorded separately and never silently expand the block.
   197	- Minor issues and suggestions do not block by default.
   198	- No praise, no generic summary, no unrelated recommendations.
   199	- Recommend the **smallest sufficient fix**, never a redesign.
   200	
   201	Each potentially blocking finding carries: location; the violated requirement or invariant; a
   202	concrete failure path; evidence or reproduction; whether this change introduced it; whether it is in
   203	scope; calibrated severity; the minimal sufficient fix.
   204	
   205	**A blocking severity requires direct reproduction, incontrovertible evidence, or independent
   206	verification before an implementer is interrupted.**
   207	
   208	## What a review does not cover
   209	
   210	**A review answers the question it was asked, not the document it was pointed at.** An artifact can
   211	accumulate passing rounds while a false sentence inside it is never in any lane's frame. A claim in
   212	an evidence document survived three rounds — a categorical assertion that a count-only canary could
   213	not catch a regression, contradicted by that block's own measured delta — because every lane was
   214	scoped to the tests and none to the prose.
   215	
   216	So prose claims are unreviewed however many rounds the artifact survived, unless a lane was scoped to
   217	the prose explicitly. Where a document's assertions are load-bearing, scope a lane to them and say so.
   218	
   219	**A PASS with zero blockers is not readiness while findings are open.** Dispositioning carried
   220	findings is new work, not a further fix cycle, and a candidate is not ready until each is adopted,
   221	deferred with its owner and gate named, or rejected with evidence.
   222	
   223	## Dispatch invariants for a lane
   224	
   225	**Pin every diff range to a frozen sha or the merge-base, never a moving branch name.** A lane told to
   226	diff against a branch that advances mid-review reports the candidate DELETING whatever the branch
   227	ADDED — the most alarming finding class there is, a block appearing to destroy someone else's work.
   228	It has cost the opening minutes of two triages to disprove, and it is entirely an artifact of the
   229	range.
   230	
   231	**State the universe and its selection criterion before sweeping, and justify it against what the
   232	block is answerable for — never against what its diff contains.** A sweep whose universe was one
   233	block's changed files read exactly like a complete sweep: same enumerator, same per-item evidence,
   234	same completeness claim. The universe is the one part a report never checks, so a complete sweep of
   235	the wrong universe is indistinguishable from a complete one.
   236	
   237	**A different universe is a first round, not a fourth.** Where a convergence stop was calibrated on
   238	resampling a proper subset, iterative repair was never under test and the stop does not apply to the
   239	first sweep over the correct set.
   240	
   241	**Fixing a broken gate is never "repair" under a no-repair stop.** A stop halts work on the artifact,
   242	never on the instrument — every verdict a broken instrument issued means less than it says, including
   243	the verdicts the stop itself rests on. One existence check matched only executables while its register
   244	named eighteen markdown proofs, so eighteen of thirty rows certified without being opened, and a
   245	planted nonexistent proof returned admissible.
   246	
   247	## Result contract
   248	
   249	Every reviewer ends its output with exactly this block, and writes the two marker lines nowhere else:
   250	
   251	    ===VERTER-RECEIPT-BEGIN===
   252	    LANE: <this reviewer's lane>
   253	    RESULT: <PASS|FAIL>
   254	    REVIEWED: <the sha reviewed>
   255	    FINDINGS: <n, or the word none>
   256	    FINDING <id> | <P0|P1|P2|P3> | <file>:<line> | <one-line summary>
   257	    ===VERTER-RECEIPT-END===
   258	
   259	Show that block literally in a prompt; never describe it in prose.
   260	
   261	`PASS` means no P0/P1. `FAIL` names what blocks. P2 and below are recorded and carried.
   262	
   263	**Severity is defined, not felt.** P0: data loss, a security or fail-open hole, or demonstrated
   264	incorrect behaviour on an input a user would actually hit — demonstrated, not reachable in
   265	principle. P1: a broken named invariant, a demonstrated race, a second implementation of something
   266	required to be singular, a test that cannot fail. A rule violation is P1 only with the rule named,
   267	the `file:line` and a concrete consequence; a violated convention or preference is P2. P2: a real
   268	but non-blocking defect — naming, an unclear assertion, a preferable structure. P3: a nit. **P0 and
   269	P1 block; P2 and P3 are carried and dispositioned later.**
   270	
   271	**Pre-existing and out-of-scope issues go in the reviewer's body, never in a `FINDING` row.** A row is
   272	a claim on this block's fix budget, so putting an inherited problem there is how a review silently
   273	expands scope.
   274	
   275	**A receipt relocated so that it validates must be proven byte-identical to the original.** Re-filing
   276	a misnamed or misplaced result is the block owner's act and is legitimate; editing it until it passes
   277	is not, and the two have the same visible outcome — the mechanical check sees a valid receipt either
   278	way. Compare digests before and after the move. For the same reason the landing agent never relocates
   279	a receipt itself: curating the evidence into the place that makes it pass is precisely what that check
   280	exists to catch.
   281	
   282	**`ALL SOUND` is a verdict about form, not outcome.** A `FAIL` is a sound result. A readiness claim
   283	that reads structural soundness as passing has not read its own evidence.
   284	
   285	Verify with `check-results.mjs`, which binds each result to its lane and to the reviewed sha, and
   286	rejects competing or stale files. The results directory is named for the frozen sha, so a leftover
   287	file from an earlier freeze cannot answer for a lane that produced nothing. An absent, truncated or
   288	inconclusive result is BLOCKED, never a pass.
   289	
   290	## Shaping a consult
   291	
   292	**Name the class, not the finding.** A prompt pointing at the row where a defect was found tests
   293	whether that fix landed. A prompt stating the defect as a general check — an invariant narrower or
   294	wider than the gate its document names — tests whether the class is gone, and only the second finds
   295	instances nobody has seen. Give the seat the surface and the questions; keep the block's conclusions
   296	out of it.
   297	
   298	**Before carrying a citation forward, open it.** A cite that no reader can follow reads as a
   299	transcription error rather than as the deletion it records, and a finding whose only carrier died
   300	with a branch needs its live carrier named instead of its dead one reproduced.
   301	
   302	
   303	**A seat that can only choose among the offered options will choose among them.** Give every consult
   304	an explicit escape — if the information does not determine the answer, say so and say what would —
   305	or a forced choice comes back looking like a finding.
   306	
   307	**Supply the facts, not the inference.** Give the assignments and let the pattern be reachable;
   308	naming it as a precedent tells the seat what to conclude. Never state a distinction as an argument
   309	toward an answer when it can be stated as a fact about the subject, and never frame a choice as
   310	binary when a third shape is available from the same facts.
   311	
   312	## Model routing
   313	
   314	Capabilities, not model names. Keep assignments here rather than repeated across prompts.
   315	
   316	| Lane | Default | Note |
   317	|---|---|---|
   318	| correctness, bug detection, architecture conformance | Codex | prime with the exact architecture documents; explicitly forbid severity inflation and scope expansion |
   319	| adversarial challenge of assumptions, spec, simplicity, scope | Opus | not the sole bug detector |
   320	| broad exploration, inexpensive second opinion | Grok, optional | not a sole correctness gate |
   321	
   322	Use max-effort settings only where judgment or risk justifies them. Routine coordination, status
   323	handling and mechanical work use cheaper settings.

   221	asserts presence goes red when it can no longer see. A test that asserts absence goes green.

   247	that changed.

    84	### Import-Route Admission Ownership
    85	
    86	`DerivedRawState.import_routes` is exclusively the CALLER-SUPPLIED
    87	authoritative route table — a bundler telling the host how ITS resolver
    88	resolves. The host memoises NO resolution there: the workspace's own
    89	bounded owner-edge candidate slot is the one resolution memo, validated
    90	per-reader against a captured immutable resolution world.
    91	
    92	- **Complete caller-supplied snapshot** — `VerterHost::set_import_dependencies`
    93	  is the **single producer**. Its entries serve until the caller replaces them;
    94	  their currency rides the `ExactResolution` facts the same push installs, and
    95	  their KEYS join the owner's authored specifiers in the import-route witness
    96	  inventory, so a caller-pushed specifier with no authored counterpart is
    97	  witnessed like any other resolution.
    98	- **Lifecycle reset** — `VerterHost::configure_projects` (project-graph
    99	  reconfiguration) and `VerterHost::upsert_via_scheduler_with_priority` (owner
   100	  source update) may `.clear()` the table.
   101	- **Deleted** — the host-side positive-route memo
   102	  (`cache_positive_import_route_result`), its `PositiveRouteStamp` /
   103	  `import_routes_positive_recorded_at_generation` sidecar, the known-miss
   104	  generation sidecar, and the per-entry oracles
   105	  `import_route_is_generation_current` /
   106	  `import_route_entry_is_generation_current`. A host-side memo duplicated the
   107	  workspace candidate slot and, having no witness of its own, needed a global
   108	  `content_generation` equality to decide whether it was still true — the last
   109	  such warm-resolution validity test in the session. What remains host-owned is
   110	  the resolved dependency EDGE set (`record_resolved_dependency_edge` writing
   111	  `DependencyState.dependencies`), which is reverse-dependency bookkeeping, not
   112	  a resolution answer.
   113	
   114	A KNOWN-MISS entry is never served warm: a negative answer is not evidence that
   115	the answer is still negative, so the reader refuses it and the specifier
   116	re-resolves through the one owner-edge authority (where a warm candidate whose
   117	exhausted probe set is unchanged is reused, so the re-resolve is cheap).

   120	
   121	- A direct `derived_raw_cache().entry(...).import_routes.insert(...)` outside
   122	  `set_import_dependencies` and the lifecycle reset methods is rejected — that
   123	  is how a host-side route memo would be reintroduced.
   124	- `positive_route_memo_producer_is_deleted` asserts the deleted producer and
   125	  stamp are absent from production source.

   127	### Parse/Resolve Ownership
   128	
   129	`IndexedReady` and `ShallowFileState` are content-addressed PARSE/INDEX
   130	artifacts. They retain authored import/export syntax, specifiers, shallow
   131	declarations, locators, and parse-domain facts — and NO resolved canonical.
   132	Materialising an artifact performs ZERO import resolution.
   133	
   134	- The complete reuse gate is `indexed_surface_is_current` = the owner's
   135	  `parse_env_hash` equals its live parse environment. No route-resolution
   136	  mutation can stale a parse artifact, so there is no edge-currency oracle and
   137	  no route-only edge-refresh materialise lane.
   138	- `IndexedReady.built_at_content_generation` is a CONTENT-domain stamp with one
   139	  consumer, `artifact_only_candidate_is_fresh` (a per-canonical comparison
   140	  against the workspace content-transition ledger). Never a global-generation
   141	  equality, never a route currency oracle.
   142	- `Route` is a pure parse-domain digest of the AUTHORED routing surface. The
   143	  resolve-domain half of a route answer rides the import-route resolution
   144	  WITNESS: a route walk collects a PATH-PRECISE witness through
   145	  `ResolutionWitnessScope` over exactly the edges it TRAVERSED, never the
   146	  owner's whole authored inventory (which for a barrel is far broader than any
   147	  route through it).
   148	- The layer-ordered wildcard walk keeps each descendant as an unresolved
   149	  `(owner, source_specifier)` edge and resolves it only when visited, so a
   150	  barrel's later-declared `export *` siblings are never resolved or loaded when
   151	  an earlier-declared one carries the requested export.
   152	- Resolution is SESSION-SCOPED for a session-bound consumer
   153	  (`SessionResolverContext::resolve_type_dependency_canonical` resolves through
   154	  the session's own overlay): with nothing baked into the artifact, a base-host
   155	  resolve would make an overlay-only dependency disappear.

   163	skill (the owner). `resolve_env_hash` carries the resolve-domain inputs (the

   173	## IndexedReady Target Contract
   174	
   175	Architectural target for the project-global cache cutover:
   176	
   177	- `IndexedReady` is the canonical post-parse per-file artifact: a shallow declaration INDEX plus body locators, NOT a body store.
   178	- Scheduler remains the sole source and parse authority. `IndexedReady` is built from scheduler-owned parsed snapshots.
   179	- `IndexedReady` stores canonical imports and exports for the file.
   180	- `IndexedReady` eagerly owns the declaration inventory: top-level symbol names, kinds, declaration/name spans, source-order contributor grouping (statement locators), type-parameter names, syntactic member headers, enum member headers, and the augmentation-scope inventory — all safe for host-owned `Send + Sync` caches. It must NOT store per-symbol lowered `TypeExpr` bodies, per-symbol body dependency vectors, member deps, `typeof` roots, a whole-file `EvalEnv`, or body semantic hashes.
   181	- Declaration BODIES lower lazily on first semantic demand through the shared lazy body service: the content-addressed `DeclBodyMemo` (a file-artifact child keyed by the owning artifact's `(canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash)`) asks the scheduler-side `DeclLoweringService` to borrow the worker-retained parse snapshot, lower exactly the demanded symbol's contributing statements, and return owned typed IR. Publishing an artifact lowers ZERO declaration bodies. First-touch singleflights per `(space, scope, name)` entry; sibling backfill is coverage-gated (only symbols whose FULL header contributor set was lowered populate). A content edit produces a fresh memo — superseded bodies can never serve a new-content demand; overlay artifacts own their own memo, never the base's.
   182	- Parse once per content generation through the lowering service's retained snapshot. Retention is LEASE-PINNED, not LRU/budget-evicted: the cold-index parse acquires ONE `SnapshotLease` for the artifact's `(canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash)` key and hands it to the artifact's `DeclBodyMemo`, so the header-index parse and every later body / whole-env / raw-surface demand reuse that ONE parse for the artifact's whole life — a live artifact never silently re-parses. The lease drops with the memo (hence the artifact), releasing the retained `Rc<ParsedEvalProgram>`. The temporary OXC parse arena stays on the worker (native) / the wasm thread-local shard, is per-file and per-version only, never crosses a thread boundary, and must not leak into long-lived `Send + Sync` shared caches; jobs return owned typed IR. A content edit produces a new key (fresh memo, fresh lease), so a superseded snapshot can never answer a new-content demand.
   183	- `IndexedReady` is authoritative for declaration STRUCTURE and locators (import edges, export edges, headers); lazily lowered bodies are authoritative only after materialization and are keyed by the observed file content/version.
   184	- `AnalysisReady` is an additive layer built from `IndexedReady`; it must not rediscover the same file structure — or body structure — through a second path.
   185	- If analysis or component-meta expands a shallow symbol, both paths must populate and reuse the same host-owned route, prepared-declaration, owner-import, and projection caches.
   186	- Shared symbol expansion helpers are the default. Do not add consumer-specific shallow expansion paths when the existing shared resolver can serve the work.
   187	- New work moves toward `SourceReady -> IndexedReady -> optional higher layers`, not further toward request-local or duplicate parser/resolver paths.

   190

The LANDED Stage 6 Option-B flip mints `HotTypeRef` handles at the dispatch boundary (the `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor) over the `Instantiate` query result — the consumer-visible `SemanticNodeId` the graph-bearing producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer — and does NOT remove `EvalEnv` / `whole_env()` (the oracle is retained as the parity rail); `EvalEnv` / `whole_env()` removal remains a LATER stage (the oracle-deletion + Stage 7+ work), not landed. The readers route through `ShallowFileState::{type_decl, value_decl, header_index}` and never materialise `whole_env()` — including any DEPENDENCY whole env (C3's export-target + alias peel routes through `resolve_value_export_target_graph_native` → `peel_value_decl_alias_graph_native`, never the legacy `resolve_value_export_target` whose peel materialises the dependency's `base_eval_env_arc`). That the consumer SET is exactly these four (no fifth) is established by the codex-confirmed exhaustive `whole_env()` consumer enumeration + the per-consumer oracle-equivalence tests + review — NOT by the guard's token-scan.
