   798	## Retired solver surface and retained carriers
   799	
   800	The former arena solver kernel is deleted. `TypeQueryEngine`,
   801	`TypeSolverHost`, `EvalEnvSolverHost`, `SessionSolverHost`, and their
   802	solve/relation/project modules must not appear in production. Structural
   803	guards in
   804	`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch_invariants_tests.rs`
   805	enforce that absence.
   806	
   807	The historical `verter_semantic::analysis::type_solver` module name remains
   808	only as a home for framework-neutral data consumed across crates:
   809	
   810	| File | Retained data |
   811	| --- | --- |
   812	| `arena.rs` | query-local node and primitive/literal carrier types; no solver caches |
   813	| `builtin.rs` | built-in utility classification and metadata |
   814	| `host.rs` | root identity, origin, utility-source, and request-status DTOs |
   815	| `prepared.rs` | prepared declaration facts and authored-body locators |
   816	| `result.rs` | exactness, execution-status, and typed diagnostic carriers |
   817	
   818	These types do not authorize evaluation. Component-meta and other consumers
   819	resolve through `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute(SemanticQueryKey::...)` and
   820	project the resulting semantic graph only at their output boundary.
   821	
   822	## Declaration symbol inventories
   823	
   824	`verter_semantic::analysis::type_eval` contains the shallow per-file
   825	declaration inventory. `EvalEnv` stores content-free facts and authored-body
   826	locators for ordered type/value contributor groups and augmentation scopes. It
   827	stores no `TypeExpr` and performs no evaluation. Authored bodies are lowered
   828	on demand by the shared semantic dispatch.
   829	
   830	The parser's `route_inventory` module owns authored syntax routes only. The
   831	semantic `ScriptShallowIndex` joins those routes with declaration headers, and
   832	semantic `decl_dependencies` owns structural dependency names. These layers
   833	perform no type evaluation and expose no resolved-element carrier. Query-time
   834	finite types are governed by the shared semantic-dispatch contract above.
   835	
   836	## Declaration Merging (CRITICAL)
   837	
   838	Same-name TypeScript declaration merging is owned end-to-end by the shared layer; there is exactly ONE merge path.
   839	
   840	**Carrier chain (owner → reducer):**
   841	
   842	- `EvalEnv.type_symbols`/`value_symbols` are `FxHashMap<String, TypeDeclGroup>`/`ValueDeclGroup` — ordered contributor groups. `add_type`/`add_value` APPEND (`group.contributors.push`), never last-wins `insert`. `TypeDeclGroup::merged_body()` returns `TypeDeclBody::Merged { contributors, kinds }` for any ≥2-contributor group whose contributors are ALL `interface` or `class` (`interface`+`interface` AND `interface`+`class` fold — the interface members augment the class INSTANCE type; the class value/static/constructor side stays on a separate value declaration). Every other group — a single contributor, or any group containing a type `alias` (a duplicate-identifier error in TS) — returns `TypeDeclBody::Single` (the last-wins representative). `ValueDeclGroup::merged_signatures()` concatenates every contributor's signatures in source order.
   843	- `ShallowTypeSymbol` / `ShallowValueSymbol` are SLIM HEADER views — they OWN no body product and hold NO `Arc<Lowered*Decl>` handle. `ShallowTypeSymbol` carries header facts only (`kind`, `type_param_names`, `member_names`, `contributor_count`); `ShallowValueSymbol` carries `kind`, `object_member_headers`, and the `.vue`-default provenance flag `is_synthesised_vue_default`. They are built directly from the `DeclHeaderIndex` (no body lowering), so `ShallowFileState::symbol(name)` / `value_symbol(name)` are header-only probes. The THREE demand surfaces are separate accessors on `ShallowFileState`: **body** — `type_decl(name) -> Arc<LoweredTypeDecl>` / `value_decl(name) -> Arc<LoweredValueDecl>` (the single `DeclBodyMemo`-owned lowered result, lowered on first touch; `value_decl` routes synthesised `.vue`-default bodies first); **dependency edges** — `type_deps(name) -> Arc<ClassifiedTypeDeps>` (per-state `local_deps` / `external_deps`, cached, edges ONLY — never a body); **augmentation bodies** — `augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` / `augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)`. The synthesised `.vue`-default is an eager macro-producer `LoweredValueDecl` stored in a dedicated body map (read through `value_decl`), with its slim header in `synthesised_value_symbols`. Shallow same-file member readers consult the content-free body surface — `type_decl(name)` yields `LoweredTypeDecl` whose `body` is `TypeDeclBody` (`Single`/`Merged` contributor SLOTS only; no `lookup_object` / embedded `TypeExpr` on the prepare surface). Member-name inventory comes from the slim header (`member_names` / `DeclHeaderIndex`); typed body demand re-borrows authored bounds lease-only through the shared lazy lowering path and reduces on the graph, never via a prepare-surface object projection. `PreparedTypeDecl` records merged declarations as `body_facts.merged_contributor_slots: Arc<[TypeBodySlot]>` (empty = single) — ordered content-free body-slot LOCATORS, never embedded `TypeExpr` bodies (the whole `PreparedTypeDecl` is fact+locator `NoTypeExpr`); the slim shallow symbols are thinner still (header facts only).
   844	- Body lowering (`lower_decl_body_with_provenance`) interns a merged interface as a distinct `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl { contributors: Arc<[SemanticNodeId]> }` carrier; a single declaration lowers exactly as before.
   845	
   846	**The load-bearing rule:** a merged declaration MUST reach the reducer as `MergedDecl`. A bare `TypeExpr::Intersection`/`SemanticNodeData::Intersection` is FORBIDDEN as the merged-decl representation — the intersection reducer applies own-body-shadows-heritage member precedence and cannot accumulate method overload groups (a same-named method in a later arm SHADOWS the earlier). `verter_session` may route/consume contributors but MUST NOT synthesise the merge as `raw_body = TypeExpr::intersection(...)`.
   847	
   848	**Peer-merge reducer** (`reduce_merged_decl_with_graph` + `merge_declaration_surfaces`, in `project_semantic_dispatch::walk`; routed through raise / expand / keyof / relation / substitute): (a) same-name methods/call-signatures ACCUMULATE into one ordered overload group (member value = ordered `Intersection` of the per-contributor function nodes); (b) conflicting non-method properties take deterministic first-contributor precedence (never `never`); (c) distinct members union; call/construct/index signatures concatenate. **`extends`/`implements` heritage is PRESERVED:** each contributor is split into its own-body surface(s) and its heritage `Ref` arms (a contributor lowers to `Intersection([heritage Ref…, own Object])`); own bodies peer-merge, then the reducer re-emits `Intersection([heritage…, merged_own_Object])` so the existing heritage-overlay path resolves inherited members lazily (own members shadow inherited same-name members). Dropping the heritage arms would lose inherited members from a `interface X extends Base {…}` + `interface X {…}` merge.
   849	
   850	**One merge engine, two consumers — display is non-mutating.** The peer-merge precedence lives in a single pure helper `merge_declaration_surfaces_core` (member union + first-contributor precedence + ordered method-overload accumulation, NO interning, NO own-body-shadows-heritage branch — that shadowing is the intersection reducer's job over real heritage arms). `merge_declaration_surfaces` calls the core then interns the overload groups + `Object`; the `display()` projection (`reduce_merged_decl_display_surface`) calls the SAME core and renders the result WITHOUT interning, so rendering a `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl` leaves `node_count` unchanged and is byte-identical to the canonical reduced surface (an accumulated overload renders as the property-intersection `m: (..) & (..)`, exactly as the reduced `Object` does — never as separate method signatures). Display must never call the interning reducer or dispatch (guard: `display_source_does_not_call_graph_interning_or_dispatch`).
   851	
   852	**Overload visibility** is a projection-time rule (`build_typeof`): a lone signature is visible (even if bodied); a multi-signature group surfaces every bodiless overload in source order and HIDES the trailing implementation (`has_implementation_body == true`).
   853	
   854	**Versioning:** same-file merged values root on the owner's single `FileWholeHash` self-root under a content-free query-identity key (R6) — no dedicated contributor-sequence fact. Cross-file ambient augmentation (`declare module`/`declare global`) is a separate concern documented under **Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL)** below — it reuses this same `MergedDecl` peer-merge path, it is not a second merge engine.
   855	
   856	**Guards** (registered in `critical_rules_have_guards.rs::CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`): `eval_env_type_symbols_are_grouped_not_last_wins_map`, `eval_env_add_decl_appends_not_overwrites`, `no_intersection_merge_synthesis_in_verter_session`, `merged_decl_lowers_to_distinct_carrier_not_intersection`, plus the discriminating `declaration_merge_facts` regression and the `declaration_merge` typeinfo oracles.
   857	
   858	**Merge/augmentation WIRE domain (architecture decision).** The wire representation of a merged declaration / module augmentation is ALREADY modelled inside `GraphTypeNode`: kinds **21–25** (`GraphMergedDeclaration` `{merged_symbol, repeated GraphDeclarationPart parts}`, `GraphAmbientModule`, `GraphModuleAugmentation`, `GraphAmbientNamespace`, `GraphGlobalAugmentation`), with decl anchors as nested `GraphDeclarationPart`. The LIVE carrier behind that wire surface is the graph node `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl { contributors }` — reduced to an `Object` / overload surface and emitted as a `GraphTypeNode`. The `SemanticQueryValue::DeclarationAnalysis(DeclarationAnalysisValue)` value variant is a **non-live shell** with NO producer and is NOT the wire carrier (its rustdoc points back here). A proposal to relocate merge to a distinct `DeclarationAnalysisGraph` wire message is **rejected**: the correct home already exists in the closed contract, so adding the message would be dead duplicate surface (new tags + TS bindings + validation + a `schema_version` bump + permanent compat). A structured-merge-graph producer (actual `GraphMergedDeclaration` emission) lands ONLY together with its first real FFI/TS consumer, as the existing kind 21 — never as a separate message. Do not re-flag "missing wire-proto relocation" as an incomplete deliverable.
   859	
   860	## Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL)
   861	
   862	Ambient declaration augmentation (`declare module "X" { ... }` / `declare global { ... }`) is a RETAINED, addressable scoped inventory — never fingerprint-only facts and never file-scope pollution.
   863	
   864	**Typed inventory (the single source of truth).** The binder retains every augmentation-block inner declaration on `EvalEnv`, keyed by `(AugmentationScopeKind {Global, Module(specifier)}, name)`:
   865	
   866	- `EvalEnv.augmentation_scopes` → ordered `TypeDeclGroup` (interfaces / type aliases), served by `ShallowFileState::augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` as a demand-lowered `Arc<LoweredTypeDecl>` (the eager header inventory lists the scoped names; bodies lower through the memo on first touch).
   867	- `EvalEnv.augmentation_value_scopes` → ordered `ValueDeclGroup` (`const`/`let`/`var`, `function`, `class`), served by `ShallowFileState::augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)` as a demand-lowered `Arc<LoweredValueDecl>`.
   868	
   869	Inner declarations NEVER enter file-scope `type_symbols`/`value_symbols`. Parse-domain `ModuleAugmentationFact`s are DERIVED from this typed inventory (`fact_emission::collect_augmentations`) — one fact per `(scope, name)` carrying the augmented name, its symbol space, and a HEADER-level shape fingerprint (kind + syntactic member headers + contributor count): publish hashes no bodies (honoring the zero-body-lowering publish invariant), so the fingerprint is invariant under a member's VALUE-type edit. Body sensitivity for every augmentation consumer therefore rides the per-contributor `FileWholeHash` facts, which BOTH the semantic augmentation stitch (`project_semantic_dispatch::collect_augmentation_contributions`) AND the compile-tier augmentation rail (`compile_fact_emission::observe_augmentation_fingerprints`) record alongside the header-level `ModuleAugmentationIndexShape` fingerprint — a member-body edit moves the augmenter's whole-hash and invalidates the consumer on both rails. There is NO raw-source byte-scan (Build Philosophy: no stage rescans raw source to rediscover what shallow processing captured — guard `shallow_walk_invariant::fact_emission_reads_only_shallow_state_never_raw_source`). There is no `ScopeId.kind`/`semantic_query::ScopeKind` — the live addressing is `AugmentationScopeKind` alone.
   870	
   871	**Cross-file augmentation merge is the SAME `MergedDecl` peer-merge path as same-file merging — NOT a second merge engine.** When a declaration `(canonical, name)` is instantiated, `stitch_module_augmentations` (in `project_semantic_dispatch::build`) finds every augmenter file via `FileArtifactStore::ensure_augmentation_index_populated`, fetches each augmenter's RETAINED inner declaration from the memo-owned augmentation inventory (`ShallowFileState::augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` / `augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)`; typed-IR only — never a source/byte scan in the resolver), lowers it in the augmenter's own file context through `prepare_augmentation_type_decl` + `lower_decl_body_with_provenance`, and folds base ∪ augmenter contributions into ONE `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl` carrier (flattening the base body if it is already a `MergedDecl`). Augmenter order is the stable `(canonical, parse_stable_hash)` key — discovery-order-independent. Relative-augmenter discovery loads the base's `reverse_deps_for` before the index scan.
   872	
   873	**Overlay-aware index.** `AugmentationTargetKey.population: AugmentationPopulation {Base, Session(u64)}`. A `Base` scan reads `is_base()` artifacts only (base parse-env hash + current parser version); a `Session` scan reads the session's overlay artifacts (matched by the session overlay discriminator) UNIONED with base, keyed by the overlay-set fingerprint. **`Session(u64)` is the overlay-set fingerprint, NOT a raw session id** — the producer (the body stitch) and the route-surface validator (`HostStoreView::validates_route_surface_domain`) derive `(population, overlay_discriminator)` through the SINGLE shared `session_view::augmentation_population_for_view`, so a session view can never be cached as, or validated against, a base-only set. Overlay augmenters NEVER poison the base index and NEVER cross sessions. There is NO base-only `assert!(view.compat_token().session.is_none(), …)` on the augmentation-index surface — a session view is accepted under `Session` population.
   874	
   875	**Cross-file FACTS** ride the stitch's own rail: the cold stitch observes one `FactKey::ModuleAugmentationIndexShape` (the augmenter-set fingerprint — the SOLE `RouteSurface` fact) plus one `FileWholeHash` per contributing file (base ∪ augmenters), and records `self_root_canonicals = {base} ∪ {augmenters}`. A content edit to ANY contributor misses the warm read; torn/partial routes through `ReturnOnly`, never warmed. Query keys stay content-free (R6).
   876	
   877	**Guards** (registered in `critical_rules_have_guards.rs::CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`): `session_overlay_augmenter_isolated_from_base_index`, `session_overlay_augmentation_isolated_from_base_meta` (the e2e overlay-isolation oracle).

   914	## Macro Type Traversal Rule
   915	
   916	When resolving cross-file macro types (`defineProps<T>()`, `defineEmits<T>()`, and other shared host-backed queries), only follow the import graph reachable from the requested type's declaration graph.
   917	
   918	**Macro resolution is one shared path — `shared_resolve(type) + normalise`.** Every macro (`defineProps` / `defineEmits` / `defineOptions` / `defineSlots` / `withDefaults`) and every imported `.vue` component surface resolves through exactly TWO steps:
   919	
   920	1. **Resolve ONE type via the shared resolver** — the generic-parameter type (`define*<T>()`) OR the object-argument type (`define*({ ... })`). `withDefaults` resolves the props payload type plus the defaults-object type and merges. `.vue`-component imports resolve the imported component's synthesized `$props` / `$emit` / `$slots` / expose surface recursively through the same dispatch (the hardest case — apply EXTRA caution: it is exactly where rule violations cause the worst hangs). Resolution is ALWAYS the shared typed-IR five-mode dispatch — no macro-specific engine, no per-surface walker, no eager element resolver.
   921	2. **Normalize from the stored stream (a thin transform, NOT a resolver)** — props: defaults / optionality / readonly / declaration provenance / `declared_in_macro_type_arg`; emits: walk the canonical `SurfaceEntry` stream once and expand each call-signature or property producer directly into a complete occurrence without a kind-array merge, name join, ordinal join, or post-hoc reorder; a resolved concrete property payload must be tuple/function-shaped, while an incompatible concrete payload closes the macro as `MacroInvalidReason::InvalidEmitsShape` on both Runtime and TSC demands (`{}` remains a valid empty emits surface, and open/opaque payloads retain conservative projection); the call-signature payload strips the leading event-name parameter; slots: function-like members only, first-parameter object becomes bindings, return type preserved; options/expose: pass-through object surface.
   922	
   923	A macro/import that resolves its surface through anything other than the shared resolver, or flattens a full surface eagerly before the consumer demands it, is a rule violation — collapse it into `shared_resolve(type) + normalise`.
   924	
   925	- There is one shared cross-file type resolver. Consumer-specific ownership rules live in `/component-meta`.
   926	- The resolver has exactly five query modes (see "Query Mode Contract" above):
   927	  - `Identity`: declaration identity and canonical source location only. No body read, no shape materialization.
   928	  - `Navigate`: minimum semantic work needed to continue a requested path. Intermediate hops run in this mode.
   929	  - `Shallow`: one surface level of the requested node without recursive expansion.
   930	  - `Expanded`: recursive materialization of the requested result.
   931	  - `Skeleton`: specialised generic-helper/cycle traversal that keeps unbound type parameters as shells.
   932	- `Skeleton` is a distinct mode, not a synonym for `Navigate`. It is currently scoped to cycle/generic-helper traversal — the materialization cycle gate's per-hop `Instantiate` (`ClassifyMaterializationCycleGate`, see `project_semantic_dispatch::cycle_gate`). New call sites must justify why they need Skeleton semantics instead of `Navigate` / `Shallow`.
   933	- Do not introduce ad hoc navigate/shallow flags; use the canonical modes and the path-precise projection surface.
   934	- Do not walk unrelated imports from the same file.
   935	- Do not treat plain imports as implicit exports.
   936	- Keep direct re-exports (`export { X } from`, `export * from`) as an explicit separate path.
   937	- Parsing a `.ts`/`.js`/declaration file for type resolution must cache discovered symbol name -> canonical location mappings.
   938	- Re-exported names and barrel hops must also be cached once discovered. If traversal follows `export * from './foo'`, cache that result so later lookups do not rescan the same barrel chain.
   939	
   940	If a file imports 20 modules but the requested macro type only references `AvatarProps` and `IconProps`, external resolution must only traverse those reachable dependencies.
   941	
   942	**TS-first resolution priority:** TypeScript types always take priority over JavaScript files when resolving ambiguous dependency candidates. Verter is a type-strict compiler that relies on TS typing for correctness. JS files should only be used as a last resort when no TS type definition is available. When `DependencyResolution.possible_canonical_ids` contains multiple candidates, use `effective_target()` which selects the single highest-priority candidate: `.d.ts` > `.d.cts` > `.d.mts` > `.ts` > `.tsx` > `.js` > `.jsx` > `.cjs` > `.mjs`. Do not try remaining candidates if the selected one lacks the needed type -- treat as not found.
   943	
   944	**Owned resolution is bounded by `workspace_root`:** For owned and project-scoped resolution, `node_modules` and package `#imports` ancestor walks stop at `IdeProjectConfig.workspace_root`. In monorepos, `workspace_root` may be above `project_root` to reach hoisted `node_modules`. In compat `createCheckerByJson()`, `workspace_root == project_root`. Unowned resolution (no owning project) remains unbounded. The boundary is passed via `ancestor_dirs(path, Some(&workspace_root))` and `ancestor_dirs_from_dir(start_dir, Some(&workspace_root))` in `verter_workspace::resolver`.
   945	
   946	## Typed-IR-Only Resolver Rule (CRITICAL)
   947	
   948	The native component-meta / typeinfo resolver pipeline drives every semantic decision from the typed IR (`TypeExpr` on the Rust side, `TypeDescriptor` from `@verter/type-ir` on the TS side). Source slicing, regex against type text, hand-rolled type-text splitters, `starts_with("Pick<")` shape sniffing, the synthesise-then-reparse pattern (`format!(...).parse_type_annotation(...)`), and `path.contains("/node_modules/")` classification are all forbidden inside that pipeline.
   949	
   950	- OXC AST lowers to `TypeExpr` via `lower_ts_type(ts_type, source)` (in `verter_semantic::analysis::type_expr_lower`) at exactly two boundary classes: macro / JSDoc PRODUCER fields lower eagerly at their producer boundary (stored on `Analyzed*Field`, `ResolvedLocalType.type_expr`, surviving every cache); top-level DECLARATION BODIES lower LAZILY on first semantic demand through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot (`DeclBodyMemo` → `DeclLoweringService`), NOT eagerly during shallow analysis — an `IndexedReady` publish lowers ZERO declaration bodies. Either way the analyzer/lowering arm takes an OXC node it already holds; downstream stages walk the resulting `TypeExpr`, never re-parse or re-lower at query time.
   951	- `parse_type_annotation` is reserved for JSDoc tag-type payloads (`{Type}` text inside `@type`/`@param`/`@returns`). Calling it from the resolver / projector / registry / policy / materialiser / compat pipeline is the bug.
   952	- Raw display strings (`Analyzed*Field.type_annotation`, `ExpandedField.raw_type`, `ResolvedLocalType.expanded`, `PropMeta.rawType`) are display passthroughs only. Resolver and compat consumers MUST NOT parse them back into `TypeExpr` / `TypeDescriptor`.
   953	- Workspace classification uses `ResolverContext::workspace_is_package_backed(canonical_id)` — the single structural predicate (workspace-owned is its complement; there is no separate `workspace_is_workspace_owned` predicate). Substring checks on canonical paths (`"/node_modules/"`, `"\\node_modules\\"`) are banned. The classification API is path-agnostic and handles symlinked / pnpm-hoisted / Windows-backslash / workspace-linked-package cases.
   954	- Hand-rolled type-text parsers must not exist inside the resolver. Walk `TypeExpr` nodes — `IndexedAccess`, `Ref { name: "Pick", type_arguments }`, `Union`, `Intersection`, etc. — directly via Rust pattern matching.
   955	- The JS compat layer reads `prop.type` (`TypeDescriptor`) for every semantic decision. `prop.rawType` is display passthrough only. Operator splits use union/intersection tag matching on `TypeDescriptor`, not hand-rolled string operator parsers.
   956	
   957	If a new requirement appears to need text manipulation inside the resolver, fix the producer (lower the right OXC node, store the right typed field, extend `@verter/type-ir` with a missing variant) rather than reparsing or pattern-matching on text. Architecture-guard tests in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs` and equivalents in `packages/component-meta` lock down this contract.
   958	
   959	See `/component-meta` skill for the full producer-side schema (typed `*_expr` fields on `Analyzed*Field`, `ResolvedLocalType.type_expr` "always populated" invariant) and the post-cutover delete list.

   961	### Typed Value Domain + Demand-Lattice Resolution (CRITICAL)
   962	
   963	The U2 query-value-domain design (`docs/arch/u2-query-value-domain-design.md`) locks the typed value
   964	domain and the demand-lattice that decides cache satisfaction/backfill. Resolution is typed end to
   965	end; display is a projection; error and absorbing types ride existing carriers.
   966	
   967	- **One key → one value arm.** Every `SemanticQueryKey` maps to exactly one `SemanticQueryValue` arm.
   968	  No non-type value is smuggled into `GraphTypeNode`; the wire taxonomy stays a closed type taxonomy.
   969	- **Demand lattice (presets, not enum order).** The five mode names (`Identity` / `Navigate` /
   970	  `Shallow` / `Expanded` / `Skeleton`) are PRESETS over `(ProjectionDemand, EvalPolicy)`. Cache
   971	  satisfaction and backfill are decided by lattice DOMINANCE over a RECORDED materialised
   972	  `(path, point)` set — NOT by enum order, and NOT by a meet-derived nominal demand. `Skeleton` =
   973	  `TypeParamShells` + carrier-stop; it is INCOMPARABLE to the expansion presets, a regime of its own.
   974	- **Display is a projection.** Canonical display is computed at publish from the cached typed value,
   975	  never a stored or re-parsed string. `display_needs` is display-only: it is masked OUT of every
   976	  typed-value family key and never drives resolution. Two queries differing only in `display_needs`
   977	  hit the SAME typed-value slot.
   978	- **Error tolerance.** A result computed over torn / broken / mid-edit input is `ReturnOnly` and is
   979	  never warm-admitted. A fact-rooted error (a recorded missing-dep fact) IS cacheable. `admit_decision`
   980	  gates on the ROOTING FACT's presence in the `ReadSetSignature`, not on the taint class.
   981	- **Error / any / never / unknown.** `unknown` = ⊤, `never` = ⊥; `any` is off-order (relates
   982	  bidirectionally); `error` taints and rides the EXISTING `SemanticNodeData::Opaque(QueryError)`. NO
   983	  new `GraphTypeNode::ErrorType` wire arm may be introduced — the wire-purity closure forbids it.
   984	- **Planned STAGE-B guards (gap tracked here per the architecture-guard rule).** The discriminating
   985	  behavioural guards land with STAGE-B: `cache_satisfaction_is_demand_lattice_not_enum_order` (U10),
   986	  `cache_satisfaction_is_materialized_point_not_nominal_demand`,
   987	  `display_needs_is_display_only_never_drives_resolution`,
   988	  `error_tolerance_broken_input_is_returnonly_fact_rooted_error_is_cacheable`, and
   989	  `error_any_never_propagation_lattice`. The design-gate guards landed NOW are
   990	  `error_rides_opaque_no_new_error_type_wire_arm` and `u2_value_domain_design_doc_locks_invariants`
   991	  (both in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_block/u2_value_domain_design_guards.rs`).

  1083	
  1084	## Flow-Return Substrate (U6)
  1085	
  1086	The whole-function flow-return capability (`U6.FLOW_RETURN_SUBSTRATE`) is a demand-sliced substrate over four artifacts plus one dispatch arm:
  1087	
  1088	- **`FunctionBodySkeleton`** (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/mod.rs`) — an arena-free (`Send + Sync + 'static`, `NoTypeExpr`) shallow statement/control skeleton with a return-site index, a lexical binding index, assignment/kill summaries, and per-site read/write/call + object-literal property footprints. Built once per function content version from the retained parse snapshot; NO type lowering at build time. **Which sub-expressions become their own tracked SITE is not this builder's own judgement**: `SkeletonBuilder::open_site` dispatches on `analysis::flow::value_descent`, the ONE wildcard-free classifier of an expression's value-structural children, and the content half's `Lowerer::lower_expr` dispatches on the SAME verdict. That is the structural fix for a planner/content split: a conditional expression got a structural arm in the CONTENT half while the planner still had no reason to descend into a branch, so every object literal in a branch lowered with each member value on the typed `SliceExpr::Elided` carrier and the whole return failed closed (`k ? { a: 1 } : 2` — `Error(Miss)` cands=0 — while `k ? {} : 2`, with no member value to elide, stayed green: the signature of an under-selected PLAN, not a broken arm). Neither half carries an UNDISPOSITIONED wildcard over `Expression` any more. `lower_expr` does end in `other => match value_descent(other)` — the wildcard is a DELEGATION, not a disposition: the wildcard-free match lives in the classifier, so a new variant does not compile until it is dispositioned THERE, and both halves inherit that disposition in the same change. `ValueDescent::TypeCarrier` is the ONE named asymmetry (the planner descends so a projection into the literal still reaches its members) — under-selection is the bug, and over-selection is not free: the content half's leaf answer for a carrier over a literal with a CALL-sourced spread embeds the spread's unreduced `ReturnType<callee>` carrier, which the leaf's fabricated-value gate refuses, so ONE carrier failed the whole RETURN closed for a value the checker types. So the content half no longer swallows a carrier over an OBJECT LITERAL: the literal keeps its structural lowering and the carrier contributes a MEMBER POLICY instead — see "Object-literal entry lowering" below. Every other carrier still leaf-lowers whole, because its type genuinely is the carrier's rather than its operand's.
  1089	
  1090	**Object-literal entry lowering never abandons the literal for ONE entry.** The fallback to the whole-literal leaf answer is not local: it folds every sibling, spreads included, into one shallow-pass answer, and a leaf answer over a CALL-sourced spread embeds the callee's unreduced `ReturnType<…>` carrier, which the fabricated-value gate refuses. One unmodellable ENTRY therefore failed the whole RETURN closed. Two entry families no longer reach it:
  1091	
  1092	- **A key whose property name is not its authored text** (`{ ...base(), [k]: 1 }`, `{ ...base(), 1: 2 }`) lowers as its OWN value position — `SliceObjectKey::Computed { value, authored }`. The evaluator names the property from the key's evaluated LITERAL (numeric keys through the SHARED canonical spelling, so `{ 1: x }` is the number `1`, never the string `"1"`); a key whose value is OPEN (`[key]` with `key: string`) leaves the surface's key SET unknown, which an object surface cannot express, so the literal fails CLOSED exactly as an unevaluable spread source does — publishing the modelled siblings alone would declare a member set missing a key the authored value has. The `authored` half is the second channel for the one nameable key the value channel cannot carry: a `unique symbol` key, whose value flattens to the bare `symbol` primitive.
  1093	- **A type carrier over an object literal** contributes an `ObjectMemberPolicy` (`Widen` / `Preserve` / `ConstAssert`) rather than swallowing the literal. The three states mirror the shared shallow pass's own object-literal widening contexts exactly, because a carrier that lowers structurally and one that reaches the leaf lowering must not disagree about the same literal. `as const` pins every member literal AND marks the literal's own members `readonly`; `satisfies` preserves uniformly (this substrate performs no contextual typing, so the target-driven half of tsc's rule is the deferred contextual-widening contract — `flow_return_catalog::flow_return_ob05_satisfies_preserves_value_shape` pins the preserving side).
  1094	
  1095	Two recorded divergences ride this, both asserted rather than silent: a SPREAD-contributed member does not take an enclosing `as const`'s `readonly` (the spread program merges the source's own modifiers — the existing spread-path `readonly` gap, reached by one more shape), and a `unique symbol` key keeps the member under a COMPUTED key rather than its nominal identity (`flow_return_ob12_keeps_unique_symbol_computed_key_shape`). Acceptance: `typeinfo_tests::value_inference::object_return_entry_forms_lower_structurally_over_a_call_spread` is the PRIMARY semantic pin against tsgo `7.0.0-dev.20260526.1`; `meta_tests::an_entry_form_over_a_call_spread_reaches_the_runtime_lane_intact` and `cases::g_block::framework_surface_executor::an_entry_form_over_a_call_spread_reaches_the_framework_surface_intact` are secondary evidence that the answer survives to a consumer.
  1096	
  1097	**Object-literal ENTRY classification is a second shared classifier on the same module** (`analysis::flow::value_descent`): `object_entry_descent(&ObjectPropertyKind) -> ObjectEntryDescent` splits an entry into `Property { key: ObjectEntryKey, value, kind: ObjectEntryKind, property }` or `Spread { source }`, with `object_entry_key` / `static_property_key_text` as the single authority for how a key NAMES its property (`Static` for an identifier or string literal, `Computed` for a computed or NUMERIC-literal key — `{ 1: x }`'s authored text is not its property name — `Unmodeled` for a private name). Accessor kinds are decided BEFORE the `method` shorthand flag, so a getter is never called a method. The classifier's guarantee is scoped: it is the single authority for the KEY and for the entry SHAPE, consumed by the skeleton's `open_object_site` and the content half's `lower_object_literal`. It is NOT the only site that decides an entry's KIND — `type_eval_build::extract_object_literal` (the shallow-pass leaf lowering the content half falls back to) and `function_program`'s property-footprint indexing each carry their own `PropertyKind` match. No behavioural divergence is measured (the precedences agree), and unifying them is not this substrate's boundary; the scoped claim is recorded here so the "single authority" phrasing is not read wider than it holds. The classifier answers a SECOND question on the same pass: `ValueDescent::UnmodeledCall` names a form whose OWN value is a call's return with no structural arm (`new f()`, `` tag`…` ``, `f?.()`, `await f()`, `(k, f())`, and a call under a type carrier), decided by the single predicate `analysis::flow::value_is_unmodeled_call` — the CONTENT half fails closed, the PLANNER half takes the `Leaf` disposition (a call's arguments never provide its value). That verdict moved here because it is a property of the FORM: the downstream carrier gate reads the leaf ANSWER, and for all of those forms the shallow pass answers a bare `any` with no carrier in it, so nothing fired and a fabricated `any` published warm and clean under a promise that a call with no structural arm fails closed. The skeleton records the branch arms as `SkeletonExprShape::BranchJoin`, and the graph turns them into `ValueDef` edges, so the demanded path threads through both arms UNCHANGED. Acceptance: `flow_return_conditional_branches_are_planned_and_lowered_by_one_descent`.
  1098	- **`FunctionFlowGraph`** (`analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs`) — the sparse per-function typed-edge dependence structure, built ONCE per content version from the skeleton ALONE (`build_function_flow_graph(&FunctionBodySkeleton)` — no AST, no resolver, no demand). Edges are typed by class: the live classes are value-def / path-write / eval-effect / control-region; the narrowing-predicate class lands across `U6.NARROW_*` (one shared `FlowFrame` lattice), closure-escape / loop-summary / try-finally-override land in `U6.LOOP_CLOSURE`. Read / callee-root / write-target edges resolve LEXICALLY: a name binds to the declaration(s) of the NEAREST enclosing region (the skeleton's `SkeletonBinding.region` + `SkeletonRegion.parent` chain), so a shadowed same-named outer binding gets NO dependence edge; only a name with no declaration on the enclosing chain falls back to same-name bindings of the HOISTING kinds only (`SkeletonBindingKind::Var` / `NestedFunction` in non-enclosing regions — block-scoped `let` / `const` / class / catch-param never enter the fallback, so a sibling-block hub can never be value-selected for a lexically unreachable read). Every whole-slot/path write emits BOTH effect directions — `site → hub` AND the reverse `hub → write site` eval-effect edge — because the demand planner's effect frontier walks out-edges only: selecting a slot's hub must select its write sites' evaluation, or a standalone preceding write (`x = "s"; return x`) silently drops out of the lowered slice's effect obligations. The graphs are memoized on `FunctionFlowGraphStore` (homed on `ProjectTypeStore.flow_slice()`); two demands against one content version build the graph once and only re-plan.
  1099	- **`ReturnPathPeeker`** (`analysis/flow/peeker.rs`) — the graph demand PLANNER, not a procedural walker: it holds ONLY `&FunctionFlowGraph` and computes the demand slice for `(return-site | expression-site origins, projection path)` as graph REACHABILITY into a `ReturnSlicePlan`. The two-frontier rule is expressed as edge-class stop conditions: value-provider edges (value-def + path-write) may STOP at a definite-present write for the demanded path head, while effect-class edges stay LIVE past value writes (a value-dead sibling still contributes its eval-effect edge). Over-budget traversals return the typed `FlowSliceBudgetExceeded` — never a truncated plan.
  1100	- **Hash-then-lower slice nodes** (`crates/verter_session/src/cache_runtime/flow_slice_node.rs`) — `FlowSliceHashNode` plans + folds exactly the selected subgraph into the opaque `FlowSliceHash` (no byte export, `Debug` redacted; sole constructor `compute_flow_slice_hash`), then `FlowSliceLoweredBodyNode` lowers ONLY the plan into the arena-free `FlowSliceIR` (each `FlowSlot` carries its binding-identifier span — the declaration-precise slot identity the content lowering gates on; the slice hash stays span-free). The hash-then-lower split is TWO rails: the type-state pins hash-before-lowered-KEY (the lowered store is unaddressable without a minted hash), and the per-thread `compute_flow_slice_hash_thread_invocations` counter behaviorally pins that the lowered COMPUTE performs zero hash computations (the type system cannot — the hasher is a public producer); the counter, its accessor, and its increment are gated behind `verter_semantic`'s `test-support` feature (enabled by `verter_session`'s dev-dependency edge — `#[cfg(test)]` cannot serve a cross-crate consumer), so production builds compile the hasher without the TLS or the increment. Keys carry the per-function body-sensitive, cosmetic-insensitive `flow_body_stable_hash` (from the per-file `FunctionProgramIndex`), NOT `parse_stable_hash` — PLUS the EXACT per-function byte hash `flow_body_exact_hash`. Both nodes publish content-addressed artifacts with EMPTY fact rails — slice identity is never a warm-validity oracle — and "the key IS the validity oracle" holds only because TWO things are true together: the key carries that exact byte axis, and the artifacts carry NO absolute source position. That second half is a TYPE, not a convention: every span in `FunctionBodySkeleton` — and therefore in `FlowSliceIR` — is a `FrameSpan` (`verter_semantic::analysis::flow::frame_span`), a private-field newtype whose only constructor from a source position is `FrameSpan::rebase(anchor, span)` and whose only way back is `FrameSpan::to_absolute(anchor)`. `SkeletonBuilder::frame_span` is the ingress crossing (so `finish` is a plain MOVE with no per-family rebase pass to apply to five families and forget on two — which is exactly what happened: the read and call footprints kept ABSOLUTE offsets, and `lower_slice_plan`'s source-order effect sort mixed the two coordinate systems, ordering every call after every write at any non-zero anchor); `Lowerer::rebase` is the one crossing on the consumer side, and `FrameSpan::to_absolute` has exactly one caller (the parameter inventory comparing stored binding positions against live default-initializer offsets). A mixed comparison — `frame.start < absolute.start`, or a sort keyed off one of each — does not COMPILE. That claim was one accessor away from false: `FrameSpan::start()` / `::end()` were `pub fn -> u32` with ZERO production callers (one test), so the comparison the module exists to forbid was writable in the module that forbids it. They are deleted; `FrameSpan` now exposes no offset at all, and every consumer comparison is `FrameSpan`-to-`FrameSpan` (`contains`, the derived `Ord`). Two things stay CONVENTIONS and the module now says so instead of implying otherwise: the anchor is a bare `u32` on both crossings, so `rebase(0, absolute)` still mints a `FrameSpan` holding an absolute offset and `to_absolute(wrong_anchor)` still lands somewhere (nothing pairs a `FrameSpan` with its anchor — it outlives the file version it was recorded on, which is exactly why the anchor is re-supplied at egress); and the derived `Ord` / `Hash` let two frames' spans compare without either frame being named (harmless because every artifact here is per-function). `SkeletonRead` carries no span at all: the reference position had no consumer, and dead state is where a stale coordinate hides. Acceptance: `skeleton_is_invariant_under_the_function_position`, `lowered_ir_is_invariant_under_the_function_position`, `lower_orders_effects_by_authored_position_at_any_anchor` (the predecessor of the last read `span.start` back off the result and asserted it ascended — the same key the lowering had just sorted on, over a fixture at offset 0 where both systems coincide, so it held by construction and passed while the invariant was violated). Each half covers a blind spot the other cannot: `flow_body_stable_hash` is an AST fold, so it is blind to a leading blank line (which moves every absolute position and is fixed by the relative anchoring) AND, because it alpha-normalizes binding/reference identifiers, blind to a local rename that shifts every position INSIDE the body (which relative anchoring does NOT survive and only the exact byte axis catches). The exact axis is deliberately per-FUNCTION, not the file's content hash, so an edit to a sibling function leaves an untouched function's artifacts warm. Acceptance: `flow_bundle_reuse_is_sound_for_every_content_its_key_admits`, `the_two_shift_edits_are_invisible_to_flow_body_stable_hash`.

  1147	### Flow-Return Substrate (U6) Debt Notes
  1148	
  1149	- **The demand-sliced substrate is the ONLY flow evaluator.** A `FlowReturn` cold path plans the demand slice as graph reachability (`FunctionBodySkeleton` → `FunctionFlowGraph` → `ReturnPathPeeker`), hashes it (`FlowSliceHashNode`), lowers exactly the plan into the content-free `FlowSliceIR` (`FlowSliceLoweredBodyNode`), and evaluates through the slice-gated owned content (`crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs` — `SliceContent`, produced per demand through the `DeclBodyMemo` lease-only retained-snapshot run). Content OUTSIDE the slice never lowers: an unread binding initializer is omitted (the gate is the `FlowSlot` binding-identifier SPAN, declaration-precise — a shadowed same-named sibling declarator the plan kept out never lowers), a sibling member value rides the typed `SliceExpr::Elided` carrier (fail-closed if ever observed), and `if`-test / expression-statement positions carry no content. Selected leaf expressions lower through the ONE shared shallow-pass per-expression entry `infer_declaration_expression_type` (literal-preserving for arrow bodies / `const` initializers, widening otherwise). There is no whole-body evaluator and no separate return scanner; a leaf-lowering budget edge can only be charged by SELECTED content (guarded by `flow_return_unread_binding_content_never_lowers` / `flow_return_member_demand_never_lowers_elided_sibling_content`).
  1150	
  1151	- **Optional-parameter body widening (U6.VALUE_INFERENCE debt).** Inside a body, a parameter declared `x?: T` evaluates to `T | undefined`. That is CORRECT under strict null checks (TS 5.8 / 6.0 semantics): a caller may omit the argument, so every body read sees the `undefined` arm. The non-strict branch (plain `T`, e.g. `number`) is NOT modeled by the flow-return substrate and remains U6.VALUE_INFERENCE debt — do not "fix" the strict branch to the non-strict answer.
  1152	- **Write-effect retype application (U6.NARROW_SUBSTITUTION / U6.VALUE_INFERENCE debt).** The evaluator does not yet APPLY the slice's `FlowSliceIR.effects` write obligations (retypes / widenings before evaluating the value providers that read the affected slots — the `flow_ir` contract). Until that lands, a lowered slice carrying a whole-slot write effect targeting a parameter or a value-selected slot fails CLOSED as the `UnappliedWriteEffect` DEGRADED SUCCESS (`ReturnOnly`, never warm) — evaluating past the write could publish a wrong type as complete (assignment narrowing; object members evaluate left-to-right). Projection-path writes (`x.a = v`) never retype the binding and stay clean; writes to slots that are neither parameters nor value-selected cannot be observed by the demanded value. The rail intentionally over-degrades source-order-safe direct reads (`return { b: x, a: (x = "s") }` degrades a correct `string | number` — recorded as the `debt:R2-UNAPPLIED-WRITE-EFFECT-SOURCE-ORDER` row on `U6.FLOW_RETURN_SUBSTRATE` in `scripts/manifests/typeinfo-programme-reconciliation.json`); a span-comparison suppression ("every read span precedes the write span") is UNSOUND — a deferred closure read (`{ b: () => x, a: (x = "s") }`) observes the write despite preceding it in source — so sound suppression requires actual write-effect application. Do not "fix" a degraded reassignment fixture by dropping the rail — implement the retype application on the same graph instead.
  1153	- **Function-scoped (`var`) reaching definitions.** The evaluator carries TWO local layers: the LEXICAL layer (`const` / `let`) that block and `if`-arm evaluation saves and restores, and the FUNCTION-scoped `var` layer those restores never touch (`var` hoists, so `{ var y = 1 } return y` is `number`). Three rails ride that layer. (a) **Conditional definitions fail closed.** A conditional-arm nesting counter rises on `if` ARMS only — a plain block executes unconditionally and never increments it — and a `var` bound under non-zero nesting enters `var_conditional_locals`; OBSERVING such a binding records the `ConditionalVarDefinition` degradation (`ReturnOnly`, never warm), mirroring `var_degraded_locals` exactly, so an unobserved conditional `var` degrades nothing and an unconditional rebind clears the flag. The substrate has nothing to join on (`SliceStatement::If` carries no test content by design), and the join algebra is owned by `U6.NARROW_*` on the shared `FlowFrame` lattice over the ONE `FunctionFlowGraph` — a merge algebra over the evaluator's `locals` / `var_locals` maps would be exactly the forbidden second flow structure. Recorded as the `debt:CONDITIONAL-VAR-BRANCH-JOIN` ledger entry on `U6.FLOW_RETURN_SUBSTRATE` in `scripts/manifests/typeinfo-programme-reconciliation.json`. Accepted cost: `if (flag) { var w = 1 } return w` was a coincidentally-correct warm `number` and is now degraded — tsc REJECTS that program (TS2454). (b) **A `var` redeclaring a PARAMETER shares the parameter's slot.** The graph's lexical resolution unions the FUNCTION-scope frame's hits with every same-name hoisting-kind binding wherever written (inner block-scoped frames stay exact, so shadowing is preserved), the content lowering resolves a hoisted-`var` name as `SliceExpr::Local` / `CallOnBinding` AHEAD of the parameter list, and both carry the parameter ordinal so an unbound read (before the declarator, or on a path that never reached it) still resolves to the parameter — never a fabricated `any`. (c) **Loop transparency requires transfer-inert selected content.** A return-free loop stays `TransparentLoop` only when it declares no escaping `var` and its body has no live selected-slot guard, call/assertion, or write whose iteration flow can change a downstream selected read. Read/write comparison is path-aware: statically distinct member siblings do not alias, while whole-root and computed segments remain conservative. Literal-dead `if` branches and a `while (false)` body contribute neither loop transfer nor unapplied-write degradation. Nested closure effects are inspected only for a function/arrow in CALLEE position — callback arguments are values, not proven invocations — and a directly invoked closure inside a loop fails closed when its own skeleton writes a captured downstream slot or reads one in a control/call site. Such iteration-dependent flow requires a fixed point the substrate does not model, so it takes the typed `SliceUnsupported::Loop` no-value rail and cannot warm. A control read with no modelled guard (`while (x + 1)`), a callback argument, and a loop with no selected capture remain transparent; precise closure-guard transfer remains deferred.
  1154	- **A bare direct invocation cannot publish an unmodeled closure transfer.** An expression statement whose callee is an inline function/arrow is checked against the downstream selected slot. If that closure writes the capture or reads it in a guard/control position, the slice takes the typed `InvokedClosureEffect` no-value rail with zero candidates. This is intentionally conservative: the substrate does not yet apply the single-invocation closure's narrowing overlay, so discarding the effect and warming the pre-invocation union would be unsound.
  1155	- **Declarator annotations SUPPLY a stable assignment and mutable-capture authority.** A declarator's authored TS annotation lowers onto `SliceStatement::Binding.declared` through the same shallow pass a `SliceExpr::Type` leaf carries. Lexical declarations seed that authority at their source-ordered binding statement; selected `var` annotations seed it at frame entry because both assignment checking and a forward read observe the hoisted declared type before the initializer (`X66_hoisted_annotated_var_authority_serves_forward_read`). Runtime values remain source-ordered: an initializer executes at its statement, and an initializer-less `var` performs NO runtime write, so `x = "b"; var x: "a" | "b"; return x` keeps the assignment-reduced `"b"`. With no preceding reaching value, an initializer-less annotated declaration still supplies its declared type (`var y: number | undefined;` is `number | undefined`, not the unbound implicit `any`). A destructured parameter element seeds both its reaching value and declared authority before its first read OR write, so a preceding write is reduced against the annotated member union. A non-union annotated initializer publishes the declared type (`const y: string = "s"` is `string`; `const y: "s" = "s"` still pins `"s"`); a declared union is assignment-reduced to comparable DECLARED constituents for both its initializer and later whole-binding writes (`let x: "a" | "b" = "a"; x = "b"` reaches `"b"`). A nested function value carries the exact declared authority for each captured mutable `let`/`var` and parameter element, keyed by binding identity rather than reconstructed from a current value. A reaching `let` value remains the closure's read authority until that closure writes it; `var` and forward-`let` captures retain authored authority. The declared node rides a separate lexical/function-scoped map from the changing reaching value, including scope-shadow close and layer snapshots, so a later write never reconstructs authorship from the current value. Assignment-context object literals retain a pre-property-widening member view solely for constituent selection. When mutually assignable object arms differ by exact present keys or discriminants, that evidence can select the best-matching declared arm; spread programs deliberately bypass exact-key selection because their final key set is not closed. Generic strict-subtype dominance is not a checker rule here: required-property presence alone does not discard an overlapping optional-property constituent. Ordinary object evaluation still uses mutable-property widening. `X65_object_assignment_declared_union_selects_matching_arm`, `X69_overlapping_object_union_assignment_selects_narrow_arm`, `X75_fresh_object_assignment_selects_optional_member_arm`, `X76_fresh_computed_object_assignment_selects_optional_member_arm`, `X77_spread_object_assignment_preserves_declared_union`, and `X84_required_property_assignment_preserves_optional_union_arm` pin those boundaries.
  1156	- **Abrupt-edge state is point-in-time and scope-closed.** Break, return, and throw edges each capture the complete reaching-definition state where the edge occurs. Every crossed lexical scope replays its shadow close onto those snapshots before a construct joins them; `if` arms likewise snapshot only after closing the arm scope. A `finally` entry joins normal completions, throw points, and pending break/return pre-states. Return inference aggregates every authored try/catch/finally return even when an abrupt `finally` overrides runtime completion, while the pending control edges exposed to an enclosing construct still obey that override: an abrupt finally replaces pre-finally returns and breaks but preserves returns and breaks authored by the finally itself. A pending named break overridden by an abrupt finally remains an implicit-`undefined` return-inference contributor when its target statement has no following current-function return; that holds for both a directly labelled try (`X68_finally_return_over_labelled_break_keeps_undefined`) and a try wrapped by labelled blocks (`X80_wrapped_labelled_try_finally_keeps_undefined`). A following return suppresses that contributor, preserving `X52_finally_entry_joins_pending_break`. Switch dispatch death is independent of a live clause fall-through chain: exhausting the no-match edge cannot delete fall-through into `default`.
  1157	- **Logical guard facts are edge-asymmetric when an operand is unmodelled.** The guard tree preserves `SliceGuard::None` operands instead of simplifying them away. On `modelled && opaque()`, the true edge may apply the modelled fact but the false edge cannot negate it; on `modelled || opaque()`, the true edge establishes nothing while the false edge may negate every modelled disjunct. Predicate leaves retain their negation bit, so De Morgan transformation is reversible: the surviving edge of `!(isStr(x) && opaque)` recovers the original positive predicate rather than erasing it. A disjunction evaluates every alternative from the same starting overlay and joins each alternative's FINAL value per subject; intermediate conjunction facts never become separate union contributors (`N21_guard_union_uses_final_alternative_overlay`, `N22_double_negated_guard_union_uses_final_alternative_overlay`). An alternative whose sequential conjunction has no surviving declared arm is represented as impossible and contributes no overlay to the disjunction (`N23_impossible_conjunction_drops_dead_disjunction_alternative`). This is one `And`/`Or` authority consumed in positive and negative modes, not two pattern-specific rewrites.
  1158	- **Guaranteed-return qualifier for labelled-break inference.** In the preceding abrupt-edge rule, a “following current-function return” means a suffix statement that guarantees the return on every normal path (a direct return, a sequential block containing one, or both arms of an `if`). The qualifier is inherited through recursively lowered blocks and labels: an abrupt `finally` retains a pending named break as a return-inference-only suffix edge when the crossed target carries it. A suffix contributor already strictly covered by an ordinary return is redundant; an incomparable suffix remains in the inferred union. Merely containing a conditional return does not suppress the implicit-`undefined` contributor.

  1207	## Tagged-Component Publication: Root Admission Commits, Members Backfill
  1208	
  1209	A mixed `Relate` / `FlowReturn` / `ResolveCall` component closes as ONE decision, but it does NOT publish as one indivisible write. The contract is two-tiered:
  1210	
  1211	- **Root admission is the COMMIT BOUNDARY.** The machinery root publishes through its family singleflight (`execute_via_cold_build_helper_capturing_publication`). That publish is the component's linearization point: it represents a successfully completed result whose read set, self-roots and generation stamp are already validated.
  1212	- **Member publication is INDEPENDENTLY FENCED BACKFILL.** `relation_drain_completed_members` / `flow_return_drain_completed_members` / `resolve_call_drain_completed_members` run strictly AFTER that commit and hand each member to `publish_{relation,flow_return,resolve_call}_member_fenced`, which re-checks cancellation and the cold-abort sweep at its own publish. A member the fence refuses releases its inline flight, stays COLD, and recomputes on the next demand. Reduced cache completeness after the commit boundary is not corrupted semantics — every member is separately validated and separately recomputable.
  1213	
  1214	Two things are NOT weakened by that split, and both admit nothing at all:
  1215	
  1216	- **Pre-linearization cancellation** — a component cancelled before the root's admitted publish releases every flight without publishing anything.
  1217	- **Genuine component failure** — any degraded / `Unknown` / budget-exceeded / abandoned-session member poisons the WHOLE component: `ReturnOnly`, no entry, no fact signature, no reverse-index metadata, for the root and every member alike.
  1218	
  1219	There is deliberately no retrospective rollback of a committed root when a later member is refused: rolling back would alter established relation semantics without adding correctness, because the refused member is never readable as a stale value — it is simply absent.
  1220	
  1221	Guards: `mixed_component_member_publish_is_fenced_backfill_behind_a_committed_root`, `pre_linearization_cancellation_admits_nothing`, `genuine_component_failure_admits_neither_root_nor_member` (`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_tests.rs`).
