367-docs/arch/refactor/rev11/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md:4965:docs/arch/parselower-design.md:224:- **LANDED in 8-A3 (the durable Kind-A fence).** Block 8-A3 landed the durable reverse-materialization (`SemanticNodeId → TypeExpr`) OUTPUT fence for the TRUE OUTPUT SINKS (Kind A) as a SEALED-TRAIT CAPABILITY — **`OutputProjector`** + the sealed carriers **`OutputTypeExpr`** (plain-raise) / **`MaterializedOutputTypeExpr`** (reduce-then-raise) — in `project_semantic_dispatch/output_materialization.rs`. The callable boundary MOVED OFF `ProjectSemanticDispatch` onto the `OutputProjector` capability; the carrier payload is a PRIVATE inner `TypeExpr` whose only reader is a capability-gated accessor (`into_type_expr` / `type_expr`, each taking `&impl OutputProjector`); each true output-**SINK** module (the exact module that projects — `meta_resolve::projectors::output_sink` (a DEDICATED terminal sink submodule, re-exported at `meta_resolve::projectors::MetaResolveProjectorsOutputCap` — extracted EXACTLY so the parent `projectors`' non-sink helpers (`macro_payload_substrate`, `published_reducer`, the per-kind projector children) cannot mint), `meta_resolve::materialize::field_types`, `host_manage::component_meta_methods`, `typeinfo::raise`, `typeinfo::framework_surface::{vue_exec,svelte_exec}` (`vue_exec`'s whole reachable scope — `vue_exec` + its `normalize` child — is output-only, so the single cap is correct), `component_meta_query_engine::{registry_decl,surface}` — **EIGHT per-sink caps**) owns a private-field capability whose constructor is `pub(in <sink-module>)` — scoped to the SINK, NOT the subtree. `pub(in P)` grants the mint to `P` AND every module at-or-under `P`, so the mint scope is scoped to a TERMINAL output sink whose entire reachable production module tree is itself output-only — that (not "per-leaf") is what makes the fence compiler-enforced for in-subtree code: a Kind-B bridge sibling (`meta_resolve::dispatch_helpers`, `host_manage::eval_env`) — or a non-sink helper sibling — is NOT reachable from any sink's mint scope and cannot name any cap's constructor (a planted `*OutputCap::new` there is `E0624`). In safe production Rust OUTSIDE the audited output-materialization payload vault, `OutputTypeExpr` and `MaterializedOutputTypeExpr` do not expose a readable `TypeExpr` field (the inner `TypeExpr` lives in the deeply-private `carrier::payload` vault): capability-free unwrap is unrepresentable by field access, auto-deref, arbitrary trait impls, or inherent methods, and the only production APIs returning `TypeExpr` / `&TypeExpr` are the capability-gated `into_type_expr` / `type_expr` accessors. The seal is COMPILER-enforced both OUT of crate and WITHIN it: `mod sealed` is PRIVATE (not `pub(super)`) inside `mod projector`, so `projector::sealed::Sealed` is nameable ONLY from within `projector` — a sibling `carrier` / `carrier::payload` (or any other crate module) that writes `impl projector::sealed::Sealed for HotCap` is `E0603` (module `sealed` is private), so the sealed trait cannot be implemented for a non-sanctioned type even from a sibling owner-descendant scope; the `output_projector_owner_registration_inventory` topology guard is the defense-in-depth backstop, not the primary. The mint half is the same shape (COMPILER-ENFORCED as the PRIMARY barrier): a hot / session / Kind-B mint is `E0624` / `E0451` (the terminal-sink capability constructor is unreachable from any non-sink module), a hot carrier-unwrap is `E0277` (unsatisfied `OutputProjector` bound — the trait is sealed) AND the inner `TypeExpr` is not even a readable field, and a hot `.type_expr_for_test()` is `E0599` (the carrier `_for_test` accessors are gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` — the production-unreachable test-support feature activated only by `verter_session`'s own dev-dep self-edge — so they are COMPILE-ABSENT from every production build, unlike a `debug_assertions` gate which would be present in ordinary debug builds). The residual TRUSTED surface is the inline payload vault + the projector registration module (and the by-name identity of which owner types are sinks), whose exact item/module/signature shape is structurally guarded as DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH (a CLOSED structural allowlist, NOT the primary barrier); this claim does NOT cover guard deletion, deliberate edits inside that trusted vault, or unsafe code unless the crate forbids unsafe globally. The FFI boundary became the session-owned BYTES facade `VerterHost::project_node_to_type_expr_json_bytes` (mints the capability + materializes + unwraps + serializes to wire JSON internally; NAPI wraps the bytes in a `Buffer`, WASM does `String::from_utf8` — schema byte-identical, functionally identical); the old `pub fn project_node_to_type_expr` and the all-`pub`-field `MaterializedTypeExpr` struct are DELETED. The raw `raise_node_to_type_expr` primitive STAYS module-private; the reduce-then-raise orchestrator `raise_and_reduce_with_context` STAYS `pub(super)`; the shell output seam `output_shell_raise_sealed` returns a SEALED `Option<OutputTypeExpr>` (never a bare `TypeExpr`) so a `project_semantic_dispatch` sibling reaching the `pub(super)` seam cannot launder. The fence SHAPE is pinned by mechanism-matched guards over that trusted surface (a CLOSED structural allowlist, complete-by-construction): the EXACT module topology of the owner file — inline `projector` / `projector::sealed` / `carrier` / `carrier::payload` and nothing else, with item/impl/trait-position macro invocations, `include!`, unknown attributes, a `sealed::Sealed` alias `use`, and any owner-file `TypeExpr` alias BANNED — plus the sanctioned sink set (the explicit `impl OutputProjector` / `impl sealed::Sealed` self-types, compared by FULL self-type path as a MULTISET so a duplicate / last-ident-colliding registration is caught) by `output_projector_owner_registration_inventory`; a closed item/signature allowlist over the carrier/payload vault (every fn returning `TypeExpr` must be capability-gated or exactly test-gated) by `output_carriers_have_no_inherent_typeexpr_escape_method`; every carrier/payload struct field private regardless of spelled type by `output_carrier_payload_fields_are_private`; an accidental-regression CANARY for the common `Deref` / `AsRef` / `Borrow` trait escapes (NOT proof-complete — completeness for the unbounded escape-trait surface comes from the payload vault) in `project_semantic_dispatch/output_materialization_guards.rs`; the out-of-crate visibility boundary by the trybuild `output_projector_non_owner_impl_is_compiler_sealed`; the mintable `TestOutputCap` staying `#[cfg(test)]`-gated by `test_output_cap_not_visible_or_mintable_in_non_test_builds`; the terminal-sink mint scope by `output_cap_mint_scope_is_per_leaf_not_subtree` — a Rust-VISIBILITY reachable-module-tree model: for every `mint: pub(in P)` it builds the production module tree at P-and-below (excluding `#[cfg(test)]` modules) and default-DENIES any reachable module not on the cap's exact sink-module allowlist (a new non-sink descendant fails WITHOUT a denylist entry), paired with the walker self-test `mint_scope_module_tree_walker_self_test_discriminates`; the carrier `_for_test` gate by `carrier_for_test_accessors_are_test_support_gated_not_debug_assertions`; the sealed raise seam by `raise_output_seam_returns_sealed_carrier_not_bare_type_expr` (recursing non-test modules + transitive `TypeExpr` aliases) — STRENGTHENED at 8-A4 to assert ZERO public/restricted `raise.rs` bare-`TypeExpr` fns, no sanctioned bridge exception remaining.

371-docs/arch/refactor/rev11/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md:5049:docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md:56:| **GI-8** | banner validator | The canonical fence performs the check mechanically: it extracts the banner region structurally (between the CLI's two `----` rules), requires the region to be CLOSED, matches model and effort WHOLE-LINE, and fails the leg on mismatch — a substituted reviewer is refused, not merely noticed. **An earlier draft of this row claimed a reformatted banner "fails rather than passes"; that was FALSE and the review caught it.** With only the opening rule present, the awk scan ran to EOF, so the whole transcript — prompt echo included — became "the banner region", and the echoed policy lines satisfied both greps while the real banner read `cheap-substituted`. The fence now requires a CLOSED region, requires it to carry the banner's structural keys (`workdir:`/`provider:`/`sandbox:`/`session id:`), and requires exactly one `model:`/`reasoning effort:` line inside it. **It is still not spoof-proof, and the fence says so:** it scrapes a stream that also contains the echoed prompt, so a sufficiently banner-shaped block in the prompt plus a malformed real banner defeats it. Two further attempts to close it by text alone both failed under review — and one of them (anchoring on "the first line is a rule") was factually wrong about the CLI, which prints `Reading prompt from stdin...` and a version line first, so it REJECTED EVERY REAL LEG until it was actually run. That is the row's own justification, twice over: a check whose failure modes are understood only by its author is not a validator, and text-scraping a contaminated stream is the wrong substrate for a gate. 1034-
1035-### Fix Quality
1036-
1037-When encountering issues during implementation:
1038-- If the correct fix aligns with the architecture → implement it properly
1039-- Never apply a dirty fix that contradicts architectural rules just to make tests pass
1040:- If the proper fix is outside approved scope, do not apply a workaround and do not use a `TODO` as its disposition. Route the finding through the applicable scope authority and record `ADOPT-NOW`, `DEFER`, or `REJECT` before related work continues. A `TODO` may reference an approved debt row but never replaces it.
1041-
1042:**Explicit finding disposition.** Every scope-deviating correctness finding is dispositioned before related work continues as `ADOPT-NOW`, `DEFER`, or `REJECT`. `ADOPT-NOW` records the scope and acceptance-contract change. `DEFER` requires a codex-DEFER ruling and a debt row naming the durable owner block, the resolution gate no later than plan close, the acceptance ID/test, and the ruling reference. `REJECT` records evidence and rationale. A TODO, a feedback entry, or an ephemeral agent identity is not a disposition; plan close requires zero open deferrals. Enforcement is judgment — codex at the scope consult, and the plan-close zero-open-deferral check.
1043-
1044-### Stub Prevention (CRITICAL)
1045-
1046-Do not use empty test bodies, trivially-passing stubs, or "deferred to follow-up commit" placeholders to satisfy a named contract — a gate check, a characterization test, a plan invariant, a review obligation, a declared completion criterion. A stub that happens to pass is a gate-bypass, not a pass.

4747-.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:1100:- **Hash-then-lower slice nodes** (`crates/verter_session/src/cache_runtime/flow_slice_node.rs`) — `FlowSliceHashNode` plans + folds exactly the selected subgraph into the opaque `FlowSliceHash` (no byte export, `Debug` redacted; sole constructor `compute_flow_slice_hash`), then `FlowSliceLoweredBodyNode` lowers ONLY the plan into the arena-free `FlowSliceIR` (each `FlowSlot` carries its binding-identifier span — the declaration-precise slot identity the content lowering gates on; the slice hash stays span-free). The hash-then-lower split is TWO rails: the type-state pins hash-before-lowered-KEY (the lowered store is unaddressable without a minted hash), and the per-thread `compute_flow_slice_hash_thread_invocations` counter behaviorally pins that the lowered COMPUTE performs zero hash computations (the type system cannot — the hasher is a public producer); the counter, its accessor, and its increment are gated behind `verter_semantic`'s `test-support` feature (enabled by `verter_session`'s dev-dependency edge — `#[cfg(test)]` cannot serve a cross-crate consumer), so production builds compile the hasher without the TLS or the increment. Keys carry the per-function body-sensitive, cosmetic-insensitive `flow_body_stable_hash` (from the per-file `FunctionProgramIndex`), NOT `parse_stable_hash` — PLUS the EXACT per-function byte hash `flow_body_exact_hash`. Both nodes publish content-addressed artifacts with EMPTY fact rails — slice identity is never a warm-validity oracle — and "the key IS the validity oracle" holds only because TWO things are true together: the key carries that exact byte axis, and the artifacts carry NO absolute source position. That second half is a TYPE, not a convention: every span in `FunctionBodySkeleton` — and therefore in `FlowSliceIR` — is a `FrameSpan` (`verter_semantic::analysis::flow::frame_span`), a private-field newtype whose only constructor from a source position is `FrameSpan::rebase(anchor, span)` and whose only way back is `FrameSpan::to_absolute(anchor)`. `SkeletonBuilder::frame_span` is the ingress crossing (so `finish` is a plain MOVE with no per-family rebase pass to apply to five families and forget on two — which is exactly what happened: the read and call footprints kept ABSOLUTE offsets, and `lower_slice_plan`'s source-order effect sort mixed the two coordinate systems, ordering every call after every write at any non-zero anchor); `Lowerer::rebase` is the one crossing on the consumer side, and `FrameSpan::to_absolute` has exactly one caller (the parameter inventory comparing stored binding positions against live default-initializer offsets). A mixed comparison — `frame.start < absolute.start`, or a sort keyed off one of each — does not COMPILE. That claim was one accessor away from false: `FrameSpan::start()` / `::end()` were `pub fn -> u32` with ZERO production callers (one test), so the comparison the module exists to forbid was writable in the module that forbids it. They are deleted; `FrameSpan` now exposes no offset at all, and every consumer comparison is `FrameSpan`-to-`FrameSpan` (`contains`, the derived `Ord`). Two things stay CONVENTIONS and the module now says so instead of implying otherwise: the anchor is a bare `u32` on both crossings, so `rebase(0, absolute)` still mints a `FrameSpan` holding an absolute offset and `to_absolute(wrong_anchor)` still lands somewhere (nothing pairs a `FrameSpan` with its anchor — it outlives the file version it was recorded on, which is exactly why the anchor is re-supplied at egress); and the derived `Ord` / `Hash` let two frames' spans compare without either frame being named (harmless because every artifact here is per-function). `SkeletonRead` carries no span at all: the reference position had no consumer, and dead state is where a stale coordinate hides. Acceptance: `skeleton_is_invariant_under_the_function_position`, `lowered_ir_is_invariant_under_the_function_position`, `lower_orders_effects_by_authored_position_at_any_anchor` (the predecessor of the last read `span.start` back off the result and asserted it ascended — the same key the lowering had just sorted on, over a fixture at offset 0 where both systems coincide, so it held by construction and passed while the invariant was violated). Each half covers a blind spot the other cannot: `flow_body_stable_hash` is an AST fold, so it is blind to a leading blank line (which moves every absolute position and is fixed by the relative anchoring) AND, because it alpha-normalizes binding/reference identifiers, blind to a local rename that shifts every position INSIDE the body (which relative anchoring does NOT survive and only the exact byte axis catches). The exact axis is deliberately per-FUNCTION, not the file's content hash, so an edit to a sibling function leaves an untouched function's artifacts warm. Acceptance: `flow_bundle_reuse_is_sound_for_every_content_its_key_admits`, `the_two_shift_edits_are_invisible_to_flow_body_stable_hash`.
4748-.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:1101:- **`SemanticQueryKey::FlowReturn`** — the ONE dispatch arm (`project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs`): key = content-free function slot + normalized type args + `FlowReturnContext` (all five env dims) + `ReturnProjectionDemand` + `FlowInputContext`. The published memo entry records `satisfied_projection` — the materialized point set the compute ACTUALLY produced (§3.4 lattice-relation satisfaction; `semantic_query_memo/flow_return_memo.rs` `cached_satisfies` decides warm hits against the REQUESTED point, never nominal demand). Warm validity roots on the sole `ProgramAnalysisFactRef::FlowBody` rail (function identity + `flow_body_stable_hash`, validated fail-closed by `StoreView::validates_program_analysis_domain`); the subplan's separate `FlowSlice` DISCRIMINANT fact does not exist on this tree (ratified C7 divergence — `FlowSlice` never enters `ReadSetSignature.facts`). Success carries `FlowReturnResult { return_type, can_fall_through, degradation }`: a degraded success (modeled-`any` substitution, typed `FlowReturnDegradation` — `NonCallableBinding`, `UnrepresentableCallee`, `FailedBindingInitializer`, the fail-closed `UnappliedWriteEffect` for a slice carrying a whole-slot write effect into a parameter or value-selected slot the evaluator does not apply, the fail-closed `ConditionalVarDefinition` for an observed function-scoped `var` whose surviving reaching definition was recorded inside a conditional arm, the fail-closed `UnreducedDeclaredUnion` for an annotated declarator whose DECLARED union could not be reduced to the constituents its initializer selects, the POSITIONAL `UnmodeledPosition` for a sub-expression whose resolver is a named downstream block, or `UnresolvedValue`) RETURNS through the success carrier but is `ReturnOnly` (never warmed). **The EVALUATION is the authority on its own degradation; the construction-time fold is a BACKSTOP, and the two deciding fields (`return_type`, `degradation`) are PRIVATE so neither can be bypassed** (`can_fall_through` is `pub` — a plain reachability bit no admission channel reads). `FlowReturnResult::new` is the sole construction point: it takes the evaluation's own observed reason and additionally consults `SemanticGraphStore::node_reaches_unresolved` (`semantic_query_memo/unresolved_reach.rs`), folding `UnresolvedValue` in when the value reaches a semantic-miss carrier (`QueryError::means_type_is_not_yet_known`). That verdict is a MEMOIZED INDUCTIVE BIT over the hash-consed immutable graph — `self_bit(n) || any(bit(child))`, decided once per node id, O(1) amortized at every later read. It carries NO budget, because a bound whose trip reports "unresolved" computes a DIFFERENT function: a 4,100-arm literal union with zero misses is fully known, and stamping it `UnresolvedValue` propagates a factually false permanent warm refusal into every enclosing result. The walk descends only structure the evaluation composes or lowers inline (`Union`/`Intersection`, `Object` members + signatures + index signatures + keyspace, `ObjectSpreadProgram`, `Array`/`Tuple`, `TemplateLiteral`, `KeyOf`/`IndexedAccess`/`Mapped`, `Conditional`, `Signature`, `InstantiationRef` args, `Alias`, and the three carriers' type ARGUMENTS through the sanctioned `carrier_type_args` accessor) and STOPS at every shallow carrier (`DeclRef`, `MergedDecl`, `BareRef`, `ImportType`, `TypeOf`) — descending one would be materialisation, and a miss inside a referenced declaration is that declaration's own admission problem. Its match over `SemanticNodeData` is wildcard-free (and covers struct FIELDS a variant match does not — `MapperKey::parameter_node` is a descent), an unresolvable node id answers "unresolved" (fail closed), `RawFallback` is not-known (agreeing with `SemanticNodeData::means_type_is_not_yet_known`, which is the reconciliation of the two classifications), and a deferred `BareRef` is explicitly NOT a miss. Without it, `function f(x: HasQ) { return x.q }` published `Opaque(Miss)` with `degradation: None` and `slot_candidate_count == 1` — a complete, warm answer with an opaque interior, so `execute_function_return_source` never folded the cache-read rails and every enclosing composition warmed around it; the same shape reached admission from FOUR independent ingress paths (the `FrameShadowed` arm, the free-leaf arm, a composed object member, and a leaf lowering's own `Array`/`Signature` interior), which is why the fold exists at all. The AUTHORITY, however, is the compute: a construction-time walk cannot see a fabricated `any` (a value cannot distinguish a fabricated `any` from an authored one), so a position whose resolver is a named downstream block RECORDS `UnmodeledPosition` where it stands and contributes the typed unresolved marker, and the fold catches only the residue no position observed. Acceptance: `a_value_reaching_a_miss_carrier_is_never_admitted_warm` + the over-degradation discriminator `a_deferred_carrier_and_a_resolved_composition_still_admit_warm`; no-value outcomes are typed `FlowReturnFailure`s through `ReturnOnly`; `FlowSliceBudget` refusals are non-admitted at every layer (planner refusal → no hash entry → unaddressable lowered store → no memo candidate). At the ONE sealed consumer entry (`execute_function_return_source`), the outcome routes through ONE exhaustive `FunctionReturnNode::consumer_fold` classification — no `degradation.is_some()` condition AT THAT ENTRY, and no second call site. (The bit is still read elsewhere, for questions that are not the consumer's fold: `flow_return.rs`'s own admission gate, `scc_publish.rs`'s component-wide publication gate, and `tsc_projection.rs`'s inferred-class-member row.) `consumer_fold()` is called from inside the `Flow` source arm ALONE (the `Declared` / `Absent` source arms return before reaching it), so only `Flow(_)` and `NoValue(_)` are LIVE there; `Declared` / `Absent` / `DeclaredMiss` are classified for the TYPE, not for a live call. A degraded success KEEPS its value and folds BOTH rails (`ConsumerFold::Partial(reasons)`), and so does a NO-VALUE outcome (`NoValue` / `DeclaredMiss`): the request-partial sticky gating component-meta/shape/materialize warm, plus the build-local `result_is_partial`/`cache_suppress` taint. `Declared` / `Absent` / a clean `Flow` are `ConsumerFold::Clean`. The carried `reasons` are derived per-OUTCOME, not per-arm — `degradation_reason_class` for a degraded success and `failure_reason_class` for a no-value failure — so a budget edge or a torn view is never folded under an inference-gap class.

5343-   572	
5344-   573	### Fix Quality
5345-   574	
5346-   575	When encountering issues during implementation:
5347-   576	- If the correct fix aligns with the architecture → implement it properly
5348-   577	- Never apply a dirty fix that contradicts architectural rules just to make tests pass
5349:   578	- If the proper fix is outside approved scope, do not apply a workaround and do not use a `TODO` as its disposition. Route the finding through the applicable scope authority and record `ADOPT-NOW`, `DEFER`, or `REJECT` before related work continues. A `TODO` may reference an approved debt row but never replaces it.
5350-   579	
5351:   580	**Explicit finding disposition.** Every scope-deviating correctness finding is dispositioned before related work continues as `ADOPT-NOW`, `DEFER`, or `REJECT`. `ADOPT-NOW` records the scope and acceptance-contract change. `DEFER` requires a codex-DEFER ruling and a debt row naming the durable owner block, the resolution gate no later than plan close, the acceptance ID/test, and the ruling reference. `REJECT` records evidence and rationale. A TODO, a feedback entry, or an ephemeral agent identity is not a disposition; plan close requires zero open deferrals. Enforcement is judgment — codex at the scope consult, and the plan-close zero-open-deferral check.
5352-   581	
5353-   582	### Stub Prevention (CRITICAL)
5354-   583	
5355-   584	Do not use empty test bodies, trivially-passing stubs, or "deferred to follow-up commit" placeholders to satisfy a named contract — a gate check, a characterization test, a plan invariant, a review obligation, a declared completion criterion. A stub that happens to pass is a gate-bypass, not a pass.

     1	//! Batched input-loading contract types: `AttemptOutcome<T>` / `LoadSet`.
     2	//!
     3	//! Per `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4: the
     4	//! compiler, resolver, `TypeInfo`, flow, and reusable query kernels consume
     5	//! one immutable observation view per attempt and perform no hidden
     6	//! filesystem/network/process/package-manager I/O. A kernel operation that
     7	//! cannot complete against its current snapshot returns
     8	//! `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` describing exactly what is missing,
     9	//! rather than blocking the calling thread.
    10	//!
    11	//! These types are new, inert vocabulary (contract-conformant but not yet
    12	//! wired into any resolver call site) — see the sequencing recorded at
    13	//! `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/scoping-spec.md` §4, step 1.
    14	//! They are a *different* envelope from
    15	//! [`crate::query::QueryResult`]'s `Completeness`/`missing_inputs` shape,
    16	//! which reports public query-result completeness, not kernel retry
    17	//! signaling — the two must not be merged.
    18	
    19	use std::collections::BTreeSet;

    26	/// depending on that crate — `verter_semantic` sits below `verter_session`
    27	/// in the dependency graph and must not name it.
    28	pub type CanonicalId = Arc<str>;

    30	/// Which lowering space a [`InputKey::DeclBody`] demand targets.
    31	///
    32	/// Added per F19
    33	/// (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/f19-deviation-consult.md`): a
    34	/// bare `(canonical, owner, name)` `DeclBody` key cannot tell a retry
    35	/// driver whether [`crate::resolver_core::ResolverObservation::type_decl`]
    36	/// or [`crate::resolver_core::ResolverObservation::value_decl`] produced

    52	/// fabricating semantic answers"). Adding a variant is a deliberate
    53	/// widening of the observation surface, not a per-caller extension point.

   240	    /// `NeedInputs`), but a useful zero value for accumulation.

   265	    #[must_use]
   266	    pub fn delta(&self, accumulated_requested: &BTreeSet<InputKey>) -> Vec<InputKey> {
   267	        self.keys

   270	            .cloned()
   271	            .collect()
   272	    }

   306	/// Typed resource/progress failures (contract §8) — distinct from a bare
   307	/// bool/`Option` "gave up" signal so callers can report unresolved keys and
   308	/// consumed budget without exposing sensitive ambient paths beyond the
   309	/// product's diagnostic policy.
   310	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   311	pub enum AttemptFailure {
   312	    /// Contract §4 step 5: `delta` was empty and neither the resolution
   313	    /// basis nor any previously observed fact changed.
   314	    InputResolutionNoProgress { unresolved: Vec<InputKey> },
   315	    InputResolutionAttemptLimit {
   316	        unresolved: Vec<InputKey>,
   317	        attempts: u32,
   318	    },
   319	    InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit {
   320	        unresolved: Vec<InputKey>,
   321	        unique_keys: u32,
   322	    },
   323	    InputResolutionByteLimit {
   324	        unresolved: Vec<InputKey>,
   325	        bytes: u64,
   326	    },
   327	    InputResolutionDepthLimit {
   328	        unresolved: Vec<InputKey>,
   329	        depth: u32,
   330	    },
   331	    InputResolutionChurnLimit {
   332	        unresolved: Vec<InputKey>,
   333	        churn: u32,
   334	    },
   335	    /// A same-key I/O flight reported a transient (non-stable-missing)
   336	    /// failure — contract §4 step 7, §7: transient permission/network/
   337	    /// process/provider failure is never cached as stable missing.
   338	    InputLoadUnavailable { key: InputKey },
   339	    /// Conditional commit (contract §4 step 8-9) lost the race past the
   340	    /// configured churn/retry budget.
   341	    InputCommitConflictExceeded { retries: u32 },
   342	    /// A driver was asked for an observation outside its own populated
   343	    /// capability subset — F19's `ObservationUnavailable` widening (see
   344	    /// [`ResolverObservationKind`]'s docs). Never itself a `NeedInputs`
   345	    /// signal: the driver genuinely cannot answer, keyed or not, so the
   346	    /// caller must fall back to a different attempt view/driver rather
   347	    /// than retry.
   348	    ObservationUnavailable {
   349	        observation: ResolverObservationKind,
   350	    },
   351	}

   353	impl AttemptFailure {
   354	    /// Whether this terminal means the input-resolution work envelope was
   355	    /// exhausted before the attempt could prove its answer.
   356	    #[must_use]
   357	    pub fn is_input_resolution_limit(&self) -> bool {
   358	        matches!(
   359	            self,
   360	            Self::InputResolutionAttemptLimit { .. }
   361	                | Self::InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit { .. }
   362	                | Self::InputResolutionByteLimit { .. }
   363	                | Self::InputResolutionDepthLimit { .. }
   364	                | Self::InputResolutionChurnLimit { .. }
   365	        )
   366	    }
   367	}

   369	/// Per-attempt outcome of a non-flow kernel operation (contract §2).
   370	///
   371	/// `Complete`/`NeedInputs`/`Terminal` are exhaustive and closed: a kernel
   372	/// method returning this type can never block the calling thread — the
   373	/// only way to signal "not yet answerable" is `NeedInputs(LoadSet)`.
   374	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   375	pub enum AttemptOutcome<T> {
   376	    Complete(T),
   377	    NeedInputs(LoadSet),
   378	    Terminal(AttemptFailure),
   379	}
   380	
   381	impl<T> AttemptOutcome<T> {
   382	    /// Maps the `Complete` payload, leaving `NeedInputs`/`Terminal` as-is.
   383	    pub fn map<U>(self, f: impl FnOnce(T) -> U) -> AttemptOutcome<U> {
   384	        match self {
   385	            Self::Complete(value) => AttemptOutcome::Complete(f(value)),
   386	            Self::NeedInputs(load_set) => AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set),
   387	            Self::Terminal(failure) => AttemptOutcome::Terminal(failure),
   388	        }
   389	    }
   390	
   391	    #[must_use]
   392	    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
   393	        matches!(self, Self::Complete(_))
   394	    }
   395	
   396	    #[must_use]
   397	    pub fn is_need_inputs(&self) -> bool {
   398	        matches!(self, Self::NeedInputs(_))
   399	    }
   400	
   401	    #[must_use]
   402	    pub fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
   403	        matches!(self, Self::Terminal(_))
   404	    }
   405	
   406	    /// Extracts the `Complete` payload, discarding `NeedInputs`/`Terminal`.
   407	    #[must_use]
   408	    pub fn complete(self) -> Option<T> {
   409	        match self {
   410	            Self::Complete(value) => Some(value),
   411	            Self::NeedInputs(_) | Self::Terminal(_) => None,
   412	        }
   413	    }
   414	}

   416	/// A successfully completed kernel attempt's answer, paired with the
   417	/// [`crate::resolver_core::AttemptOutput`] it accumulated along the way.
   418	///
   419	/// Exactly the shape F16
   420	/// (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/f16-deviation-consult.md`)
   421	/// designed `AttemptOutput` to eventually feed and F19
   422	/// (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/f19-deviation-consult.md`)
   423	/// named as part of item 3's first implementation step.
   424	/// `AttemptOutcome::Complete(T)` itself stays UNCHANGED — this wrapper
   425	/// exists at the TOP-LEVEL kernel entry point ([`KernelAttempt`]), not on
   426	/// [`ResolverObservation`]'s 13 inbound query methods, which have no
   427	/// outbound effects of their own to accumulate.
   428	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   429	pub struct CompletedAttempt<T> {
   430	    pub value: T,
   431	    pub output: crate::resolver_core::AttemptOutput,
   432	}
   433	
   434	impl<T> CompletedAttempt<T> {
   435	    #[must_use]
   436	    pub const fn new(value: T, output: crate::resolver_core::AttemptOutput) -> Self {
   437	        Self { value, output }
   438	    }
   439	}

   441	/// The top-level kernel attempt envelope: [`AttemptOutcome`] specialized
   442	/// so a successful attempt carries its accumulated
   443	/// [`crate::resolver_core::AttemptOutput`] alongside the answer.
   444	/// `NeedInputs`/`Terminal` carry no output — an attempt that does not
   445	/// reach `Complete` discards everything it accumulated (contract §4: no
   446	/// torn/partial output is ever promoted).
   447	pub type KernelAttempt<T> = AttemptOutcome<CompletedAttempt<T>>;

     1	//! The capability-limited, immutable observation interface (C1-AC-5,
     2	//! C1-AC-7).
     3	//!
     4	//! Per `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md` and F3 of
     5	//! `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/scoping-spec.md`, this trait is a
     6	//! genuinely NEW, separate sealed trait — it does NOT extend
     7	//! `verter_session::resolver_core::ResolverContext` and cannot name
     8	//! `VerterHost` or any scheduler type, because `verter_semantic`'s
     9	//! dependency closure cannot reach those types (they live in a crate that
    10	//! depends on this one, never the reverse).
    11	//!
    12	//! Every method returns [`crate::resolver_core::AttemptOutcome`] — never a
    13	//! bare value, a `Result`, or a call that can block. This is the structural
    14	//! mechanism C1-AC-5 relies on: a method added later that does not return
    15	//! `AttemptOutcome<T>` fails to compile, rather than being a gap a sampled
    16	//! test could miss.
    17	//!
    18	//! Real methods grow onto this trait per
    19	//! `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/C1/disposition-table.md` —
    20	//! ONLY once a method's return type and I/O-vs-immediate shape are
    21	//! confirmed dependency-neutral in that table (F8/F9's explicit
    22	//! instruction: no method lands ahead of its disposition-table row
    23	//! closing). This is deliberately a PARTIAL surface — most of
    24	//! `project_semantic_dispatch`'s 23 `ResolverContext` methods are not
    25	//! covered yet; see the disposition table's "not yet audited" list.

    36	/// Private marker `ResolverObservation` is sealed against. Only types

    39	///
    40	/// `pub(crate)` (not fully private) so a sibling module within
    41	/// `verter_semantic` — e.g. [`crate::resolver_core::ResolverAttemptView`]

    43	/// EXTERNAL crates: `pub(crate)` is still crate-restricted, so an

    46	/// This is a SEPARATE seal from `verter_session::resolver_core`'s

    48	/// authority, not a shared hierarchy (F3).
    49	pub(crate) mod sealed {

    89	    /// project root claims the file.
    90	    fn workspace_is_package_backed(&self, canonical: &str) -> AttemptOutcome<bool>;
    91	
    92	    /// Ambient-library declaration lookup for `symbol`, scoped to
    93	    /// `consumer_project`. Disposition-table row: confirmed
    94	    /// dependency-neutral (`AmbientSymbolHit`/`ProjectStableKey` are plain

   112	fn load_requested_inputs(
   113	    inputs: &mut ResolutionInputs,
   114	    keys: &[InputKey],
   115	    mut snapshot_path_probe: impl FnMut(
   116	        &str,
   117	    ) -> (verter_semantic::resolver_core::PathProbe, Vec<String>),
   118	    mut snapshot_realpath: impl FnMut(&str) -> (Option<String>, Vec<String>),
   119	    mut snapshot_package_manifest: impl FnMut(
   120	        &str,
   121	    )
   122	        -> (Option<crate::types::PackageManifest>, Vec<String>),
   123	) -> Result<bool, Box<InputKey>> {
   124	    let mut progressed = false;
   125	    for key in keys {
   126	        match key {
   127	            InputKey::PathProbe { path } => {
   128	                let (value, directories) = snapshot_path_probe(path);
   129	                progressed |= !inputs.snapshot.contains_path_probe(path);
   130	                Arc::make_mut(&mut inputs.snapshot).insert_path_probe(path.to_string(), value);
   131	                inputs
   132	                    .observation_inputs
   133	                    .insert(key.clone(), SnapshotInput::PathProbe { directories });
   134	            }
   135	            InputKey::RealPath { path } => {
   136	                let (value, directories) = snapshot_realpath(path);
   137	                progressed |= !inputs.snapshot.contains_real_path(path);
   138	                Arc::make_mut(&mut inputs.snapshot)
   139	                    .insert_real_path(path.to_string(), value.map(Arc::from));
   140	                inputs
   141	                    .observation_inputs
   142	                    .insert(key.clone(), SnapshotInput::RealPath { directories });
   143	            }
   144	            InputKey::PackageManifest { directory } => {
   145	                let manifest_path =
   146	                    verter_semantic::resolver_core::join_paths(directory, "package.json");
   147	                let (manifest, directories) = snapshot_package_manifest(&manifest_path);
   148	                let fingerprint = manifest
   149	                    .as_ref()
   150	                    .map(crate::resolution_currency::manifest_fingerprint_of);
   151	                let value = manifest.map(|manifest| {
   152	                    Arc::new(ResolutionPackageManifest {
   153	                        main: manifest.main,
   154	                        module: manifest.module,
   155	                        types: manifest.types,
   156	                        typings: manifest.typings,
   157	                        exports: manifest.exports,
   158	                        imports: manifest.imports,
   159	                    })
   160	                });
   161	                progressed |= !inputs.snapshot.contains_package_manifest(directory);
   162	                Arc::make_mut(&mut inputs.snapshot)
   163	                    .insert_package_manifest(directory.to_string(), value);
   164	                inputs.observation_inputs.insert(
   165	                    key.clone(),
   166	                    SnapshotInput::PackageManifest {
   167	                        fingerprint,
   168	                        directories,
   169	                        manifest_path,
   170	                    },
   171	                );
   172	            }
   173	            _ => return Err(Box::new(key.clone())),
   174	        }
   175	    }
   176	    Ok(progressed)
   177	}

   208	fn apply_attempt_output(
   209	    reader: &crate::resolution_currency::TransactionReader<'_>,
   210	    inputs: &ResolutionInputs,
   211	    output: &AttemptOutput,
   212	) -> bool {
   213	    verter_debug_assert::verter_debug_assert!(output.observed_facts().is_empty());
   214	    verter_debug_assert::verter_debug_assert!(output.ambient_dependencies().is_empty());
   215	
   216	    for observation in output.consumed_resolution_observations() {
   217	        match observation {
   218	            ConsumedResolutionObservationKey::PathProbe { path } => {
   219	                let key = InputKey::PathProbe {
   220	                    path: Arc::clone(path),
   221	                };
   222	                let Some(SnapshotInput::PathProbe { directories }) =
   223	                    inputs.observation_inputs.get(&key)
   224	                else {
   225	                    return false;
   226	                };
   227	                let Some(value) = inputs.snapshot.path_probe(path) else {
   228	                    return false;
   229	                };
   230	                reader.record_snapshot_directories(directories);
   231	                reader.record_snapshot_canonical_path(path, value);
   232	            }
   233	            ConsumedResolutionObservationKey::RealPath { path } => {
   234	                let key = InputKey::RealPath {
   235	                    path: Arc::clone(path),
   236	                };
   237	                let Some(SnapshotInput::RealPath { directories }) =
   238	                    inputs.observation_inputs.get(&key)
   239	                else {
   240	                    return false;
   241	                };
   242	                let Some(value) = inputs.snapshot.real_path(path) else {
   243	                    return false;
   244	                };
   245	                reader.record_snapshot_directories(directories);
   246	                reader.record_snapshot_canonical_realpath(path, value.as_deref());
   247	            }
   248	            ConsumedResolutionObservationKey::PackageManifest { directory } => {
   249	                let key = InputKey::PackageManifest {
   250	                    directory: Arc::clone(directory),
   251	                };
   252	                let Some(SnapshotInput::PackageManifest {
   253	                    fingerprint,
   254	                    directories,
   255	                    manifest_path,
   256	                }) = inputs.observation_inputs.get(&key)
   257	                else {
   258	                    return false;
   259	                };
   260	                reader.record_snapshot_directories(directories);
   261	                reader.record_snapshot_canonical_manifest(manifest_path, *fingerprint);
   262	            }
   263	            ConsumedResolutionObservationKey::RecoveryScope { canonical_prefix } => {
   264	                reader.record_snapshot_canonical_recovery_scope(canonical_prefix);
   265	            }
   266	        }
   267	    }
   268	    true
   269	}

   282	pub(crate) fn drive_attempt<T>(
   283	    reader: &dyn crate::traits::WorkspaceRead,
   284	    mut load_requested_inputs: impl FnMut(
   285	        &mut ResolutionInputs,
   286	        &[InputKey],
   287	    ) -> Result<bool, Box<InputKey>>,
   288	    mut apply_attempt_output: impl FnMut(&ResolutionInputs, &AttemptOutput) -> bool,
   289	    mut run: impl FnMut(&ResolverAttemptView, ResolutionBasis) -> KernelAttempt<T>,
   290	) -> Result<T, Box<AttemptFailure>> {
   291	    let mut active_basis = None;
   292	    let mut inputs = ResolutionInputs::default();
   293	    let mut requested = Vec::new();
   294	    let mut delta = Vec::new();
   295	    let mut last_load_set: Option<LoadSet> = None;
   296	    let mut last_load_failure = None;
   297	
   298	    for _ in 0..INPUT_RESOLUTION_ATTEMPT_LIMIT {
   299	        let basis = crate::resolution_currency::resolution_basis_for_reader(reader)
   300	            .unwrap_or_else(ResolutionBasis::unbound_placeholder);
   301	        if active_basis != Some(basis) {
   302	            active_basis = Some(basis);
   303	            inputs = ResolutionInputs::default();
   304	            requested.clear();
   305	            last_load_set = None;
   306	            last_load_failure = None;
   307	        }
   308	        let view = attempt_view(&inputs, basis);
   309	        let outcome = run(&view, basis);
   310	        drop(view);
   311	        match outcome {
   312	            AttemptOutcome::Complete(completed) => {
   313	                #[cfg(test)]
   314	                crate::engine::resolution_test_hooks::fire(
   315	                    crate::engine::resolution_test_hooks::ResolutionPhase::ProviderProjection,
   316	                );
   317	                if !apply_attempt_output(&inputs, &completed.output) {
   318	                    return Err(Box::new(AttemptFailure::InputResolutionNoProgress {
   319	                        unresolved: last_load_set
   320	                            .as_ref()
   321	                            .map_or_else(Vec::new, |load_set| copy_terminal_keys(load_set.keys())),
   322	                    }));
   323	                }
   324	                return Ok(completed.value);
   325	            }
   326	            AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set) => {
   327	                if load_set.basis() != basis {
   328	                    last_load_set = Some(load_set);
   329	                    active_basis = None;
   330	                    continue;
   331	                }
   332	                delta.clear();
   333	                #[cfg(test)]
   334	                let had_delta_capacity = delta.capacity() != 0;
   335	                delta.extend(
   336	                    load_set
   337	                        .keys()
   338	                        .iter()
   339	                        .filter(|key| !requested.contains(*key))
   340	                        .cloned(),
   341	                );
   342	                #[cfg(test)]
   343	                if !had_delta_capacity && !delta.is_empty() {
   344	                    DRIVER_DELTA_MATERIALIZATIONS.set(DRIVER_DELTA_MATERIALIZATIONS.get() + 1);
   345	                }
   346	                if delta.is_empty() {
   347	                    return Err(Box::new(AttemptFailure::InputResolutionNoProgress {
   348	                        unresolved: copy_terminal_keys(load_set.keys()),
   349	                    }));
   350	                }
   351	                match load_requested_inputs(&mut inputs, &delta) {
   352	                    Ok(true) => {
   353	                        requested.append(&mut delta);
   354	                        last_load_failure = None;
   355	                    }
   356	                    Ok(false) => {
   357	                        last_load_failure = delta.first().cloned();
   358	                    }
   359	                    Err(key) => {
   360	                        last_load_failure = Some(*key);
   361	                    }
   362	                }
   363	                last_load_set = Some(load_set);
   364	            }
   365	            AttemptOutcome::Terminal(failure) => {
   366	                if failure.is_input_resolution_limit() {
   367	                    reader.note_resolution_budget_exhausted();
   368	                }
   369	                return Err(Box::new(failure));
   370	            }
   371	        }
   372	    }
   373	    match last_load_failure {
   374	        Some(key) => Err(Box::new(AttemptFailure::InputLoadUnavailable { key })),
   375	        None => {
   376	            reader.note_resolution_budget_exhausted();
   377	            Err(Box::new(AttemptFailure::InputResolutionAttemptLimit {
   378	                unresolved: last_load_set
   379	                    .as_ref()
   380	                    .map_or_else(Vec::new, |load_set| copy_terminal_keys(load_set.keys())),
   381	                attempts: INPUT_RESOLUTION_ATTEMPT_LIMIT,
   382	            }))
   383	        }
   384	    }
   385	}

   388	    #[cfg(test)]
   389	    DRIVER_TERMINAL_KEY_COPIES.set(DRIVER_TERMINAL_KEY_COPIES.get() + keys.len());
   390	    keys.to_vec()
   391	}

   393	pub(crate) fn resolve_tracked(
   394	    resolver: &ModuleResolverCore,
   395	    _capability: &crate::engine::TrackedResolutionCapability,
   396	    reader: &crate::resolution_currency::TransactionReader<'_>,

     1	#![deny(missing_docs)]
     2	//! Public host typeinfo substrate.
     3	//!
     4	//! Audited / non-audited host methods that expose the shallow-state
     5	//! symbol inventory and the dispatch-backed type evaluation surface
     6	//! to downstream consumers (the `@verter/typeinfo` TS package, MCP
     7	//! tools, IDE integrations).
     8	//!
     9	//! Public methods (the published surface of the typeinfo
    10	//! substrate):
    11	//!
    12	//! 1. [`crate::VerterHost::list_file_symbols`] — shallow read; no
    13	//!    audit.
    14	//! 2. [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_named_symbol`] /
    15	//!    [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_named_symbol_with_audit`] —
    16	//!    audited resolution of a named declaration with optional
    17	//!    generic instantiation.
    18	//! 3. [`crate::VerterHost::evaluate_type_expression_with_audit`] —
    19	//!    audited evaluation of a synthetic type expression in a
    20	//!    file scope, with an optional host-owned scratch cache.
    21	//! 4. [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_shallow_surface`] — resolves a
    22	//!    named declaration to its span-rich, one-level
    23	//!    [`surface::TypeInfoSurface`] (members + call / construct / index
    24	//!    signatures + the keyspace) WITHOUT expanding member bodies. The
    25	//!    shallow-by-default rule holds: each member `value` is a
    26	//!    reference-style node, never an eagerly expanded object. Every
    27	//!    span on the returned surface is a [`surface::CanonicalSpan`]
    28	//!    (byte offsets + the canonical declaration file), so a consumer
    29	//!    slices the source on demand at the FFI / consumer boundary —
    30	//!    the surface itself holds NO owned type / display strings.
    31	//!
    32	//! Sub-modules:
    33	//! - [`types`] — public DTOs (`SymbolEntry`, `EvaluateTypeExpressionRequest`, …).
    34	//! - [`symbol_inventory`] — `list_file_symbols` impl.
    35	//! - [`resolve_named_symbol`] — `resolve_named_symbol_with_audit` impl.
    36	//! - [`evaluate_type_expression`] — `evaluate_type_expression_with_audit` impl.
    37	//! - [`shallow_surface`] — `resolve_shallow_surface` impl.
    38	//! - [`surface`] — the span-rich [`surface::TypeInfoSurface`] projection.
    39	//! - [`scratch_cache`] — host-owned LRU for typeinfo scratch URIs.
    40

    55	// The output-sink capabilities for this subtree are defined PER-SINK in the
    56	// exact output-SINK modules that project — NOT subtree-wide:
    57	// `TypeinfoRaiseOutputCap` in `raise.rs`, `TypeinfoVueSurfaceOutputCap` in
    58	// `framework_surface/vue_exec/` (whose whole reachable scope — `vue_exec` +
    59	// its `normalize` child — is output-only, so the single cap is correct), and
    60	// `TypeinfoSvelteSurfaceOutputCap` in `framework_surface/svelte_exec.rs` (whose
    61	// only submodule is a `#[cfg(test)]` test module). A subtree-wide cap
    62	// (`pub(in crate::typeinfo)`) would let any `typeinfo` sibling (e.g. a future
    63	// `framework_surface::executor` raise-then-decide site) mint it; terminal-sink
    64	// minting (each mint scope's whole reachable production module tree is
    65	// output-only) makes the output-materialization fence compiler-enforced.
    66	
    67	/// Bounded number of times a typeinfo query-returner re-reads the base
    68	/// store view trying to settle on a proven-[`crate::resolver_store::StoreViewRead::Current`]
    69	/// snapshot under churn before reporting a non-current miss.
    70	///
    71	/// A typeinfo query-returner builds a request-bound dispatch context from
    72	/// the base store view and RETURNS the resolved node — there is no outer
    73	/// `run_stable_request` publish fence to suppress a stale answer. So it MUST
    74	/// resolve against a CURRENT snapshot: a `ReturnOnly` read means the manager
    75	/// could not prove the snapshot coherent, and computing the query against it
    76	/// would return a result derived from already-superseded dependency state.
    77	/// The retry budget mirrors the store-view manager's own bounded
    78	/// no-torn-snapshot retries — a transient mutation burst settles within a
    79	/// few rounds; sustained churn exhausts the budget and the query-returner
    80	/// surfaces a miss (`None`) rather than a stale answer.
    81	pub(crate) const TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS: usize = 3;
    82	
    83	/// Acquire a proven-[`crate::resolver_store::CurrentHostStoreView`] for a
    84	/// typeinfo query-returner, retrying a bounded number of times when the
    85	/// store-view manager hands back a known-stale
    86	/// [`crate::resolver_store::StoreViewRead::ReturnOnly`] read under churn.
    87	///
    88	/// Returns `None` when every attempt within
    89	/// [`TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`] observed a non-current read —
    90	/// the host is under sustained churn and the query CANNOT be answered
    91	/// against a coherent snapshot. `None` is the established typeinfo miss
    92	/// signal ("could not be resolved"): the FFI surface already maps it to a
    93	/// `null` payload, so the consumer re-queries on the next request once the
    94	/// host settles. The loop is bounded, so it always terminates — it never
    95	/// spins.
    96	#[must_use]
    97	pub(crate) fn current_store_view_for_query(
    98	    host: &crate::VerterHost,
    99	) -> Option<crate::resolver_store::CurrentHostStoreView> {
   100	    for _ in 0..TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS {
   101	        if let Some(current) = host.resolver_store_view_read().current() {
   102	            return Some(current);
   103	        }
   104	        // Non-current read: the manager could not prove this snapshot
   105	        // coherent. Re-read — a transient mutation burst settles within
   106	        // the bounded budget. No sleep / yield: the manager's own
   107	        // build_coherent retry already absorbs the contention window, and
   108	        // a tight bounded re-read keeps the path non-blocking.
   109	    }
   110	    None
   111	}

   130	// schema, identity derivation, admission gate, probe synthesis, hover
   131	// extraction, source-side walk, pure-data registry, and — under `oracle-gen` —
   132	// the tsgo-driving snapshot generator). Compiled in `test` mode (the lifted
   133	// unit-test rows consume it) AND under the `oracle-gen` feature (the
   134	// `src/bin/oracle_gen` generator reaches its `run_oracle_gen` entry — a
   135	// `src/bin/*` is a separate crate that sees only `pub`/`pub(crate)` lib items,
   136	// not the `#[cfg(test)]` `typeinfo_tests` tree). It declares no oracle rows
   137	// itself: it is the shared foundation the `TypeExpr`-projection oracle rows
   138	// consume. The tsgo driver lives behind
   139	// `oracle-gen` only, so the default resolver build + default test gate stay
   140	// tsgo-free (the `tsgo`-forbidden-at-runtime invariant, design §3 inv 1).
   141	#[cfg(any(test, feature = "oracle-gen"))]

     2	//! Public host typeinfo substrate.
     3	//!
     4	//! Audited / non-audited host methods that expose the shallow-state
     5	//! symbol inventory and the dispatch-backed type evaluation surface
     6	//! to downstream consumers (the `@verter/typeinfo` TS package, MCP
     7	//! tools, IDE integrations).
     8	//!
     9	//! Public methods (the published surface of the typeinfo
    10	//! substrate):
    11	//!
    12	//! 1. [`crate::VerterHost::list_file_symbols`] — shallow read; no
    13	//!    audit.
    14	//! 2. [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_named_symbol`] /
    15	//!    [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_named_symbol_with_audit`] —
    16	//!    audited resolution of a named declaration with optional
    17	//!    generic instantiation.
    18	//! 3. [`crate::VerterHost::evaluate_type_expression_with_audit`] —
    19	//!    audited evaluation of a synthetic type expression in a
    20	//!    file scope, with an optional host-owned scratch cache.
    21	//! 4. [`crate::VerterHost::resolve_shallow_surface`] — resolves a
    22	//!    named declaration to its span-rich, one-level
    23	//!    [`surface::TypeInfoSurface`] (members + call / construct / index
    24	//!    signatures + the keyspace) WITHOUT expanding member bodies. The
    25	//!    shallow-by-default rule holds: each member `value` is a
    26	//!    reference-style node, never an eagerly expanded object. Every
    27	//!    span on the returned surface is a [`surface::CanonicalSpan`]
    28	//!    (byte offsets + the canonical declaration file), so a consumer
    29	//!    slices the source on demand at the FFI / consumer boundary —
    30	//!    the surface itself holds NO owned type / display strings.
    31	//!
    32	//! Sub-modules:
    33	//! - [`types`] — public DTOs (`SymbolEntry`, `EvaluateTypeExpressionRequest`, …).
    34	//! - [`symbol_inventory`] — `list_file_symbols` impl.
    35	//! - [`resolve_named_symbol`] — `resolve_named_symbol_with_audit` impl.
    36	//! - [`evaluate_type_expression`] — `evaluate_type_expression_with_audit` impl.
    37	//! - [`shallow_surface`] — `resolve_shallow_surface` impl.
    38	//! - [`surface`] — the span-rich [`surface::TypeInfoSurface`] projection.
    39	//! - [`scratch_cache`] — host-owned LRU for typeinfo scratch URIs.

    71	/// A typeinfo query-returner builds a request-bound dispatch context from
    72	/// the base store view and RETURNS the resolved node — there is no outer
    73	/// `run_stable_request` publish fence to suppress a stale answer. So it MUST
    74	/// resolve against a CURRENT snapshot: a `ReturnOnly` read means the manager
    75	/// could not prove the snapshot coherent, and computing the query against it
    76	/// would return a result derived from already-superseded dependency state.
    77	/// The retry budget mirrors the store-view manager's own bounded
    78	/// no-torn-snapshot retries — a transient mutation burst settles within a
    79	/// few rounds; sustained churn exhausts the budget and the query-returner
    80	/// surfaces a miss (`None`) rather than a stale answer.
    81	pub(crate) const TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS: usize = 3;
    82	
    83	/// Acquire a proven-[`crate::resolver_store::CurrentHostStoreView`] for a
    84	/// typeinfo query-returner, retrying a bounded number of times when the
    85	/// store-view manager hands back a known-stale
    86	/// [`crate::resolver_store::StoreViewRead::ReturnOnly`] read under churn.
    87	///
    88	/// Returns `None` when every attempt within
    89	/// [`TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`] observed a non-current read —
    90	/// the host is under sustained churn and the query CANNOT be answered
    91	/// against a coherent snapshot. `None` is the established typeinfo miss
    92	/// signal ("could not be resolved"): the FFI surface already maps it to a
    93	/// `null` payload, so the consumer re-queries on the next request once the
    94	/// host settles. The loop is bounded, so it always terminates — it never
    95	/// spins.
    96	#[must_use]
    97	pub(crate) fn current_store_view_for_query(
    98	    host: &crate::VerterHost,
    99	) -> Option<crate::resolver_store::CurrentHostStoreView> {
   100	    for _ in 0..TYPEINFO_CURRENT_VIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS {
   101	        if let Some(current) = host.resolver_store_view_read().current() {
   102	            return Some(current);
   103	        }
   104	        // Non-current read: the manager could not prove this snapshot
   105	        // coherent. Re-read — a transient mutation burst settles within
   106	        // the bounded budget. No sleep / yield: the manager's own
   107	        // build_coherent retry already absorbs the contention window, and
   108	        // a tight bounded re-read keeps the path non-blocking.
   109	    }

   110	## GAP 3 — Full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` proof
   111	
   112	The charter’s exhaustive-`impl` mechanism is invalid.
   113	
   114	- Adding a required method makes an existing impl incomplete, but adding a defaulted method does not. The repo demonstrates this directly: `ResolverContext::is_request_bound` has a default at `resolver_context.rs:179-181`, while the large `impl ResolverContext for VerterHost` beginning at `:817` omits it and compiles.
   115	- Even a required method proves only that the double supplies a body. A new method returning bare `T` can be added, implemented with bare `T`, and the exhaustive impl compiles. The impl does not constrain the trait author’s return type.
   116	- Generic methods, associated output types, and `async fn` do not improve this. They may make the trait non-dyn-compatible—the current code separately pins that at `resolver_context.rs:805-815`—but they do not force `AttemptOutcome`. An associated type can resolve to any type.
   117	- A Rust type alias to `AttemptOutcome<T>` is type-identical and therefore valid. It only defeats textual/name-based checking, not Rust type equality.
   118	- A foreign exhaustive double is forbidden by GAP 1’s seal. Only an in-module semantic test type can implement it, and it still suffers the default/return-shape defects above.
   119	- “Sole entry surface” is currently false: ProjectResolver uses `WorkspaceRead` directly (`resolver.rs:321-365`), component-meta reaches the host/scheduler (`component_meta/mod.rs:251-288`), and dispatch lowering calls host materialization (`lower.rs:403-418`).
   120	
   121	Replace the operation trait with one closed, non-overridable inherent gateway:
   122	
   123	```rust
   124	pub enum NonFlowOperation { /* every C2-reachable operation */ }
   125	pub enum NonFlowValue { /* heterogeneous results */ }
   126	
   127	impl TypeInfoCore {
   128	    pub fn attempt(
   129	        &self,
   130	        observations: &ObservationSnapshot,
   131	        operation: NonFlowOperation,
   132	    ) -> AttemptOutcome<NonFlowValue>;
   133	}
   134	```
   135	
   136	Keep the implementation modules and fields private. Match `NonFlowOperation` exhaustively with no wildcard. Adding a variant then forces the dispatcher to change, while every cross-crate operation necessarily returns the one inherent method’s `AttemptOutcome`. Compile-fail fixtures prove foreign code cannot implement a query/observation trait or access an alternate kernel operation. This is a mechanically valid proof of the closed cross-crate entry surface and its return shape.
   137	
   138	It is not—and stable Rust cannot make it—a complete proof that every internal helper is I/O-free. `verter_semantic` can still compile `std::fs`, `std::net`, a blocking primitive, a global/TLS read, or an I/O-capable callback without naming `VerterHost` or scheduler. Cargo’s crate firewall cannot observe those effects. A dedicated `#![no_std]` capability crate could strengthen that proof, but the binding ruling requires the existing `verter_semantic` crate.
   139	
   140	The honest mechanically checkable criterion is therefore:
   141	
   142	- Every external C2 operation is a `NonFlowOperation` and enters through `TypeInfoCore::attempt`.
   143	- All kernel internals are private to that module tree.
   144	- The semantic Cargo closure contains only layers 1–3.
   145	- Compile-fail tests pin sealing and private-entry unreachability.
   146	- Exhaustive all-missing-observation tests cover every enum variant and require `NeedInputs` or `Terminal`, never blocking.
   147	- Internal absence of direct I/O/blocking remains an audited/linted source invariant, not a type-system proof.
   148	
   149	Accepted ADR: unchanged by all three gap resolutions.
   150	
   151	Program DAG edge: unchanged; the planned dependency inversion remains higher layers → `verter_semantic`.
   152	
   153	Program outcome: unchanged; full non-flow extraction and full behavioral `AttemptOutcome` coverage remain required.
